findings.label: The "no briefing / no plan / no Losee coverage" nulls are scoped to BAGLEY, not to the detail — and he expressly disclaimed knowledge about everyone else. One library file's summary layer drops that scope.
findings.what_the_record_says: Every one of the defence's negative questions is addressed to what HE attended, was given, or was assigned, and he twice qualifies with "that morning." Asked "did you attend any type of debrief or briefing or meeting to prepare for the security of this event?" — "I did not because that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags" (02:43:36). Asked again whether he "never attended any kind of… debrief or meeting" — "No, not that morning" (02:44:16). Then the dispositive exchange: "Do you know if there was such a meeting?" — "I don't know because when I got there, it was starting to… People were throwing stuff down on the tent" (02:44:18). On written materials: "Did you RECEIVE any type of briefing materials, written materials prior to the event…?" — "No, not that morning" (02:48:12). After lunch, counsel opens with her own premise — "we talked about that you had had no briefing or no materials about security on campus for this particular event" — and the question she actually puts is "Did you ever have any operational or tactical plan THAT YOU WERE GIVEN for that event?" — "For this event, no" (04:05:26). On the Losee: "Were you ever assigned that area before the shooting?" — "No." "Do you know who was?" — "I don't" (02:45:53–02:45:55). Note that last question PRESUPPOSES someone was assigned; the answer is non-knowledge, not a null.
findings.locator: files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/prelim-hearing-transcripts/day1.txt — 02:43:36, 02:44:16, 02:44:18, 02:45:43–02:45:55, 02:48:12, 04:05:26 (Rev stream offsets, ±5 min as clock times; answers labelled "Richard Novak," speaker inferred from content — the witness gives his own name as Christopher Bagley at 44:50 and is addressed as "Officer Bagley" by the court and both counsel throughout). Library file tested: files - Court record/CR-E05_prelim-hearing-Day1_Bagley-Hull-first-tranche.md §3.5, §7, and the findings roll-up.
findings.limits: CR-E05's RECORDING layer (§3.5) is already correct and carries the scope expressly — "he does not know whether any security meeting occurred" — so this is not a claim that the file misread the transcript. The defect is internal: §7's consolidated line "the security posture before the shot (no briefing, no plan, six officers, no magnetometers, no Losee coverage)" and the findings roll-up's "nobody assigned to the Losee building" both strip the scope and read as facts about the arrangement rather than about one witness. "No Losee coverage" is the sharper error: it converts "I don't [know who was]" into a null. Steelman for the flattened reading: an officer with 26 years' service, on an overtime shift he signed up for in advance, who received no materials and attended nothing, is meaningful circumstantial evidence about the detail as a whole — and no contrary evidence appears anywhere in Day 1. That is a fair inference; it is not a Tier 1 finding, and the two layers must not be merged. What would change it: any UVU PD operations order, event-security plan, or briefing record for 2025-09-10, or testimony from Chief Long or another of the six. NOT established: that no briefing occurred; that no plan existed; that nobody was assigned to the Losee. Also NOT established, and not asserted: any failure or fault by any person. By contrast, files - Kirk assassination questions/kirk-shooting-official-timeline.md scopes it correctly — "Bagley testified he ATTENDED no pre-event security planning meeting."

findings.label: Asked whether he COMMUNICATED with Mr. Kirk's security team, the officer answered with a SIGHTING. The record establishes co-location on the Hall of Flags, not coordination.
findings.what_the_record_says: "Were you aware of whether Mr. Kirk had his own security team present there with him?" — "Yes" (02:46:51). "Did you communicate with any of those people?" — "I saw one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me, yes" (02:46:55). "And that was before the shooting?" — "Yes. And then I saw several down in the crowds and down by him, yes" (02:47:00). "And were you aware of whether that person was armed either?" — "I was aware he was armed" (02:47:07). The verb in the question is "communicate"; the verb in the answer is "saw," twice, and then a third time. No content, time, subject or direction of any communication is given anywhere in the testimony. What IS established at T1: a member of Mr. Kirk's security team was posted on top of the Hall of Flags immediately beside the police overwatch post before the shot; further members were in the crowd and near Mr. Kirk; and the officer understood the individual beside him to be armed.
findings.locator: day1.txt — 02:46:45 through 02:47:08 (a single 23-second exchange on cross by Ms. Nestor). Compare 01:02:41 for the police post at the same location.
findings.limits: REPORTED BY ROLE ONLY, and the transcript does not name him — see the measured null below. Nothing here implies any failure, omission or fault by any member of Mr. Kirk's security team, and no such implication may be drawn: none of these people is accused of anything by anyone. Steelman for the ordinary reading: two armed professionals standing beside each other on a walkway for over an hour almost certainly spoke, and the witness's "yes" may simply be an affirmative to the question as asked, with "I saw" supplying the detail rather than correcting the verb. That reading is reasonable and may well be right — it is just not what the record establishes. What would change it: Bagley's body-worn camera, which he testified was active and chest-mounted and which counsel described as "27 minute and 35 second" footage "that STARTS when you're at the Hall of Flags" (04:08:28, 04:12:54) — that artifact covers the exact period and the defence has reviewed it. NOT established: that UVU PD and the private team coordinated, deconflicted sectors, shared a channel, or exchanged any information at all. Bears directly on the State's grave-risk theory (which places team members close to Mr. Kirk) and on the defence's answer that the shooter's observation of security personnel "an unknown distance" away is speculation.

findings.label: The affirmative Tier 1 law-enforcement posture, in the officer's own words — what the arrangement DID include, logged as squarely as what it did not.
findings.what_the_record_says: Agency and status: UVU Police Department, senior officer, five years there, 26 years a police officer, POST-certified (~600 hours), prior K-9/SWAT/motors/FTO/detective assignments with Utah County Sheriff, Springville City PD and Salt Lake County Sheriff (44:50–47:21; he has since moved to Spanish Fork PD). Shift: he knew of the event in advance and "signed up for an overtime shift… For the special event" (02:43:21), checking in "about 11 o'clock in the morning" (01:02:29) — staffing augmented above normal duty. Strength: "Employ, there was 15" UVU officers; "There was six of us that were… assigned to cover it" (02:44:31–02:44:36), i.e. 40% of the department. Anticipation: "Did you all have an idea there were going to be thousands and thousands of people there or was that a surprise to you?" — "Had an idea" (02:44:49); his own estimate from the overwatch was "several thousand people" (01:37:58). Arming: "of those six officers, are you all armed?" — "Yes"; "Glock pistols" (02:45:06). Post: "to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end… we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area" (01:02:41) — an ELEVATED position directly overlooking the tent, behind a pre-placed physical barrier he identified as "some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk" (01:03:13). Command present: "my chief, Chief Long, that was right next to me" on the courtyard grass moments after the shot (01:40:24). Communications, which functioned and functioned fast: he was "informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody" within "[w]ithin 30 seconds maybe" (01:39:26, 02:54:56); he "asked dispatch to get on the camera system" and dispatch came back with an answer (02:34:17); he "advised other officers that I needed the Losee building secured, searched" (02:37:09). Surveillance: campus CCTV accessible from station desktops and a dispatch camera wall, used "[e]very day," and he had personally built navigation maps for dispatch (47:44–48:28); he reviewed the footage himself at the campus PD on level three of the Gunther Trade Building (02:37:11–02:37:46). Recording: body camera active on his chest throughout (04:08:28). NOT included: no magnetometers (02:45:30); no UVU drone capability at all (02:54:15).
findings.locator: day1.txt — direct examination 44:50–02:42:15; the posture-specific answers cluster at 01:02:29–01:03:13, 01:37:58, 01:39:26, 02:34:17, 02:37:09, and on cross at 02:43:21–02:45:39, 02:54:56.
findings.limits: This is Tier 1 as to what a named sworn police witness said under oath in a public role — Officer Christopher Bagley, a public official, properly named. It is NOT a finding that the arrangement was adequate, nor that it was inadequate; this project has verified no independent fact about UVU PD's staffing decisions, and adequacy is a normative question the record does not answer. Every figure is one witness's recollection ten months after the event, given without notes on most points (he consulted "my notes" only for the 1:01/1:03 roof-release time, 02:32:47). The "six" figure is not clean — see the next finding. What would change it: UVU PD's own event documentation, the CAD/radio log, or testimony from any of the other five officers or from Chief Long. Logged deliberately as a both-directions confirmation, because a file about security at an assassination is the natural home of insinuation and the affirmative record must carry its full weight.

findings.label: The much-repeated "six officers" figure is the witness's own and is affirmed twice — but whether Chief Long is inside or outside the six is unresolved, and "patrol one" contradicts his own "the two officers that were on duty."
findings.what_the_record_says: "That were assigned to cover it? There was six of us that were, there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief" (02:44:36). Counsel then misstates it — "And you only had five officers?" — "Six, yes" (02:44:51) — and corrects herself: "Six. I'm sorry. I'm counting you" — "Yes" (02:44:53), so the six is inclusive of Bagley. But the phrase "five others that were there WITH the chief" reads most naturally as placing Chief Long alongside the five rather than among them, and the chief is independently established as physically present on the courtyard grass beside Bagley at the moment of the shot (01:40:24). Separately, his earlier account of the same morning says the chief "sent THE TWO OFFICERS THAT WERE ON DUTY down to secure the area" (02:43:36) — two on duty, against "patrol one" in the composition answer. Both statements are his.
findings.locator: day1.txt — 02:43:36 (two on-duty officers), 02:44:31–02:44:56 (fifteen employed, six assigned, composition), 01:40:24 (chief on scene). Library figure tested: files - Kirk assassination questions/kirk-shooting-official-timeline.md, "Six officers were working an event with roughly 3,000 attendees" (T3, NewsNation/CNN).
findings.limits: High confidence that these are the words spoken; Medium on the composition, which the testimony does not resolve and which I am flagging rather than resolving. CONFIRMATION LOGGED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the T3 "six officers" figure carried in the library's timeline file is independently corroborated at T1 by the officer's own twice-affirmed answer — the journalism was right. But "six" may undercount UVU sworn personnel on scene: if Chief Long is outside the six, at least seven were present. Steelman for the clean reading: "patrol one" is plausibly a unit call-sign rather than a headcount, and a chief is not ordinarily counted in an assignment roster, so "six assigned officers plus the chief" may be exactly what he meant and internally consistent. NOT established: the true headcount, the sector assignments of the other five, or whether the chief's presence was planned. Also NOT established by this witness: total attendance — "several thousand" is his own eyeball estimate from the overwatch (01:37:58); the "roughly 3,000" figure in the library is T3 and does not come from him, and the timeline file cites it correctly as such. What would change it: the UVU PD roster or overtime sign-up sheet for 2025-09-10.

findings.label: Bagley's testimony CANNOT establish that no other agency covered the event — he answered "I don't know," and counsel's question itself merged a private security team with law-enforcement agencies.
findings.what_the_record_says: "Was there any other LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY besides Mr. Kirk's PRIVATE SECURITY TEAM and your six officers, including you, that were covering that event that day? In other words, did you have any Provo police or Orem police or anyone that you knew of or federal agencies?" — "I don't know" (02:47:08–02:47:28). Follow-up: "You never saw any that day?" — "No, not until the response came in" (02:47:31). Two things are wrong with the premise and the witness adopts neither: the question treats Mr. Kirk's private security team as though it were a law-enforcement agency, which it is not; and it asks a single officer standing on one elevated walkway to speak for the whole campus. His answer is a clean non-knowledge answer, and his second answer is scoped to what he personally SAW from that post.
findings.limits: NOT established: that only UVU PD and the private team covered the event; that no other agency was present; that responsibility was or was not split. What IS established is only that this witness did not know and did not see. The distinction matters because the record's own answer to any inadequacy inference is precisely that responsibility was split across at least three bodies — the university police, the principal's private team, and (by the same-day T2 press conference attributed to Chief Long) the wider mutual-aid response — and a witness's "I don't know" cannot be recruited to collapse that. Steelman for the defence's use of it: an officer with 26 years' experience who saw no outside agency all morning is genuine evidence that no visible outside presence existed at his post, and that is a fair argument to make. What would change it: the mutual-aid request log, any inter-agency operations plan, or testimony from Chief Long, Utah County Sheriff, Orem PD or any federal agency. NOTE ON CATEGORY DISCIPLINE: Agent David Hull's day2 reference to "an officer who was doing security detail" — Officer Goforth, Spanish Fork PD — is a SWORN POLICE OFFICER, not a member of Mr. Kirk's private team; I have not merged the two anywhere, and this finding is the reason the boundary needs stating.

findings.label: MEASURED NULL, positive-controlled: no member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named anywhere in Bagley's testimony, and neither is the event organiser.
findings.what_the_record_says: I enumerated every proper name appearing in the BODY of Bagley's testimony (lines 620–6292 of day1.txt), after stripping Rev's speaker-label constructions, under BOTH U+FFFE readings — join and hyphen — which returned identical results (262 distinct capitalised tokens each). The complete roster of PERSONAL names is: Christopher Bagley (the witness), Chief Long (UVU police chief), Melissa Richards (state forensic examiner), Sergeant Cam Nelson and Sergeant Ken Nielsen (Provo PD, drone operator, rendered two ways), Charlie Kirk, Robinson, and counsel/court (Grunander, Nestor/Nester, Graf). No name attaches to any private security member. Three independent capable patterns were run: (a) naming constructions — "his/the name is/was", "named [Name]", "identified him/as [Name]" — ZERO hits; (b) honorific-plus-surname — "Mr./Ms./Agent/Sergeant/Chief/Officer/Deputy [Surname]" — 96 unique hits, all of them counsel, court, police, Mr. Kirk, or Mr. Robinson, none a security member; (c) "Turning Point|TPUSA" — ZERO hits, so the organisation is never named either. The individual on the Hall of Flags is referred to only as "one of the individuals," and the team only as "his own security team" / "Mr. Kirk's private security team" (4 hits on securit\w*, all opened and read).
findings.locator: day1.txt lines 620–6292 (the whole of Bagley's testimony, direct 44:42–02:42:15, cross 02:42:56–04:20:05, redirect 04:20:18–04:22:09). Search performed with ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/artifact_search.py find(), which tests both U+FFFE readings; load() raised no NUL error, so the 2026-08-16 repair holds for this file.
findings.limits: THE NULL IS CAPABILITY-TESTED: pattern (b) demonstrably finds names in this exact text — 96 hits including one-off surnames such as Richards, Nelson and Nielsen that appear once each — so a name, had one been spoken, would have been matched. SCOPE: this is a claim about the Rev rendering of day1.txt within Bagley's testimony only. It is NOT a claim about the certified transcript, about Hull's or any later witness's testimony, about days 2–5, or about the world. CORPUS-CONTAMINATION NOTE: every search here was confined to a slice of day1.txt, so the mis-banked unrelated-case file (…2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286-1-4-1_dc28417731.txt) was never in scope and no per-term exclusion was needed or applied — I am stating this rather than claiming an exclusion I did not perform. WHY IT MATTERS: it means this library can state the full security posture at Tier 1 without ever approaching the identification harm the State's own sworn proffer of 2026-02-02 (dkt 368 ¶¶5–6) describes as ongoing, and it forecloses any later claim that "the transcript names him." What would change it: reading the certified transcript, or any later witness naming a team member — in which case the project rule still applies and the name still does not get compiled.

findings.dropped: Losee roof access at T1: the outdoor stairway is "open to the public," the guardrail "probably about a couple feet high that somebody could jump over," and the area is "restricted"/"off limits" only by that "natural barrier" and the absence of a paved path (01:12:45–01:13:38) — no lock, no forced entry needed. || Open-carry, the record's own answer to any inadequacy inference: asked whether a Utah campus is a gun-free zone, "It's an open carry state, so yes" (02:46:25) — already banked by the coordinator, re-verified here. || The Hall of Flags posting was REACTIVE and this CONFIRMS CR-E05 v1.1's correction: Chief Long received "a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent" and "sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area"; Bagley dressed and joined them (02:43:36) — simultaneously his stated reason for no briefing AND evidence of live command function that morning. || Pre-placed physical control: what he first called "what looks like yellow crime scene tape" in Exhibit 1 he identified as "some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk" (01:03:13) — a pre-shooting barrier on the elevated walkway, though Exhibit 1's date and authorship were never established, so the identification rests on him alone. || Communications functioned and functioned fast: "shooter in custody" over the radio within "[w]ithin 30 seconds maybe" (01:39:26, 02:54:56); he tasked dispatch to pull campus CCTV and got an answer (02:34:17); he tasked responding officers to secure and search the Losee (02:37:09). || Campus CCTV capability: station-desktop access plus a dispatch camera wall, used "[e]very day," and he had personally built click-through navigation maps for dispatch (47:44–48:28); he reviewed the footage himself at UVU PD, level three of the Gunther Trade Building (02:37:11–02:37:46). || Body camera: active, chest-mounted, running from the Hall of Flags; 27 min 35 s; battery died on the roof BEFORE the tape went up; the only body-cam he has for the day and he never re-docked it (04:08:28, 04:12:23–04:12:54). || Equipment absent: no magnetometers anywhere on campus (02:45:30); UVU had no drone capability at all — "Did you have a drone on campus that you used?" "No" (02:54:15) — drones arrived post-incident from Provo PD; and he had no crime-scene tape on his person, responding officers "threw it up to me" (04:10:58). || Unresolved name discrepancy INSIDE one witness's testimony: the Provo PD drone sergeant is "Sergeant Cam Nelson" at 02:54:06 and "Sergeant Ken Nielsen" at 04:18:21 — same agency, same subject, two renderings; may be Rev mis-transcription or witness memory, not resolved here. || Armed-awareness tension, reconcilable and logged without insinuation: "did you see anybody that was armed that day other than law enforcement?" — "I did not see" (02:46:35), then 32 seconds later, of the security-team member beside him, "I was aware he was armed" (02:47:07); awareness is not a sighting and concealed carry reconciles both, but no basis for the awareness is stated. Implies nothing about anyone's conduct. || CATEGORY BOUNDARY, flagged so it is not merged: an unidentified man in civilian clothes with a handgun backed him up to the Losee roof — "He had a badge on" and "I don't know who he was exactly" (04:08:44–04:08:56). Badged, therefore on Bagley's own account not private security; agency unknown to him. || The empty concealed pistol holster on the courtyard grass (02:52:45–02:53:45): the witness attributes it to NO ONE, never collected it, never told anyone to, does not know if it was fingerprinted, and left it in place. It is recorded here strictly as an unattributed item. Any connection drawn to a member of Mr. Kirk's security team would be pure insinuation on this record and is REFUSED AND FLAGGED as such — the transcript supplies no owner and none may be supplied. || Crowd size: "several thousand people" is Bagley's own T1 eyeball estimate from the overwatch (01:37:58); "3,000" appears nowhere in his testimony, and the library's "roughly 3,000" is T3, correctly cited as such in the timeline file. || His stated clock times, distinct from Rev stream offsets: check-in ~11:00 a.m.; shot 12:23; Losee roof 12:44; roof released ~1:01–1:03; off campus ~9 p.m.; returned next morning, worked "[o]n and off." || Scene turnovers, both to post-incident responders and not to the event detail: the Losee roof to "a county deputy, a female" with instructions to admit no one but police or investigators (02:33:05); the northeast drop-off scene to "two Payson police officers" in uniform, same instruction (02:40:42). || The word "detail" never appears in Bagley's testimony in the security sense — 2 hits, both unrelated ("in detail describing," "in as best detail as you can"); he says only "his own security team" and adopts counsel's "Mr. Kirk's private security team." || Losee coverage, the exact defect: "Do you know who was?" is a PRESUPPOSING question — it assumes someone was assigned — and "I don't" is a non-knowledge answer to it, which is why CR-E05's "no Losee coverage" over-reads. || He never characterises the arrangement as adequate or inadequate; the inadequacy framing throughout is counsel's, built by leading questions, and he assents only to the narrow facts put to him.

findings.label: Hull's testimony contains no account of the pre-shot security posture at all — a measured null over 755 of his own answers, with capable patterns and positive controls
findings.what_the_record_says: I parsed both transcripts into speaker segments and isolated the 755 segments actually labelled to the witness (day1 n=379 'David Hull', L6296–L10916; day2 n=376 'Agent Hull', L392–L3906). Across all 755, the stems securit/guard/detail appear in FIVE answers, and only TWO concern Mr. Kirk's private team — both post-shot: 'Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene' and 'one of the team's vehicles'. The other three are sworn police: 'an officer who was doing security detail' (Goforth), 'There was an officer standing security' (Losee roof, that night), and Mr. Olsen's UVU video 'team'. ZERO hits for guard/bodyguard/escort/flank/protective detail/counter-sniper/advance team/threat assessment/magnetometer/metal detector/bag check/roof access, in either the join or hyphen reading of U+FFFE. Hull never named any member of the private team. Cross established why: 'Does the SBI on occasion assist other agencies with preparing for big events like this…?' — 'Not something that I've ever been involved with, no' (day2 01:40:54), and he arrived on campus 'shortly after 1:30', which Nestor put as 'approximately an hour after Mr. Kirk had already been removed' — 'Approximately, yes' (day2 01:41:03–01:41:13).

findings.limits: This does NOT establish that the security arrangement was inadequate, adequate, or anything at all — it establishes that THIS witness is not a source on it, in either direction, and that a file built on Hull cannot answer the question. The patterns are demonstrably capable of matching the thing claimed absent: the same battery returned 'security detail' (Goforth), 'officer standing security', 'sniper pad'/'sniper position' (7 hits, Bagley), 'magnetometer' (1 hit, Bagley), 'open carry' (1 hit, Bagley) elsewhere in the same files. Steelman: Hull was the lead case agent and could in principle have learned the posture second-hand during the investigation; the State simply never asked and the defence never pressed him on it. Scope: I searched only day1 and day2; days 3–5 and faumuina_condensed.txt were not opened, so this null is bounded to Hull's testimony, not to the hearing.

findings.label: 'A dead-on view of Mr. Kirk and his parts of his security team' is defence counsel's characterization inside an unanswered compound question — Hull never adopted it
findings.what_the_record_says: Ms. Nestor: 'there was a video that was taken by Mr. Ty Phillips from behind the individual that was speaking to Mr. Kirk.' Hull: 'Correct.' Nestor then put a two-clause question: 'And it showed a dead-on view of Mr. Kirk and his parts of his security team. Is that right? And then you also have video that you described that shows the back of the tent at the moment the shot happened. Is that right? Behind Mr. Kirk.' Hull's reply went only to the second clause: 'You're referring to the UVU video in the breezeway?' — 'Yes.' — 'We have that video, yes.' The first clause was never answered, and Hull never elsewhere described Exhibit 7 as showing security personnel; his own foundation for it was only 'Mr. Phillips was positioned towards the front of the crowd, and it does depict the moment that Mr. Kirk is shot' (day1 05:21:52).
findings.locator: day2.txt L2820–L2840, ts 01:57:29–01:58:27; Hull's own Exhibit 7 description at day1.txt L8057, ts 05:21:52
findings.limits: This corrects a recording-layer item into its proper layer: the sentence is faithfully recorded as something COUNSEL said, and it is not a fact Hull testified to. It does not establish that Exhibit 7 fails to show security personnel — only that this witness never said it does. Steelman for the other reading: Hull's 'Correct' two seconds earlier could be read as a running assent to Nestor's whole framing; against that, his very next words redirect to a different exhibit, which is the behaviour of a witness answering the clause he understood. What would change it: the exhibit itself, or a witness who describes its content.

findings.label: The Officer Goforth vehicle contact is post-incident — approximately 12:30 AM on 2025-09-11, roughly twelve hours after the shot — and belongs to the fourth campus visit, not to event security
findings.what_the_record_says: Narrating State's Exhibit 12.4 in sequence, Hull put the shot at '12:23:28', the roof departure and Campus Drive crossing at '12:24:42' on September 10. He then reached a clip of 'the intersection of Campus Drive and 800 South… a vehicle attempting to turn right onto Campus Drive.' Asked why he believed it was Robinson's vehicle: 'When that vehicle was stopped, it actually made contact with an officer who was doing security detail' — 'Officer Goforth' — 'Spanish Fork Police.' Asked the time: 'It was approximately 12:30 AM' — 'On September 11th, 2025.' Hull's account of the contact itself is what Goforth told him: 'cop intuition, but there was something about the interaction that made him make a note of the license plate', and he later 'ran a partial plate' returning two registered owners. This dovetails with the Ring/Nest doorbell footage Hull placed at 'approximately 038 hours on the morning of the 11th' — 12:38 AM — 'a short period after' the law-enforcement interaction.
findings.limits: CATEGORY DISCIPLINE: Officer Goforth is a sworn Spanish Fork Police officer acting in a public role and is properly nameable; he is NOT a member of Mr. Kirk's private security team, and nothing here should be merged with that category. What this does NOT establish: what Goforth's detail was securing. Hull never said. The time (00:30 on 9/11), the place (a campus-perimeter intersection) and Hull's separate testimony that 'the campus was locked down and secured' make a post-incident scene/perimeter posture the natural reading, but that is inference, not testimony. Goforth did not testify on day1 or day2, so his account reaches the record only as Hull's hearsay — Medium-high for the underlying facts, High only for what Hull said. 'When that vehicle was stopped' is ambiguous between a traffic stop and a vehicle halted at an intersection; Hull did not resolve it and neither should the file.

findings.label: The 'hasty transport' is Hull's reconstruction, not observation — and only one element of it is tied to an exhibit; the rest is hedged and unsourced
findings.what_the_record_says: Asked what happened to Mr. Kirk immediately after he was shot: 'My recollection is that Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid and they conducted what would be called a hasty transport to Timpanogos Hospital.' Asked whether that is portrayed in Exhibit 9: 'It's kind of on the left side, the back of the pop-up tent and then you can see Mr. Kirk being carried down the left side of the video under that breezeway.' Asked what a hasty transport means: 'Just they were trying to get him to medical as quickly as possible. So I believe he was thrown into one of the team's vehicles and then transported to the hospital as opposed to waiting for an ambulance.' Hull separately confirmed he arrived on campus about an hour after Mr. Kirk had been removed. CONFIRMATION LOGGED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, as the objectivity rule requires: this is the record's own affirmative account of the private detail's immediate response — they removed him, administered first aid en route, and did not wait for an ambulance. Hull, a 12-year peace officer with roughly 40 homicide investigations, used a term of art ('hasty transport') rather than a criticism.
findings.limits: ROLE ONLY: no member of this detail is named here or anywhere in Hull's testimony, and none is accused of anything by anyone. Tier discipline: only the CARRYING is tied to a video Hull watched (Exhibit 9, the UVU breezeway camera). 'Whilst administering first aid', 'thrown into one of the team's vehicles', and the hospital destination are prefaced 'My recollection is' / 'I believe' and are not sourced to any exhibit — Hull did not say Exhibit 9 shows a vehicle, and he was not on campus when it happened. Grade the carrying at Medium-high, the first aid and vehicle at Low. What would change it: Exhibit 9 itself, or testimony from someone present. This finding does not support, and must not be read to support, any inference about the detail's conduct before the shot.

findings.label: What Hull's sworn foundation actually establishes about Exhibits 7, 8 and 9 — and what he conspicuously did not say about any of them
findings.what_the_record_says: Exhibit 7 is the cell-phone video of a minor witness (Mr. Phillips; his mother witnessed the 1102, Exhibit 7.1): 'Mr. Phillips was positioned towards the front of the crowd, and it does depict the moment that Mr. Kirk is shot.' Exhibit 8 is the TPUSA videographer's footage (Visual Impulse; 1102 from its owner-operator, Exhibit 8.1): 'a view from the cameras that Visual Impulse had established at the event actually looking out from the stage into the crowd… shows the moment that Mr. Kirk is shot.' Exhibit 9 is UVU surveillance: 'a view kind of looking what would be east under the breezeway towards the back of the stage where Mr. Kirk was situated. It shows some movement behind the stage area and I believe through the gaps you can see some of the crowd' — 'three minutes', no audio, custodian Kurtis Olsen, UVU director of infrastructure (1102 = Exhibit 12.3, taken 2026-06-24). Hull described the banner as the rear of a pop-up gazebo, Mr. Kirk 'approximately dead center' and 'three to five feet' in front of it. In NONE of the three foundations did Hull describe the position, number, or movement of any security personnel.
findings.limits: This does not establish that the exhibits lack such content — only that Hull's foundation testimony does not describe it. The defence's 2026-08-11 briefing characterizes the SAME Exhibit 8 as depicting 'two security personnel in front and diagonal to Mr. Kirk, standing in the grass area by the barrier' and 'One of Mr. Kirk's security guards comes into frame from the right of Mr. Kirk three seconds after the shot.' Those descriptions come from counsel reading the exhibit, not from a sworn witness describing it, and the two must be kept on separate layers and separately graded. Publication posture matters to any future acquisition: Exhibits 7, 8 and 9 were admitted but NOT published in the courtroom and NOT filmed; only their 1102 statements (7.1, 8.1, 12.3) were published. Nothing here identifies any private security individual and nothing should.

findings.label: The two-directional pair on who was behind Mr. Kirk — and the exact, narrow scope of each answer, which bears directly on the State's grave-risk theory
findings.what_the_record_says: CROSS (Ms. Nestor, using Exhibit 9): 'having reviewed that at the time the shot was fired, there was no one standing directly behind the tent. Is that correct?' Hull first refused: 'You'd have to show me it again. I wasn't specifically looking for that.' After re-viewing: 'So there's a videographer on the right side of the tent and then I can only see as far as the video allows me to. So I can't speak to whether there's anybody out of frame who could have been behind the tent.' Pressed to the middle: 'There's no one stood in the middle behind the tent. No.' REDIRECT (Mr. Sturgill, same exhibit, wider window): 'Leading up to the shot, what's going on behind that banner?' — 'There are representatives, I believe, of TP USA… There are law enforcement representatives. I don't know if there's any student body. But essentially, people are moving to and fro behind that area. A couple of individuals are retrieving items from a vehicle, but there's consistent movement behind and in that area.' — 'Directly behind the banner?' — 'Correct.' Hull also established the banner is opaque in both directions: 'You would not be able to see through it from the audience side of the amphitheater'; from the breezeway side, 'You can't' see Mr. Kirk.
findings.limits: The two answers are not in conflict and must not be reported as if they were: cross fixed a single instant ('at the time the shot was fired') at a single spot ('the middle'); redirect covered a period ('leading up to the shot') over a wider area ('behind and in that area'). Hull's own limiter — 'I can only see as far as the video allows me to… I can't speak to whether there's anybody out of frame' — caps both. CATEGORY DISCIPLINE: the people Hull placed behind the banner were TPUSA representatives and law-enforcement representatives, plus a videographer; he did not identify any of them as Mr. Kirk's private security team, and the file must not convert them into it. This bears on, but does not resolve, the State's charged grave-risk aggravator or the defence's answer that the theory rests on speculation about what the shooter observed.

findings.dropped: BAGLEY VERIFICATIONS (done to test the coordinator's item 8, all day1, all Tier 1, all under both U+FFFE readings): (1) 15 UVU officers employed in total, 6 assigned to the event — "there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief" (02:44:31–02:44:51) — this upgrades the "roughly six officers / 3,000 attendees" line in kirk-shooting-official-timeline.md from T3 to T1. (3) But CR-E05's "no briefing, no debrief, no meeting that morning" OVERSTATES a scoped answer: Bagley said "No, not that morning" twice and, asked whether such a meeting existed at all, "I don't know" — a null about his own attendance, not about the event; CR-E05 should be narrowed. (4) Bagley knew of the event in advance and "signed up for an overtime shift… for the special event" — the event was staffed as a planned special-event detail, which cuts against reading the morning as unplanned. "Ryman" returns 0 contexts in day1 and 13 in day2. Confidence Medium-high that day1's media-access argument is Ryman, not Novak. (9) day1 L10804–L10876 assigns "David Hull" to defence counsel's speech ("we're happy to accommodate the state on that", "I made my objection already") — the witness's own label is unreliable at the very end of day1. HULL, POST-INCIDENT RESPONSE (all told-or-reconstructed, not observed): (10) "hundreds if not a thousand officers. High hundreds would've responded"; he parked on University Avenue and walked in "between hundreds of police cars." (20) The 12.1/12.4 dispute: the enhanced UVU compilation (12.1) was REFUSED on day1 for want of a 1102 from whoever made the zooms, circles and blurs; the State produced an unenhanced 12.4 overnight, which was admitted and broadcast on day2, and 12.1 was then admitted but reviewed only on the judge's monitor. findings.label: The Hall of Flags is a pleaded pillar of the State's zone-of-danger theory that the defence's 34-page brief never once mentions — and sworn testimony independently establishes people were gathered there, above the tent, in numbers that required police management
findings.what_the_record_says:
STATE, RECORDING LAYER (Information, read directly): "Directly above and behind Mr. Kirk was the UVU Hall of Flags, an indoor walkway spanning several hundred feet with floor-to-ceiling glass windows which overlook the plaza where Mr. Kirk was seated. People were in the walkway at the time of the shooting."

DEFENCE, MEASURED NULL: "Hall of Flags" = 0 hits and "flags" = 0 hits in BOTH banked extractions of the 2026-08-11 brief, under both U+FFFE readings. Positive controls in the same run on the same files: "walkway" 8 (all four distinct hits are the Losee/computer-science walkway the shooter crossed, never the Hall of Flags), "Bagley" 12, "securit" 8, "breezeway" 2, "window" 8 (all "window of time" or case-law), "glass" 2 (Sosa-Hurtado's glass case). The pattern is demonstrably capable; the null is real.

ANALYST LAYER — sworn corroboration the defence brief does not engage. The UVU officer on direct examination by Mr. Grunander (day1 ~01:02:41) on his assignment: "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end. So we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area." On cross (~02:43:36), explaining why no briefing occurred: "that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags… The Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent. Therefore, he sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area." And at ~01:03:13 a physical barrier: "it looks like yellow crime scene tape. That was some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk."

Agent Hull confirmed the same structure is Exhibit 9's location (day2 ~02:17:51): "The breezeway underneath the Hall of Flags." So the "breezeway" the defence brief does discuss is the underside of the structure whose top it never discusses.

findings.limits: Does NOT establish that anyone on the Hall of Flags was geometrically downrange of the shot, or in any actual danger — that is exactly what nobody testified to and what Hull expressly declined to answer. The distinction between the INDOOR glass walkway the Information describes and the OUTSIDE top walkway the officer was posted on (he testified there are "an inside one and an outside one") is drawn by neither party and is not resolved here. STEELMAN FOR THE DEFENCE: its brief is a legal argument about the KGRD aggravator's Utah construction, and it may have judged the Hall of Flags immaterial because the State's own preliminary-hearing brief (unheld) may not have pressed it; silence in a brief is not concession, and the Information is a 2025 charging document, not the 2026 argument the court will rule on. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: the State's 2026-07-28 brief; any testimony fixing where Hall of Flags occupants stood relative to the bullet's path; the 2026-09-01 argument transcript. Rev offsets are stream positions, ±5 min as clock times, and are NOT converted to times of day. The day1 witness's answers carry the Rev label "Richard Novak" (a defence attorney's name); speaker inferred from CONTENT — he describes his own overtime shift, his own report, his chief, and is addressed on the record as "Officer Bagley" by both counsel.

findings.label: Agent Hull affirmatively placed a person behind the tent and expressly disclaimed knowledge of anyone out of frame — the defence brief's narrow citation is faithful, but its concluding sentence overstates that testimony
findings.what_the_record_says:
WHAT THE BRIEF SAYS. Narrow version (accurate): "Confirmed in testimony from Agent Hull, no one is immediately behind the center of the 'American Comeback' pop-up tent when the shot occurred. PH2:69." Broad version, in the brief's KGRD conclusion (not supported): "there was no one under the tent on the side that Mr. Kirk was struck or behind him in the breezeway."

WHAT HULL ACTUALLY SAID, day2 ~02:00:21–02:01:21, on cross by Ms. Nestor:
— "You'd have to show me it again. I wasn't specifically looking for that."
— "So there's a videographer on the right side of the tent and then I can only see as far as the video allows me to. So I can't speak to whether there's anybody out of frame who could have been behind the tent."
— Q: "is there anyone directly behind the middle of the tent?" A: "Yes. There's a videographer who stood behind the tent." Q: "To the right?" A: "Yes, behind the tent."
— Only then, to the re-narrowed question "directly in the middle of the tent, is there anyone standing?": "There's no one stood in the middle behind the tent. No."

This matters because it is the exact allegation in the State's Information: "…as well as some behind his canopy." On this record at least one person (role: a videographer) was behind the tent, and the case agent could not exclude others out of frame.

ALSO VERIFIED, AND IT CUTS TOWARD THE DEFENCE: the brief's "Agent Hull testified that he 'can't answer' what would have been visible to the shooter on the Losee Center roof. PH2:68" is faithful — at ~01:58:59 Hull answered "I can't answer that question." But note the question he refused was the DEFENCE's proposition ("this area behind the tent would not have been visible to anybody that was on the Losee building. Is that fair?"). The refusal denies both sides the inference.

findings.limits: Does NOT establish that the videographer was in any danger, nor that this person was a member of Mr. Kirk's security team — no witness said so and this file does not infer it; the role stated on the record is videographer. STEELMAN FOR THE DEFENCE, and it is substantial: (a) the videographer was on the RIGHT and Mr. Kirk was struck on the LEFT side of the neck, so the defence's side-specific claim about the struck side is untouched; (b) "behind him in the breezeway" may be shorthand for the same centre-scoped point Hull did confirm; (c) the breezeway (a tunnel under the Hall of Flags) and the immediate rear of the tent may be different locations, and Hull's videographer was described relative to the tent. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: the certified PH2 transcript pages 69–70 (this project holds only the Rev machine transcript and cannot check the brief's page pinpoints); State's Exhibit 9 itself, which is not published.

findings.label: The State's own charging documents never use the word "security" — the State's pleaded proximity theory is about "Mr. Kirk's team members," and "security personnel" enters the State's case only through the defence's paraphrase of a brief this library does not hold
findings.what_the_record_says:
THE STATE'S THEORY AT SOURCE, verbatim from the Information: "Mr. Kirk's team members were very close to him on his right and left, as well as some behind his canopy and others at various close locations near him. The large crowd surrounded Mr. Kirk on three sides. Temporary metal fencing separated attendees from Mr. Kirk by only a matter of feet." And: "The bullet's trajectory passed closely to several other individuals beside Mr. Kirk, including the questioner who was standing directly in front of Mr. Kirk."

MEASURED NULL: "securit" = 0 hits, "guard" = 0, "bodyguard" = 0 in the 10-page Information AND in the 3-page PC affidavit, under both U+FFFE readings. Positive controls in the same run on the same two files: "team" 2 hits in the Information (both the sentence above), "detail" 2 in the affidavit (both "detailed in this statement"). Patterns capable; nulls real.

WHERE "SECURITY PERSONNEL" COMES FROM: all four uses in the defence brief. Two describe exhibits ("what appear to be two security personnel"; "One of Mr. Kirk's security guards"), one is the fence ("a security barrier"), and the fourth is the defence's characterisation of the State's argument — speculation item (a), "That the shooter actually observed security personnel standing an unknown distance from Mr. Kirk." The State's 2026-07-28 preliminary-hearing brief is NOT banked: a sweep of all 63 top-level .txt artifacts for /preliminary hearing brief/ returned hits in exactly two files, both the defence's own brief and its alternate extraction.

SWORN SUPPORT FOR THE STATE'S ACTUAL PLEADING, day1 ~02:47:00, the UVU officer on cross, asked whether he communicated with Mr. Kirk's team: "I saw one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me, yes… And then I saw several down in the crowds and down by him, yes."
findings.locator: ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2025-09-16_information-charging-document_dc27880532.txt (PC narrative) · 2025-09-16_affidavit-of-probable-cause_dc27880530.txt · 2026-08-11_defendant-prelim-hearing-briefing.txt lines 570–574, 786–787 · day1.txt ~02:46:45–02:47:07
findings.limits: "Team members" is broader than "security personnel" and may include TPUSA staff, media, or event crew; nothing here establishes that the persons the Information places on Mr. Kirk's right and left were security. The officer's "several down in the crowds and down by him" was given in answer to a question that had already framed them as Mr. Kirk's security team, so the categorisation is counsel's, adopted by the witness. The null does NOT show the State never argued security proximity — its 2026-07-28 brief is unheld and may well use the word; it shows only that the word is absent from the two State filings this project holds, so no file may write "the State says security personnel were close to Mr. Kirk" and cite the Information. findings.label: Nothing in the held record measures the distance from the shooter to any person other than Mr. Kirk — the only surveyed figures are perch-to-tent, and days 4 and 5 contain no security testimony at all
findings.what_the_record_says:
THE ONLY MEASURED GEOMETRY, day4 ~04:37–04:38, Sgt. Faumuina on direct by Mr. McBride: "the distance from the perch area directly to the tent where Mr. Kirk was sitting was approximately 415 feet"; "without taking into account the elevation drop, it was actually 410 feet. So just horizontal straight across. And then the elevation difference between that is approximately 68 feet." McBride restates: "410 feet from the perch to the tent with a 68-foot vertical drop. Is that right?" — "Yes." Every endpoint is the TENT. No witness was asked, and none volunteered, the distance from the perch to any security position, to the questioner, or to the crowd line.

DAYS 4 AND 5, MEASURED NULL ON SECURITY: "securit" returns 4 hits in day4 and 3 in day5 — three of day4's and all of day5's are Rev.com site chrome ("Help Center Developers Security Contact"), and the one remaining day4 hit is "UVU security footage," i.e. surveillance, not a detail. "detail" returns 11 (day4) and 6 (day5), every one either "go into detail" or forensic "possible ridge detail and/or smudging." "private securit", "his team", "security team", "Kirk…team", "bodyguard", "entourage" all return 0 across days 3, 4 and 5. Patterns capable ("tent" returns 64 on day4, 24 on day5); nulls real.

ACROSS THE WHOLE FIVE-DAY EVIDENTIARY RECORD there are exactly three substantive references to Mr. Kirk's security team: the day1 cross of the UVU officer (~02:46:45–02:47:31), Hull on direct at day1 ~05:58:03 ("Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid… a hasty transport"), and defence counsel's own compound question at day2 ~01:58:06 ("a dead-on view of Mr. Kirk and his parts of his security team") — which the witness never adopted; he answered only the second half of the question.

findings.limits: This is a null about what was ASKED as much as what exists — the State bore no burden to survey bystander positions at a preliminary hearing, and Exhibits 7, 8, 9, 12.1 and 12.4 may show the geometry the transcript does not state. It therefore does NOT establish that security personnel were far from Mr. Kirk; it establishes that on this record the distance is unquantified, which is precisely what the defence's phrase "an unknown distance from Mr. Kirk" asserts — a confirmation running in the defence's favour, logged as such. It equally does not establish they were far: the Information pleads "very close… on his right and left," and the day1 officer's "several down in the crowds and down by him" is consistent with close. findings.label: The parties' sharpest exhibit dispute — the State's "at least two individuals … under the tent," which the defence calls reckless — is a dispute over the NUMBER, not over presence: the defence's own reading of the same exhibits places a person under the tent beside Mr. Kirk
findings.what_the_record_says:
RECORDING LAYER, BOTH SIDES. The defence brief, footnote 8: "The State claims in its brief that '[a]t least two individuals were standing under the tent where Mr. Kirk was seated[.]' StBr:16. This claim is contrary to the evidence and is indicative of the State's reckless recitation of the evidence in its brief. See, e.g., StEx 7; StEx 8 at 00:40."

But the same brief's own frame-by-frame reading of the exhibits says, of StEx 7: "There is one individual seen to Mr. Kirk's right and behind Mr. Kirk under the tent… This individual is on the opposite side of where the bullet struck Mr. Kirk." And of StEx 8 at 00:32: "There are what appear to be two security personnel in front and diagonal to Mr. Kirk, standing in the grass area by the barrier seen in Exhibit 7," with the shot at 00:48 and "One of Mr. Kirk's security guards comes into frame from the right of Mr. Kirk three seconds after the shot."

So on the defence's own account of the exhibits: one person under the tent (right, behind, opposite side from the wound); two more in the grass in front and diagonal, by the barrier; and one entering frame from the right three seconds post-shot. The contested proposition is whether the count under the tent is one or two — not whether anyone was beside Mr. Kirk.
findings.locator: ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2026-08-11_defendant-prelim-hearing-briefing.txt lines 548–574 and footnote 8 at lines 588–592
findings.limits: ⚠️ T1 FOR WHAT WAS FILED ONLY — neither party's characterisation of any exhibit is evidence of what the exhibit shows, and this project has viewed none of Exhibits 6, 7, 8, 9, 12.1 or 12.4. The State's words are known ONLY through the defence's quotation of a brief this library does not hold; the quoted fragment "[a]t least two individuals were standing under the tent" must never be promoted to a State filing. STEELMAN FOR THE DEFENCE: its point is legal, not arithmetic — under Sosa-Hurtado II mere presence is insufficient, so conceding one person under the tent costs it nothing, and the "opposite side" observation is the substantive answer to the trajectory allegation. STEELMAN FOR THE STATE: its Information pleads "on his right and left," and a person to Mr. Kirk's right under the tent is squarely within that. NOTHING HERE IMPLIES ANY CRITICISM OF ANY INDIVIDUAL'S CONDUCT; positions are recorded, no person is named, and no member of Mr. Kirk's team is identified. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: the State's 2026-07-28 brief, or publication of Exhibits 7 and 8.

findings.label: An empty concealed pistol holster was found in the crowd area, left in place and never taken into custody, and a trooper's report recorded a firearm found in a holster there — the case agent did not recall it; ownership is unestablished
findings.what_the_record_says:
DAY 1, the UVU officer on cross (~02:52:45–02:53:45): "as I was clearing people out and making sure that the evidence was preserved, about towards the top, after a little bit, I saw an empty holster sitting there" — on the south side of the courtyard, on the tiered grass "towards the top, maybe just right before the cement is where everybody's standing." Described as "An empty concealed holster," "For a pistol." Then: "And what happened to that holster?" — "I have no idea." "Did you ever take custody of it?" — "Nope." "Did you ever tell anyone else to take custody of it?" — "Nope." "You just left it on the grass?" — "I did." "Was it ever fingerprinted to your knowledge?" — "I have no idea." At ~04:05:52, asked whether any other guns were confiscated on scene that day: "I am not [aware]… I don't know."

DAY 2, Agent Hull on cross (~01:46:25–01:49:01): asked about "an individual named Noah Gonzalez" — "I don't recall that name specifically"; then "I know that a trooper was interviewed, having been on scene. I don't recall if it was Gonzalez." Asked whether he recalled the trooper saying a gun was actually found in that holster — "I do not." Shown the report: "Trooper Gonzalez included in his report that there was a gun, yes." Counsel established the trooper was "an off-duty trooper who happened to be there that day" — "Correct."

This bears directly on the KGRD zone-of-danger population and on the same officer's answer, minutes earlier, that Utah "is an open carry state" and that he did not see anybody armed "other than law enforcement."
findings.locator: ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/prelim-hearing-transcripts/day1.txt ~02:52:04–02:53:45 and ~04:05:45–04:06:35 · day2.txt ~01:46:25–01:49:01
findings.limits: 🚨 OWNERSHIP IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT INSINUATED. The holster is not attributed to any member of Mr. Kirk's security team, to the off-duty trooper, or to any identified person — nobody testified whose it was, and nothing in the held record supports any attribution. No individual member of Mr. Kirk's security team is named, described or implicated anywhere in this finding, and none of them is accused of anything by anyone. The trooper's report content reaches this record as hearsay inside a memory-refreshing question; Hull confirmed only what the report states, and did not adopt it. Trooper Gonzalez is categorised as a public official (a sworn state trooper, named by counsel in open court in the context of an official report) — but the categorisation is qualified: he was OFF DUTY and did not testify at this hearing. STEELMAN AGAINST OVER-READING: an unattended holster in a stampeding crowd during an active shooting has many innocent explanations; the officer's own account is that his priority was clearing people out, and a preliminary hearing is not the forum where chain-of-custody for a non-charged item gets resolved. Confidence is Medium-high rather than High because the underlying Davis report and the trooper's interview are not held by this library. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: the Davis report (Exhibit 13), the trooper's interview, or any evidence log for the courtyard scene.

Cam Nelson of Provo PD, and UVU had no drone capability at all (day1 ~02:54:01–02:54:24) — a concrete, non-insinuating datum on the event's security posture that neither brief uses.

The responsibility split is on the record and must be given its weight: the defence's own question frames it as "Mr. Kirk's private security team and your six officers," and Bagley answered "I don't know" whether any other agency covered the event, seeing none "until the response came in"; he then handed the roof scene to a woman deputy sheriff and the drop-off scene to Payson Police.
Hull's day1 ~05:58:03 testimony that "Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid and they conducted what would be called a hasty transport to Timpanogos Hospital," portrayed in State's Exhibit 9 — the single instance in five days of testimony describing what the team actually did, and it is a description of them rendering aid.
Officer Goforth of Spanish Fork PD, struck by a vehicle "who was doing security detail" (day2 ~00:57:54), is a sworn officer on a public detail and is kept strictly outside the private-team category, as is the "officer standing security" at the roof crime scene that evening (day2 ~01:49:37).
The opacity of the tent's rear banner — "You would not be able to see through it… You cannot" — was elicited on the STATE's redirect (day2 ~02:18:32–02:19:16), not extracted by the defence, so it is common ground rather than a contested finding.
Hull's prone-duration estimate was expressly hedged twice ("It was my guess, my guess, I would estimate, between 15 and 30 seconds… but the video would verify that", day2 ~01:56:55–01:57:20), and he corrected counsel that the crawl into position took longer than the prone interval — the defence brief's "35-44 seconds" derives from the video timestamps, not from Hull.

A titling divergence, recorded not registered: the defence brief calls the forensic witness "Agent Jennifer Faumuina" while the day4 transcript addresses her as "Sergeant Faumuina" throughout.

Structural note for the register: the State's 2026-07-28 brief remains unheld (Q-45 / CR-E07's F-15, only partly cured by CR-E08), and this lens found five distinct "StBr:" pinpoints (2-3, 9-10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 16-17) whose contents exist in this library solely as the defence's quotation of its opponent.

findings.label: The "we didn't" line: UVU Police Chief Jeff Long, ~2–3 hours after the killing, conceding nothing specific
findings.what_the_record_says: Speaker identified from CONTENT, not label: the man self-identifies — "So my name is Jeff Long. I'm the police chief here at UVU." Gov. Cox hands off to him with "Chief Long?" after a reporter asks "Can you talk a little bit about the security of the event itself, who was there security-wise." FULL SURROUNDING CONTEXT, contiguous: "But I can tell you about our venue today. This was an open venue. This was outside. We did have six officers working that event. We had probably over 3,000 people that were in attendance... he was in a lower area surrounded by buildings. // We had some plainclothes police officers that were in the crowd as well. We trained for these things and you think you had things covered and these things, unfortunately, they happen. You try to get your bases covered and unfortunately today we didn't. And because of that, we had this tragic incident. So, we did have officers there. We had Charlie Kirk's team. He has a security team that travels with him and they were here with him when he was shot." WHAT HE PRECISELY CONCEDED: that the generic aspiration ("you try to get your bases covered") was not achieved on the day. He names no omitted measure, no breached protocol, no responsible party, and no failing by any person. The sentence sits between "We trained for these things" and an enumeration of what WAS in place, and its grammatical subject shifts from generic second person ("you try") to "we" — whose referent (UVU PD alone? the whole effort?) he never fixes. He was also speaking before the shooter was identified, before the shot's origin was established (Commissioner Mason at the same podium said only "Potentially from a roof"), and before any review existed — so he was not in a position to know what specifically had not been covered.
findings.locator: files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2026-08-16_rev_press-conference-on-charlie-kirk-shooting.txt — Jeff Long block opening at ( 12:52 ), quote in the ( 13:48 ) segment; Rev timestamps are stream offsets, ±5 min as clock times, not converted here
findings.limits: HIGH confidence that he said these words in this capacity. This does NOT establish that a security failure occurred, that any measure was omitted, or that any person underperformed — it establishes an expression of regret by a grieving chief hours after a killing on his campus. The strongest reading AGAINST treating it as an admission: five minutes later he describes the arrangement as joint and routine (Finding 4), which a considered admission of failure would sit badly with; no other official at any of the four conferences echoes, endorses or elaborates on it; and it is the ONLY sentence approaching self-criticism in ~95 minutes of official remarks across four conferences (Finding 5). Nothing here bears on any member of Mr. Kirk's private team, none of whom is named, described or implicated. What would change it: a Long deposition, an after-action report, or sworn testimony in which he specifies what "we didn't" refers to.

findings.label: Named state official disclaims all DPS and FBI role in planning or securing the event — and leaves "was that roof being monitored?" unanswered
findings.what_the_record_says: Speaker identified from CONTENT: "I'm Beau Mason, commissioner for the Utah Department of Public Safety." James Matthews of Sky News asks, on the record: "can I ask what were the security arrangements in place? Was that roof being monitored? It's a question many people will have." Mason answers on the suspect at length, then: "As far as the security, I cannot speak to that. Neither the Department of Public Safety nor the Federal Bureau of Investigation was involved in the planning or security of this event, and that'll have to be a question later for other agencies." The roof-monitoring half of the question is never answered — not by Mason, not by FBI SAC Robert Bohls (self-identified, "special agent in charge of the Salt Lake field office"), not at either later conference. Combined with Finding 4, this narrows the responsibility map to four bodies, each sourced to a named official: Turning Point USA organized the event (Utah County Attorney Jeff Gray, 09-16: "Turning Point USA... organized a public outdoor event"); UVU hosted it; UVU PD supplied six officers (Long, 09-10; corroborated under oath, Finding 6); Mr. Kirk's private team traveled with him (Long, 09-10). DPS and FBI are affirmatively excluded from the planning side by the DPS commissioner himself.
findings.locator: files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2026-08-16_rev_fbi-press-conference-on-kirk-shooting.txt — question at Media ( 08:31 ), answer at ( 09:03 ); Mason self-ID at ( 00:37 ). Phrase "planning or security" returns ZERO across all 80 .md files in the repo — new to the library.
findings.limits: Establishes what DPS's commissioner asserted about his own and the FBI's role, one day after. It does NOT establish that no federal or other state entity had any pre-event awareness — Mason speaks only for DPS and FBI, and the coordinator's held Bagley cross shows Bagley did not know whether other agencies covered the event ("I don't know"). The steelman for Mason: a co-lead investigating agency has an obvious institutional reason to state early and plainly that it was not the planning authority, and that is a legitimate clarification, not evasion. The unanswered roof question is an absence at ONE press conference, not evidence that the roof was unmonitored — see Finding 3 for what the record does say about that roof.

findings.label: T1: the State's own charging document describes the shooting position as adjacent to an open, publicly-accessible walkway reachable by climbing one railing
findings.what_the_record_says: Verbatim from the filed 10-page Information: "The suspected shooting position is adjacent to an open, publicly-accessible walkway. To access the suspected location, a person must climb over a railing and then drop to the roof only slightly below. The UVU officer climbed over the railing and down onto the roof." Surveillance is described as recording the individual "cross the railing from the public walkway and drop onto the roof at approximately 12:15 p.m." County Attorney Jeff Gray read this near-verbatim aloud at the 09-16 charging conference. Independently corroborated at T1 by the sworn Day-1 witness (addressed on the record by both counsel as "Officer Bagley", though every answer carries the Rev label "Richard Novak" — CONTENT WINS), who reached the roof the same way: "And it's a public stairway?" — "Yeah"; "When I got on top, I hopped over the guardrail." This is the STATE — the party charging the grave-risk-of-death aggravator, with every incentive to characterize the position as concealed or fortified — describing it as open and public.
findings.locator: files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2025-09-16_information-charging-document_dc27880532.txt ("5 The suspected shooting position is adjacent to an open, publicly-accessible walkway"); read aloud at 2026-08-16_rev_update-on-charlie-kirk-shooter.txt ( 10:35 )–( 11:19 ); Bagley at prelim-hearing-transcripts/day1.txt ( 01:42:55 ) and ( 01:43:12 ). Note: the phrase is ABSENT from the short filed PC affidavit (dc27880530) and ABSENT from CR-E08 — a completeness gap in the library, not an error.
findings.limits: Established: the physical description in the State's own filing, both U+FFFE readings, positive controls in the same file (officer 6, police 20, Kirk 44, roof 14). NOT established: that leaving that position uncovered was unreasonable, or that anyone was assigned or expected to cover it. It cuts BOTH ways and must be recorded as cutting both ways — no locked door was defeated and no perimeter was breached, because the record describes none there; equally, no forced entry was required. Whether a six-officer detail should have posted the Losee roof is a judgment nobody in this record makes. The one sworn answer on point is Bagley's: asked whether anyone ever discussed covering the Losee building, "No"; asked who was assigned it, "I don't." What would change it: a UVU PD event plan, a post-order, or expert testimony on campus-event standards.

findings.label: CONFIRMATION LOGGED: both officials who described the arrangement described it as joint and routine — and the sworn record shows a live assignment, not an absent one
findings.what_the_record_says: Asked directly, "Was it your team or Kirk's team or a combination of both that kind of set the security protocol for the event?", Chief Long answered: "So we work together. He has his team and they do this all over the country, we all know. That this is not uncommon for them. They're very comfortable on campuses. And I was coordinating with his lead security guy. So yeah, we were working together." (No individual is named; "his lead security guy" is a role, and this file keeps it a role.) The record's own answers to the security question, given their full weight: Utah "is an open carry state, so yes" students may carry (Bagley, sworn); the venue was outdoor and open on a public campus (Long: "This was an open venue. This was outside"); plainclothes officers were in the crowd (Long); responsibility was genuinely split across at least four bodies (Finding 2). VERIFICATION OF CR-E05, NOT INHERITED — I re-read day1.txt directly. All four CR-E05 propositions hold verbatim, but with a qualifier CR-E05's summary compresses away and which materially helps the officials: Bagley's answers are scoped to himself and to that morning. "Did you attend any type of debrief or briefing or meeting to prepare for the security of this event?" — "I did not because that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags... Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent. Therefore, he sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area." Asked whether such a meeting happened at all: "I don't know." Briefing materials: "No, not that morning." Operational or tactical plan: "For this event, no." AND, on direct, he did receive a specific assignment on coming on duty: "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end. So we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area."
findings.locator: files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2026-08-16_rev_press-conference-on-charlie-kirk-shooting.txt, question at Speaker 14 ( 14:56 ), answer at Jeff Long ( 15:06 ); day1.txt ( 01:02:41 ) assignment, ( 02:43:27 )–( 02:44:22 ) briefing, ( 02:47:57 ) materials, ( 04:05:02 ) tactical plan. "lead security guy" returns ZERO across all 80 repo .md files — new to the library.
findings.limits: HIGH that Long asserted coordination and that Bagley so testified. MEDIUM-HIGH at most for the proposition the assertion implies. Long's "we work together" is an unelaborated T2 claim by the official with the most at stake in it; nothing in the record states what the coordination consisted of, when it occurred, or what it produced. The genuine tension — and it is a gap, not a contradiction — is that the chief describes command-level coordination while the one officer who has testified describes receiving no briefing, no written materials and no plan. Both can be true: Long describes what he did with a counterpart; Bagley describes what reached one of six officers on an overtime shift during an emergent disturbance. Do not resolve it either way on this record. Nothing here reflects on the conduct of any member of Mr. Kirk's private team, and no such person is named. What would change it: testimony from Chief Long, or from any of the other five officers.

findings.label: Three named officials, three crowd figures — and the outlier is in the State's own filing, where crowd size is an element
findings.what_the_record_says: Chief Long, 09-10: "We had probably over 3,000 people that were in attendance." Officer Bagley under oath on direct, asked how many were present: "I'd say there was several thousand people because you had it on the grass that was jam packed... So it was pretty packed, several thousand people" — and on cross, asked "Did you all have an idea there were going to be thousands and thousands of people there or was that a surprise to you?", he answered "Had an idea." The State's filed Information, 09-16, read aloud verbatim by Jeff Gray: "Consequently, several hundred people attended." That is roughly an order of magnitude apart, and the low figure is the one in the charging instrument. (An unrelated "several hundred" appears in the same document describing the Hall of Flags walkway as "spanning several hundred feet" — I opened both hits and they are distinct.)
findings.locator: 2026-08-16_rev_press-conference-on-charlie-kirk-shooting.txt ( 13:09 ); prelim-hearing-transcripts/day1.txt ( 01:37:58 ) and ( 02:44:42 )–( 02:44:49 ); 2025-09-16_information-charging-document_dc27880532.txt ("Consequently, several hundred people attended"), read aloud at 2026-08-16_rev_update-on-charlie-kirk-shooter.txt ( 07:31 ). findings.limits: HIGH that the three figures are stated as recorded. It is NOT established that any of them is wrong or that any official misstated anything: "several hundred" is not falsified by "several thousand" if the pleader was counting only the fenced seating area or writing conservatively, and a charging document has no motive to understate a crowd when the aggravator it charges depends on people being at risk — which is the strongest argument that it is a drafting choice, not an error. Why it matters anyway, twice over: (a) the six-officers ratio, which is the whole quantitative core of the security-adequacy question, is 1:500 or 1:50 depending on which figure is right; (b) crowd size feeds the charged grave-risk-of-death aggravator, live and unresolved before Judge Graf on 2026-09-01. Recommend a new D-number. What would change it: the UVU event registration or attendance estimate, or the State's own basis for "several hundred" on the record.

findings.label: THE PROFFER'S PROCEDURAL FUNCTION: a party's unobjected-to proffer offered for a limited closure purpose — and the court granted only part of one request and denied the other outright
findings.what_the_record_says: Filed 2026-02-02, signed "/s/ Ryan McBride, Deputy Utah County Attorney" for the State, captioned "PROFFER OF FACTS REGARDING CLOSURE OF PORTIONS OF EVIDENTIARY HEARING ON MOTION TO DISQUALIFY UCAO," invoking Utah R. Jud. Admin. 4-202(2)(A),(B),(E). Its opening records the limited posture: counsel "conferred with defense counsel and, for the purposes of closing the courtroom … for the testimony of Prosecutor A and Adult Child only, defense counsel does not object to the following proffer." Its footnote 1 records that "The Court previously denied the motion to close the entirety of the Evidentiary Hearing." Paragraph 6 is the operative one for this task: "Members of Charlie Kirk's security team have reported threats, doxing – the publication of personal information online for harassment purposes, and risks to them since Charlie Kirk's murder" — sitting alongside ¶5 (witnesses threatened; some relocated; many deleted accounts and changed handles), ¶7 (defence counsel hired private security), ¶8 and ¶9 (UCAO and Sheriff raised security protocols). WHAT THE COURT DID: the 2026-02-03 minute order records two ORAL closure requests and two different outcomes — on the defence's motion for "the next witness," the court "denies in part and grants in part"; on the State's request for the following witness, "Court addresses counsel and denies the request to close the hearing for the next witness," and Chad Grunander then testified in open court.

findings.limits: ⚠️ REV TIMESTAMPS ARE STREAM OFFSETS, ±5 minutes as clock times, and are not converted to times of day here. THE ANCHORS ARE NOT THE CONNECTIONS: that a chief coordinated with a team lead does not establish that any particular measure was taken, and the same testimony that supplies these confirmations also supplies the counterweight — no briefing, no meeting, no operational or tactical plan, no written materials, no magnetometers, no drones, nobody assigned to the Losee building, and "I don't know" whether any other agency covered the event. Long's account is a same-day statement by an official whose own department's posture was at issue, made before any investigation reported; it is Tier 2, not tested, and Q-40-style caution applies. ⚠️ Bagley's "I don't know" answers about other agencies are a LINE OFFICER'S knowledge and do not contradict the chief's account of coordination — those are different questions and must not be merged. The "several down in the crowds" line runs TOWARD the team's presence being denser than the library records, which is exactly why an audit trail that only ever runs one way is a bias signal; it is one witness's recollection, uncorroborated, and nothing about numbers or positioning follows from it. Grade Medium-high, not High, because the phrase is a single sworn answer in a machine transcript and no certified transcript is held. Confidence is NOT a judgement that the arrangement was adequate — this project takes no position on that, and no security member's conduct is criticised or questioned anywhere in this pass.
