findings.label: The master calibration: security adequacy is not an element of any charged offence, so the preliminary-hearing record would not contain it even if the underlying facts exist
findings.what_the_record_says: The defence's 2026-08-11 briefing states the sole aggravator is that Mr. Robinson "knowingly created a great risk of death to another other than Charlie Kirk and the defendant," called "the sole aggravator alleged." Across ~50 passages of KGRD argument and roughly two dozen out-of-state authorities, security personnel enter the analysis ONLY as bodies whose proximity might create risk — never as agents whose arrangements are in question. The defence's attack is that the State asks the court to speculate "[t]hat the shooter actually observed security personnel standing an unknown distance from Mr. Kirk." The State's interest is that people were close to Mr. Kirk; the defence's interest is that their positions and distances are unknown. Neither party's interest is served by establishing whether the security arrangement was adequate.
findings.locator: ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2026-08-11_defendant-prelim-hearing-briefing.txt — search "sole aggravator alleged" and "That the shooter actually observed security personnel"; corroborated in the ALT-EXTRACTION twin. Both U+FFFE readings run; the hyphen reading surfaced additional matches (e.g. "at-tended") confirming both were exercised.
findings.limits: This does NOT establish that no security plan, threat assessment or after-action review exists — it establishes the opposite of a necessary-containment relationship. A preliminary hearing tests probable cause for the charged offences; the adequacy of the victim's security arrangements is not an element of any of them, so the search space would NOT necessarily contain the record if it existed. Every absence in this file inherits that weakness and must not be read as evidence of absence. Steelman of the contrary view: the KGRD aggravator does put persons-near-the-victim in issue, so SOME security-adjacent facts had to be developed — and they were (Finding 5); what was never in issue is whether the arrangement was sufficient. What would change it: a defence motion to strike the aggravator that turned on security positioning, or a civil/legislative proceeding where adequacy IS an element.

findings.label: Thirteen pre-event institutional records are absent under capable patterns — and the corpus proves the patterns work, because it contains a fully developed security regime for the COURTROOM
findings.what_the_record_says: Null across all 71 sweepable artifacts under both U+FFFE readings: event security plan; operations order / incident action plan; advance team or site survey; security contract/agreement/provider; pre-event threat or risk assessment; UVU event-security policy; after-action or post-incident review. Every "in charge / incident command" hit is POST-shooting (Hull put in charge of the scene "approximately an hour after"; the Fugal incident command centre). Capability controls all fired: "security plan" 6 hits, "credible threat" 10, "debrief" 4, "contract" 6 (non-contaminant), "roof" 616, "policy" 182, "how many" 86. The contrast is the finding: "security plan" DOES exist in this corpus — in the certified transcript of the 2025-10-24 sealed motion hearing, where the State argues the defence request "is contrary to the security plan for this court that the court's security administrator has developed," anchored to Utah Judicial Council Rule 3-414(9)(C), with "the sheriff, who's responsible to provide security here" named as the responsible agency. A written plan, a named administrator, a promulgated rule and a named responsible body — for the courtroom. Nothing of the kind for the event at which Mr. Kirk was killed.

The courtroom-security contrast has an innocent and probably sufficient explanation: the defendant's restraint was a live litigated motion, so courtroom security HAD to be developed; event security was never in issue (Finding 1). What would change it: any of these records surfacing via GRAMA, a civil suit, or a legislative review.

findings.label: The only institutional account of the event's security posture is a named police chief's extemporaneous same-day press statement — and no part of it was ever tested under oath, including a plainclothes-officer claim that appears exactly once in the entire corpus
findings.what_the_record_says: Asked "Can you talk a little bit about the security of the event itself, who was there security-wise," Governor Cox says "Chief Long?" and the speaker self-identifies: "So my name is Jeff Long. I'm the police chief here at UVU." He states: "This was an open venue. This was outside. We did have six officers working that event. We had probably over 3,000 people that were in attendance, sat down in kind of a bowl area here on the central campus... he was in a lower area surrounded by buildings." Then: "We had some plainclothes police officers that were in the crowd as well. We trained for these things and you think you had things covered and these things, unfortunately, they happen. You try to get your bases covered and unfortunately today we didn't." And: "we did have officers there. We had Charlie Kirk's team. He has a security team that travels with him and they were here with him when he was shot." The phrase "plainclothes" appears ONCE in 71 artifacts — here. It appears in zero sworn testimony. Officer Bagley, one of the six, was asked directly whether any agency besides "Mr. Kirk's private security team and your six officers" covered the event and answered "I don't know," and said he saw nobody armed "other than law enforcement" — nobody ever asked him about plainclothes colleagues.

Bagley: prelim-hearing-transcripts/day1.txt 02:47:28 and 02:46:35.
findings.limits: HIGH as to what Chief Long SAID; the truth of its contents is UNVERIFIED. He is a named public official speaking in his public role and is properly named. This was said within hours of the shooting, before any investigation — the ordinary hazards of same-day remarks apply in BOTH directions: "we trained for these things" is an unverified affirmative claim of preparation, and "today we didn't [get our bases covered]" is an unverified self-critical concession. Neither should be adopted. The apparent tension between "six officers" and "plainclothes officers as well" is NOT resolved here: Bagley's "six of us... patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief" may or may not include plainclothes personnel, and no source in the corpus resolves it. This is emphatically NOT a finding of misconduct by anyone. What would change it: sworn testimony or a UVU PD staffing record for 2025-09-10.

findings.label: Not one member of Mr. Kirk's private security team testified or was interviewed anywhere in the held record, and the only number ever attached to them is a description of a video frame
findings.what_the_record_says: Eight witness slots across five hearing days: Bagley, Hull, Faumuina, Bakker, Davis, Karner, Oliver — every one a police officer, agent, or forensic examiner. No security-team member, no UVU administrator, no TPUSA staff member, no event organiser. Null under patterns capable of matching sworn/interviewed security personnel. The team appears in the corpus in only three registers, never more: bare existence (Bagley — "Were you aware of whether Mr. Kirk had his own security team present there with him?" "Yes"; "I saw one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me"; "I was aware he was armed"); post-shot action (Hull — "Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid and they conducted what would be called a hasty transport to Timpanogos Hospital"); and position in a video frame for the KGRD argument (defence brief — "what appear to be two security personnel in front and diagonal to Mr. Kirk, standing in the grass area by the barrier"; "One of Mr. Kirk's security guards comes into frame from the right of Mr. Kirk three seconds after the shot"). That "two" is the ONLY numeral attached to private security anywhere in 71 artifacts — and it describes what is visible in one exhibit, not a roster. Note also that Bagley was asked "Did you communicate with any of those people?" and answered "I saw one of the individuals..." — an answer establishing visual proximity, not communication. No account of police/private-security coordination exists in the record.

findings.limits: ROLE ONLY — no individual is named here, and none may be. Docket 368 ¶¶5–6 (sworn proffer, Deputy Utah County Attorney, filed 2026-02-02) records that security-team members "have reported threats, doxing... and risks to them," and that witnesses "have relocated" and "deleted online accounts"; compiling identities or backgrounds would be an active, court-documented harm. This absence is WEAK evidence of anything: the State proved its probable-cause case through law enforcement, and a security member's testimony was not needed for any element (Finding 1). None of these people is accused of anything by anyone, and nothing here implies otherwise. The "two" figure is a description of an exhibit image by an advocate, is expressly hedged ("what appear to be"), and must never be reported as the size of the detail. What would change it: a witness list for the 2026-09-01 argument day or trial, or a civil proceeding.

findings.label: Verified in the other direction: the record affirmatively establishes the facts that support the arrangement's reasonableness, and the State itself put the roof's accessibility in evidence
findings.what_the_record_says: Logged as explicit confirmations, because an audit trail that runs one way is a bias signal. (a) On the State's DIRECT, Bagley established the Losee roof's access: four stories; reachable by "an outside stairway," asked "Is that open to the public?" — "It is"; from the pathway "there's actually a little handrail, like a little guardrail, probably about a couple feet high that somebody could jump over"; asked "Is that area restricted? Is it off limits?" — "Yes, it is. There's a natural barrier with the guardrail... It's gravel roof"; "But someone could hop over that railway?" — "Yes." Reaching the roof required no forced entry and defeated no access control, because there was none to defeat. (b) Utah "is an open carry state" (Bagley, 02:46:25) — lawful arms on campus were not themselves a security signal. (c) The venue was open and outdoors on a public campus, in "kind of a bowl area... surrounded by buildings" (Chief Long) — geography adverse to any perimeter. (d) Responsibility was genuinely split: UVU PD, Mr. Kirk's private detail, and other agencies including a sworn officer on a security detail from another department. (e) UVU PD is small: 15 officers employed total, six assigned (Bagley, 02:44:31–02:44:36). (f) The morning was consumed by a live incident: Chief Long got "a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent," and sent the two on-duty officers to it — Bagley's stated reason for attending no briefing.
findings.locator: prelim-hearing-transcripts/day1.txt — roof access 01:12:36–01:13:38; open carry 02:46:25; staffing 02:44:31–02:44:36; Hall of Flags disturbance 02:43:36 and 02:48:12 (line ~4745). Chief Long: 2026-08-16_rev_press-conference-on-charlie-kirk-shooting.txt ~13:09–13:48. Officer Goforth on security detail: day2.txt 00:57:54.
findings.limits: ⚠️ SPEAKER-LABEL HAZARD APPLIED: every Bagley answer above carries the transcript label "Richard Novak," a defence attorney's name. Attribution here is by CONTENT — the witness is answering examination questions, was addressed as "Officer Bagley" in adjacent turns, and gave his own employment history; the 01:12–01:13 questions are the State's direct (Grunander-labelled), the 02:4x questions are Ms. Nester's cross. Content wins over labels throughout. The roof-access facts establish the PHYSICAL arrangement; they establish nothing about whether anyone considered controlling that stairway for this event — Bagley was never assigned Losee and "I don't" know who was. The Hall of Flags account's first sentence is what the chief was TOLD, second-hand inside the testimony; Bagley's own first-hand line is "when I got there... People were throwing stuff down on the tent." These confirmations do not establish adequacy — they establish that the ordinary inference of neglect is not the only available reading.

findings.label: The discovery-producer inventory is entirely governmental — but by its own caption, which means it cannot support the inference it invites
findings.what_the_record_says: The 2026-04-02 continuance motion, Exhibit E, is captioned "List of Law Enforcement Agencies Producing Discovery to Utah State Bureau of Investigation (as of March 26, 2026)" and lists 28 entries — American Fork PD, ATF, BYU PD, Cottonwood Heights PD, FBI, Lehi, Lindon, Lone Peak, Orem, Payson, Provo, Salem, Salt Lake City PD, Salt Lake County SO, Santaquin, Saratoga Springs, Spanish Fork, Springville, St. George, SBI, SIAC, UCAO Investigations, University of Utah PD, UT Crime Lab (UBFS), Utah County SO, Utah State University PD, Utah Valley University PD, Washington County SO. Not one private entity; no security contractor; no TPUSA. Exhibits B–D put the production at 19,612 files, 61,500 pages, 61 audio files (31 hours) and 5,134 video files (>698 hours). Relatedly, the only contract touching the event anywhere in the corpus is TPUSA's videographer arrangement — "Visual Impulse... they contract with TPUSA to film their events" — not a security contract. And Exhibit 5.1, the one TPUSA institutional document in evidence (a self-authenticating Rule 1102 statement by David Engelhardt, litigated at length on Day 2), covers TPUSA's IRS status, purposes, mission, Mr. Kirk's relationship to it and the "200 plus" events he headlined — and says nothing about how those events were secured.

findings.limits: THIS IS AN ANTI-OVERREACH FINDING. The list is captioned "Law Enforcement Agencies," so a private security provider would be excluded from it BY CONSTRUCTION even if it had produced material. The inventory therefore CANNOT support "no private-security material is in discovery" — it supports only that the sole producer inventory the record gives is framed governmentally, and that no counterpart list of non-law-enforcement producers appears. Nor does it exclude private-security material arriving via a police agency's file. The Exhibit 5.1 point is likewise scoped: it was offered for motive and the victim-targeting enhancement, so its silence on security is what one would expect, not a suppression. What would change it: a discovery index by custodian rather than by agency, or a privilege/production log.

SURVIVES on the primary source. The defect's EXTENT is corrected UPWARD, and four fidelity/locator slips are fixed.

=== SEARCH-HAZARD DISCLOSURE (stated before any null) ===
day1.txt read in Python with errors='replace'. Measured on this file: NUL bytes = 0; U+FFFE occurrences = 0. The both-readings hazard therefore does not bite here, but I did not assume that — every pattern below was ALSO run through artifact_search.find(), which tests BOTH the joined and hyphenated readings, and returned identical counts. CORPUS CONTAMINATION: the mis-banked 2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286 artifact is outside my search space entirely (my space is day1.txt and CR-E05), so it is excluded by scope, not by term, and no true hits are destroyed.

=== CONFIRMED VERBATIM (T1 · High, as to what the witness said) ===
1. 02:43:36 (L4742/4746). Q: "did you attend any type of debrief or briefing or meeting to prepare for the security of this event?" A: "I did not because that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags... The Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent. Therefore, he sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area."
2. 02:44:04→02:44:16 (L4750/4754). Q: "So you never attended any kind of... debrief or meeting to talk about what the officers on scene were going to do that day to keep everybody safe?" A: "No, not that morning."
3. 02:44:16→02:44:18 (L4758/4762). Q: "Do you know if there was such a meeting?" A: "I don't know because when I got there, it was starting to... People were throwing stuff down on the tent." DISPOSITIVE, and confirmed exactly as the finding renders it.
4. 02:48:12 (L4974/4978). Q: "Did you receive any type of briefing materials, written materials prior to the event that talked about who would be covering what...?" A: "No, not that morning. Like I said, it started getting hectic..."
5. 04:05:26 (L5431/5435), first substantive question after lunch, the judge having noted "we left off cross-examination." Counsel restates her own premise — "we talked about that you had had no briefing or no materials about security on campus for this particular event" — then asks "Did you ever have any operational or tactical plan THAT YOU WERE GIVEN for that event?" A: "For this event, no." The finding is right that the premise is counsel's, not the witness's, and right that the question as put is scoped to what he was GIVEN.
6. Qualifier count confirmed: "that morning" appears three times in this stretch, twice as the express qualifier "not that morning."

=== FIX 1 — THE FINDING'S STATED LIMIT IS WRONG; §3.5 IS NOT CLEAN ===
The finding says CR-E05 §3.5 "is already correct and carries the scope expressly" and locates the defect only in §7 and a findings roll-up. Read directly, §3.5 line 193 states:
    "**Nobody was ever assigned to cover the Losee building**, and he does not know if anyone was."
That bolded lead clause is an unscoped universal negative about the arrangement, immediately self-contradicted by its own second clause. It is the SAME error the finding attributes solely to §7, and it sits in the RECORDING layer — the layer the finding expressly exonerates. Fixing §7 while leaving §3.5 untouched would leave the sharper error in the more authoritative layer.
Additionally, §3.5 line 189 — "**No briefing, no debrief, no meeting** that morning; **no operational or tactical plan, no written materials**; he does not know whether any security meeting occurred" — is scoped as to TIME ("that morning") but not as to PERSON for the plan and materials sub-claims, whereas the transcript scopes them expressly ("that you were given," "did you receive"). The trailing clause restores epistemic scope for the MEETING sub-claim only. Partial credit to §3.5, not a clean bill.

=== FIX 2 — THE LOSEE QUESTION IS COMPOUND, AND THE FINDING QUOTES ONLY HALF ===
Actual text at 02:45:43 (L4838): "And did anyone ever talk to you about covering anything near or on top of or in the Losee building? Were you ever assigned that area before the shooting?" — a COMPOUND question answered by a single "No" (02:45:53). The finding quotes only the second clause. This does not damage the finding; the omitted clause is also witness-scoped ("talk to YOU") and reinforces it. But the recording layer must carry the question as actually put.

=== FIX 3 — LOCATOR CORRECTION ===
The finding attributes "nobody assigned to the Losee building" to "the findings roll-up." It is not there. §6 and §6A contain no Losee-assignment claim at all. The string lives in the REVISION LOG, v1.0 row (line 422): "His cross records no pre-event briefing or plan, six officers for thousands, no magnetometers, nobody assigned to the Losee building..." The prefix "His cross records" supplies partial scope; the phrase itself still states a universal negative. Cite the revision log, not §6.

=== FIX 4 — THE PRESUPPOSITION POINT IS RIGHT AND SHOULD BE STATED AS A RULE ===
"Do you know who was?" (02:45:54) does presuppose that someone was assigned, and "I don't" (02:45:55) is non-knowledge. Correctly, the finding refuses to treat the presupposition as evidence EITHER WAY. A questioner's premise is not an answer — it neither establishes that nobody was assigned nor that somebody was.

=== CAPABLE-PATTERN NULL, RE-RUN (the finding rests partly on "no contrary evidence appears anywhere in Day 1") ===
Battery over day1.txt, stems, both readings: brief 32 hits · debrief 4 · meeting 14 · plan 14 · tactical 2 · operational 2 · assign 32 · Losee 180 · Chief 12 · securit 22 · detail 12 · coverage 2 · cover 22 · six 24 · "6" 24 · "15" 224. The battery is DEMONSTRABLY CAPABLE — "brief," "meeting," "plan," "assign" and "tactical" all return the target passages, so a contrary passage could not hide from it. Result: every pre-event briefing/plan/materials hit in the entire day falls inside Bagley's cross (L4742–L5431). The only other "plan"/"assignment" language is Hull at L6763–L6823 describing the POST-shooting investigative response ("we did have a plan"; SBI agents "assigned specific tasks") — a different subject, after the shot, and not evidence about the pre-event security arrangement. The finding's null holds, now with a stated scope: a claim about this Rev rendering of Day 1, not about the world or the certified transcript.

=== BOTH DIRECTIONS — CONFIRMATION LOGGED EXPRESSLY, RUNNING AGAINST THE FLATTENED READING ===
This must be recorded because it is the strongest available answer to any "he was given nothing" inference, and the finding did not surface it:
- On DIRECT, 01:02:32 (L1572): "Did you receive a specific assignment shortly after coming onto duty?" — "Yes, I did." At L1584: "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end... so we wanted to secure that area. So I was put up on top of the Hall of Flags on the south end." At L1608 he identifies a barrier "that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk."
- On CROSS, 02:44:36 (L4778), asked how many were assigned to cover the event: "There was six of us that were, there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief." He knows the deployment structure.
So the witness WAS assigned a post before the shot, a barrier WAS maintained, and he DID know the shape of the deployment. The negatives concern briefings, written materials and a formal operational/tactical plan given to him — not an absence of assignment or of responsive activity. CR-E05 §7's pro-prosecution paragraph already logs the responsive-activity half; credit where due, and that paragraph should be cross-referenced from the corrected §3.5 bullet so the two never travel apart.
- Also giving the record's own answer its full weight: Utah is an open-carry state (02:46:25); the event was outdoors on a public campus; a member of Mr. Kirk's security team was present and armed on the Hall of Flags beside the officer before the shot (02:46:55–02:47:07); and responsibility was split across at least three bodies, with the witness expressly disclaiming knowledge of what other agencies covered the event (02:47:28: "I don't know").

=== THE NARROWER SUPPORTED FORM ===
T1 · Confidence: High (as to what the witness said and how it was scoped).
"On cross-examination the witness testified that HE attended no briefing, debrief or meeting to prepare for the event that morning; that HE received no briefing or written materials; that HE was given no operational or tactical plan for that event; that no one talked to HIM about covering the Losee building and HE was never assigned that area before the shooting; and that HE does not know whether such a meeting occurred or who, if anyone, was assigned to the Losee. Separately and first-hand, when he reached the Losee roof after the shot there was no law enforcement on the roof, the stairway or the walkway. He also testified on direct that he DID receive a specific pre-event assignment — to secure the south end of the Hall of Flags — where a barrier had been placed."

=== NOT ESTABLISHED (carry verbatim wherever the above is used) ===
That no briefing occurred. That no plan existed. That nobody was assigned to the Losee building. That there was "no Losee coverage." Nothing in Day 1 establishes any of these; every negative in the day is scoped to one witness's attendance, receipt or assignment. The post-shooting rooftop observation is first-hand but is about the state of the roof AFTER the shot and cannot carry a claim about pre-event assignment.

=== THE FAIR INFERENCE, KEPT IN ITS OWN LAYER ===
Steelman preserved and endorsed: an officer of 26 years, on an overtime shift signed up for in advance, who received no materials and attended nothing, is meaningful circumstantial evidence about the arrangement as a whole, and no contrary evidence appears anywhere in Day 1 under a capable pattern. That is a defensible inference and should be stated AS an inference in the analyst layer, graded no higher than Medium, never as a Tier 1 finding, and never merged into the recording layer.

=== WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT ===
Any UVU PD operations order, event-security plan, post assignment sheet or briefing record for 2025-09-10; or testimony from Chief Long or any other of the six officers. → acquisition target.

=== SCOPE AND CARE ===
Residual: I re-verified only the passages named above plus the Day 1 briefing/plan/assign pattern space and the Losee mentions in CR-E05. I did not re-verify CR-E05's other sections, Days 2–5, or the timeline file. Rev offsets are stream offsets, ±5 minutes as clock times, and none is converted to a time of day here. No individual member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named or described anywhere above; they appear only by role. NO FAULT OR FAILURE BY ANY PERSON is asserted or implied — not by the officer, not by the chief, not by any member of the security team. The point of this correction is the OPPOSITE of insinuation: it removes three unscoped negatives that read as findings about an arrangement when the record supports only statements about one witness's own knowledge. Tyler Robinson is presumed innocent and has NOT been bound over; the preliminary hearing is unfinished, with 2026-09-01 its last day, argument only, on a closed evidentiary record.

On direct, hours before the cross, the same witness testified: "Did you receive a specific assignment shortly after coming onto duty?" — "Yes, I did." — "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end... I was put up on top of the Hall of Flags on the south end" (01:02:32-01:02:41), and a tape barrier was placed to keep people off the overlook above the tent (01:03:13). Any consolidated line reading "no plan" is contradicted inside the same file.

BOTH DIRECTIONS, LOGGED EXPLICITLY. Cutting toward adequacy on this record: the chief of police was personally on scene ("five others that were there with the chief," 02:44:36); Chief Long received the report of people on the Hall of Flags and diverted the two on-duty officers to it, which is a command function operating; Bagley was posted on the elevated overlook with a barrier; a member of Mr. Kirk's security team was armed and posted on that same Hall of Flags overlook beside him before the shot (02:46:51-02:47:07), so an elevated overwatch position WAS staffed by the private detail; Utah is an open-carry state (02:46:25); the event was outdoors on a public campus; and responsibility was split across at least three bodies, with Bagley unable to exclude other agencies (02:47:28).

SCOPED NULL, stated as the project requires. No pre-event security-planning evidence of any kind appears in this Rev rendering of day1.txt. verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES ON ITS CORE, BUT IS OVERSTATED IN FIVE PLACES — one of them a count of the primary text that is simply wrong, and one a remedy clause that contradicts the finding's own steelman.

WHAT HELD, BY DIRECT READING OF day1.txt lines 4899–4933:
The four quoted Q/A pairs are verbatim and the timestamps are exact. Q 02:46:45 "Were you aware of whether Mr. Kirk had his own security team present there with him?" / A 02:46:51 "Yes." Q 02:46:52 "Did you communicate with any of those people?" / A 02:46:55 "I saw one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me, yes." Q 02:46:58 "Okay. And that was before the shooting?" / A 02:47:00 "Yes. And then I saw several down in the crowds and down by him, yes." Q 02:47:03 "And were you aware of whether that person was armed either?" / A 02:47:07 "I was aware he was armed." The locator "02:46:45 through 02:47:08" and "23-second exchange" are both correct (02:47:08 is the next question stamp). The comparison locator 01:02:41 is correct and reads: "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end… So I was put up on top of the Hall of Flags on the south end."

SPEAKER, RESOLVED FROM CONTENT, NOT LABEL. The Rev label on every one of these answers is "Richard Novak" — a defence attorney of record (the signature block of tyler-robinson-ballistics-motion.txt reads "/s/ Richard G. Novak"). The witness is Officer Christopher Bagley, established from content twice: line 628 "the state calls Officer Chris Bagley," and line 672 the witness spelling his own name, "Christopher Bagley. Last name spelling B-A-G-L-E-Y." He is sworn at line 636–648 and leaves the stand at 04:22:09 (line 6287), so the whole exchange sits inside his testimony. Capacity: sworn police witness, cross-examination — a nameable public-capacity actor. The finding's attribution is right.

THE NULL, RE-RUN WITH CAPABLE PATTERNS, AND IT HOLDS. Scoped to Bagley's range (lines 628–6291), a battery of 18 stems capable of matching a described communication — communicat / radio / channel / dispatch / coordinat / deconflict / frequenc / walkie / earpiece / comms / liais / talk / spoke / speak / told / tell / conversation / greet / acknowledg / contact / inform / advis / relay / notif / discuss — returned 76 matching lines. POSITIVE CONTROL, and it is decisive: the battery DID catch every communication Bagley described — "I was informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody" (01:39:26), "Dispatch came back and advised me" (02:34:19), "I advised other officers that I needed the Losee building secured" (line 4482), "I advised her not to let anybody inside the crime scene" (line 4374), "relay information that I'd found to responding units" (line 4674), "I spoke to her" (line 3922), "I talked to her on the phone" (line 6171). Not one of the 76 describes any exchange with a member of Mr. Kirk's private security team. "communicat" occurs exactly ONCE in the whole of Bagley's testimony — inside counsel's question at 02:46:52. "channel," "deconflict," "frequenc," "walkie," "earpiece," "comms," "liais" return ZERO across all of day1 under both U+FFFE readings. A parallel sweep of day2.txt for securit/communicat/bodyguard adds nothing: the only security-posture hits are the already-known Officer Goforth line (00:57:54, a sworn Spanish Fork officer on a detail — a different category, not merged here) and counsel's Ty Phillips-video question (01:58:06). HAZARDS STATED: day1.txt carries ZERO U+FFFE and ZERO NUL bytes (measured), so the two readings are byte-identical for this file — the null is not being credited to a hazard it never faced; I ran artifact_search.find() anyway and both readings returned identically. The mis-banked contaminant (gov-uscourts-utd-165286) was out of scope for every transcript sweep; it entered only the corpus-wide Nester/Nestor sweep, where it returned zero for both spellings.

FIVE OVERSTATEMENTS.

(1) A WRONG COUNT OF THE PRIMARY TEXT. "the verb in the answer is 'saw,' twice, and then a third time." Measured inside the finding's own locator (02:46:45–02:47:08): "saw" = 2, "see" = 0. There is no third. The nearest candidate is "I did not see" at 02:46:35, which is outside the locator, is a negation, and answers a different question ("did you see anybody that was armed that day other than law enforcement?"). Two is enough to carry the point; three is not what the record says.

(2) "THE POLICE OVERWATCH POST" IS NOT IN THE RECORD AND IMPORTS A FUNCTION THAT WAS NEVER ASSIGNED. Bagley's own account of the assignment (01:02:41) is crowd control in response to a disturbance already under way: "we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area," elaborated on cross (02:43:36) as the chief diverting the two on-duty officers after a report of "people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent." "Overwatch" is a term of art connoting a covering or counter-sniper position. CR-E05 already holds the opposite on this exact point: "nothing in this record shows UVU PD had identified the Hall of Flags as an elevated firing position or had done any pre-event elevated-threat planning." Using "overwatch" recasts an ordinary co-location as a failed protective pairing — precisely the insinuation the standing constraint forbids, and it is unearned.

(3) "POSTED" IS AN INFERENCE. The testimony supports only that the officer SAW the individual "on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me." Nothing establishes that he was stationed there, by whom, or for how long. Note also that this transcript uses "individuals… on top of the Hall of Flags" earlier (02:43:36) for the civilians throwing things onto the tent, so the phrase has a competing referent a few minutes upstream; the security-team reading is right here (the question's antecedent is "those people" = Mr. Kirk's team, and the follow-up asks whether "that person" was armed), but "posted" is not what was said.

(4) THE REMEDY CLAUSE IS WRONG ON ITS FACE AND CONTRADICTS THE FINDING'S OWN STEELMAN. "that artifact covers the exact period" — it cannot. T1 puts Bagley at the Hall of Flags from shortly after his ~11:00 a.m. check-in (01:02:29, 01:02:41) until the shot he timed at 12:23 (01:37:11) — over 80 minutes — while the body camera is described as 27 minutes 35 seconds, starting at the Hall of Flags and ending on the Losee roof AFTER the shooting, where the battery died before the crime tape went up (04:12:23–04:12:54). 27:35 cannot span 80+ minutes plus the post-shot movement; it covers at most the tail of the co-location. The finding's own steelman says the two men stood together "for over an hour," so its two halves contradict each other. Compounding it: the duration is DEFENCE COUNSEL'S characterisation embedded in a compound question, and the witness's "Yes" at 04:12:54 answers the operative clause "that's the only body cam you have that day?" Nobody testified to measuring it. CR-E05 grades it exactly this way and keeps Q-53 open; the finding should not silently upgrade it.

(5) THE COUNSEL NAME IS A REV SPEAKER LABEL. "Ms. Nestor" is the label, not evidence. Measured across all banked .txt artifacts under both U+FFFE readings: "Nestor" = 1,388 hits confined to four files — day1.txt (604), day2.txt (390), day2_condensed.txt (390) and 4 in tyler-robinson-ballistics-motion.txt — i.e. essentially nothing but Rev speaker labels. "Nester" = 510 hits across 28 files, including every court filing (dkt250, dkt293, dkt348, dkt413, dkt137, dkt242, the 2026-08-11 defence briefing, the xchange case history) AND the transcript prose itself: her own self-introduction at 02:43:01 — "Officer Bagley, my name is Kathy Nester" — and the judge's own address at 01:05:17 and 01:05:45, "Ms. Nester." ⚠️ COUNTER-EVIDENCE LOGGED because the both-directions rule requires it: the signature block of tyler-robinson-ballistics-motion.txt reads "/s/ Kathryn N. Nestor," in the same filing that uses "Nester" elsewhere. So the spelling is not unanimous in the primary record — but the finding inherited the label without a stated basis, which is the hazard.

VERIFY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — CONFIRMATIONS LOGGED EXPLICITLY, because an audit that only ran one way would be a bias signal. Bagley affirmed Mr. Kirk DID have his own security team present (02:46:51); one member was on the Hall of Flags next to him before the shot (02:46:55–02:47:00); several more were in the crowds and near Mr. Kirk (02:47:00); and he was aware that member was armed (02:47:07). That last is the single strongest datum FOR the ordinary reading — how he became aware is not stated, and it may well have been by being told — so it does not resolve against the steelman. Utah is an open-carry state (02:46:25), the event was outdoors on a public campus, and UVU PD did take responsive action at this very location: the chief diverted the on-duty officers to the disturbance (02:43:36), a tape barrier was maintained along the walkway (01:03:13), and six armed officers covered the event (02:44:36, 02:45:03). DECISIVELY: Bagley never testified that there was no coordination. Asked whether any other agency covered the event — "I don't know" (02:47:28). Asked whether a security meeting occurred — "I don't know" (02:44:18). The record is SILENT on coordination, not NEGATIVE. That is why the headline needs tightening: "establishes co-location, not coordination" reads as establishing an absence. It establishes neither.

NOTHING HERE IMPLIES ANY FAULT, FAILURE OR OMISSION BY ANY MEMBER OF MR. KIRK'S SECURITY TEAM, and none may be drawn. No individual member is named, described, or identified anywhere in this refutation; the transcript does not name him, and the measured "Cutler" null across all 71 sweepable artifacts and every repository .md file stands unchallenged by anything I read. None of these people is accused of anything by anyone.

RESIDUAL SCOPE — WHAT I DID NOT RE-VERIFY: CR-E08's formulation of the State's grave-risk theory; day3 and day4; the 2026-02-02 proffer (dkt368) itself; the 2025-09-10 press conference attribution to Chief Jeff Long; State's Exhibits 8 and 9 as artifacts (I read only the defence's characterisation of them, which I did verify verbatim in the 2026-08-11 briefing); and Bagley's body-worn camera, which this library does not hold.

verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES ON ITS CORE, BUT IS OVERSTATED IN FOUR PLACES AND ONE SUB-CLAIM IS AFFIRMATIVELY WRONG.

WHAT I VERIFIED AND CONFIRMED (logged in both directions, per the standing rule):
1. Every quotation is verbatim. day1.txt lines 4899-4934 reproduce all four Q&A pairs exactly as the finding gives them, at exactly the timestamps claimed (02:46:45 / :51 / :52 / :55 / :58 / 02:47:00 / :03 / :07 / :08). The only deviation is a trimmed leading "Okay." at 02:46:58 — non-substantive.
2. The 01:02:41 comparison locator is correct: "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end... So I was put up on top of the Hall of Flags on the south end."
3. THE CENTRAL NULL IS REAL AND NOW PROPERLY MEASURED. Capable patterns, both U+FFFE readings (day1.txt carries 0 U+FFFE splits and 0 NULs, so the readings are identical here — I ran audit() to establish that, and ran find() under both anyway): "channel" 0 hits, "deconflict" 0 hits, "liaison" 0 hits. "coordinat" 4 hits, ALL OPENED: every one is Agent Hull on post-incident investigative coordination among agencies (crime lab, scene techs), none about pre-shooting UVU PD / private-team arrangements. "radio" 2 hits, both post-shot internal police traffic. "communicat" 3 hits: two are the judge's courtroom-decorum admonitions, and the third IS the question at issue — so the word appears exactly once in substantive testimony all day. The finding is right that the topic was raised once and never developed.
4. Lens (a) PASSES. No individual private security member is named or identifiable. Role-only reference throughout; no employment history, residence, family, social media, photograph, physical description, vehicle or licensing. The attributes carried (posted on the walkway, armed, present before the shot) are posture-in-a-public-capacity facts, not personal background. I confirm the transcript itself attaches no name: all five mentions of the security team in day1.txt (lines 4901, 4933, 4913, 8880, 8884) are nameless.
5. Lens (d) PASSES — no expression of regret is involved anywhere in the passage.
6. CR-E05's carried details check out against the transcript: overtime shift (4737), ~11:00 a.m. check-in (4725), Hall of Flags post (1583), no briefing/debrief/meeting (4741-4761), no operational or tactical plan (5430-5434), no written materials (4973-4977).

WHERE IT FAILS:
A. THE HEADLINE SUPPRESSES THE TERMINAL "YES". The answer is "I saw one of the individuals... right next to me, YES." To a yes/no question, an answer ending in "yes" is an affirmative. "The officer answered with a SIGHTING" is not a fair summary of an answer that both affirms and adds detail. The finding concedes this in its steelman and then proceeds as though the steelman lost — it did not.
B. "OR EXCHANGED ANY INFORMATION AT ALL" IS WRONG AND MUST COME OUT. This sits in the "NOT established" list, but the witness said "yes" to "did you communicate." You cannot list as unestablished the very thing the witness affirmed. The first three items in that list (coordinated, deconflicted sectors, shared a channel) survive; the fourth does not.
C. THE COUNT IS WRONG AND THE CLAUSE INSINUATES. "The verb in the answer is 'saw,' twice, and then a third time" — I counted the segment: "saw" appears TWICE, not three times. The word appearing three times is "aware." Worse, the clause implies the witness evaded the question. Nothing supports evasion: he answered affirmatively and volunteered detail unprompted. This is an insinuation about a NAMED SWORN OFFICER's candour, and it must go.
D. THE UNADDRESSED TENSION THAT CUTS AGAINST THE THESIS. Twenty seconds earlier, at 02:46:35, Bagley said he did NOT see anybody armed "other than law enforcement." At 02:47:07 he says he "was AWARE he was armed." "Aware" is not a sight verb. The finding builds its whole case on a sight/communicate verb distinction while ignoring that its fourth answer uses a knowledge verb whose basis is unstated — and one ordinary way to become aware another person is armed is to be told. The finding's strongest counter-argument is inside its own quoted passage and it does not engage it.
E. THE BODY-CAMERA "WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT" IS OVERSTATED. The locators (04:08:28, 04:12:54) and quotes are accurate, but "that artifact covers the exact period" is not established. Counsel described 27:35 of footage that "starts when you're at the Hall of Flags and ends while you're still on the roof but haven't put the crime tape up yet" (5770), ending because the battery died (5758). Bagley's own timeline — ~30 seconds on the stairs (5478), the grassy area, the crowd push, the empty holster, the Losee climb, the roof — could plausibly consume most or all of 27:35 post-shot. Whether the recording reaches back before the shot is nowhere established. Also, the "active... on my chest" testimony was elicited about the POST-shooting sequence ("the whole time that this going on", following 04:08:12-15 on the holster and the Losee building), not the pre-shot period.
F. "OVERWATCH POST" IS THE FINDING'S WORD, NOT THE RECORD'S — and it matters here. The record's word is "post" (3120). The assignment was to clear and secure a walkway because members of the public were on top of it "throwing stuff down to the tent" (4745). Calling it an "overwatch post" imports a tactical watch function the record never assigns, which in a file about security adequacy reads as a watch that failed. Lens (b) correction.
G. A REFERENTIAL AMBIGUITY WORTH STATING. At 02:43:36 (4745) Bagley uses "individuals on top of the Hall of Flags" to mean MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC. At 02:46:55 he says "one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me." The security-team reading is correct — it is fixed by the question and by the armed follow-up, and both counsel and witness proceed on it — but it rests on question-context, not on the answer's own words, and the file should say so.

CATEGORY WARNING FOR WHOEVER WRITES THE FILE: at 04:08:32-04:09:06 counsel puts to Bagley, from the body camera, "another individual who was with you that went to the Losee building who was in civilian clothing, but appeared to have a gun." Bagley: "I don't know who he was exactly. He had a BADGE on... I had somebody with me to back me up," agency unknown, handgun. A badge points to law enforcement, this is POST-shooting, and per standing rule 3 this individual must NOT be merged into the private-team category. He is an unidentified badged armed individual of unestablished agency. Do not let this passage migrate into the security-team finding.
verdicts.corrected_form:
NARROWER SUPPORTED FORM.

FINDING. On cross by Ms. Nestor, Officer Bagley affirmed that Mr. Kirk's own security team was present, and answered "yes" to whether he communicated with any of them — but the answer supplied a sighting rather than any communication, and no content, time, subject or direction of any exchange appears anywhere in his testimony. The record therefore establishes co-location and an unelaborated affirmative; it describes no coordination arrangement between UVU PD and the private team, and nobody was asked to describe one.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED — T1, High (day1.txt 02:46:45-02:47:08, four Q&A pairs across 23 seconds on cross):
- Bagley was aware Mr. Kirk had his own security team present (02:46:51).
- Asked "Did you communicate with any of those people?", he answered "I saw one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me, yes" (02:46:55). The answer both affirms and describes a sighting.
- This was before the shooting (02:46:58-02:47:00), and he further saw "several down in the crowds and down by him."
- He "was aware he was armed" as to the individual beside him (02:47:07).
- Bagley's own post was the south end of the top of the Hall of Flags, assigned to secure that area because members of the public had gathered on it and were throwing objects down toward the tent (01:02:41; 02:43:36).

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED — T1 null, properly measured, High:
That UVU PD and the private team coordinated, deconflicted sectors, or shared a radio channel. Capable patterns run over day1.txt under both U+FFFE readings: "channel" 0, "deconflict" 0, "liaison" 0; "coordinat" 4 hits all opened and all concerning post-incident inter-agency investigative coordination; "radio" 2 hits both post-shot internal police traffic. The word "communicate" appears exactly once in substantive testimony all day — in the question itself.
DELETED FROM THE PRIOR FORM: "or exchanged any information at all." The witness answered "yes." That clause is contradicted by the record it cites.

AMBIGUITY, NOT RESOLUTION — Medium:
Two readings of 02:46:55 both live and the record does not choose between them. (i) The terminal "yes" is a straightforward affirmative to "did you communicate," with "I saw" supplying detail. (ii) The answer substitutes a sighting for a communication. Reading (i) is at least as strong; the finding is not entitled to resolve to (ii). Pressing further toward (i): at 02:47:07 Bagley says he "was AWARE" the individual was armed, a knowledge verb, twenty seconds after testifying at 02:46:35 that he did not see anyone armed "other than law enforcement" — so the basis of that awareness is unstated and could as easily be verbal as visual. What is durable across both readings is only this: no content of any exchange is in the record.

REFERENT. The security-team reading of "one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags" is fixed by the question and by the armed follow-up, both counsel and witness proceeding on it. Note that at 02:43:36 the same phrasing denotes members of the public whom Bagley was dispatched to clear.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. Bagley's body-worn camera — chest-mounted and active (04:08:28), described by counsel as "27 minute and 35 second" footage that "starts when you're at the Hall of Flags" and ends on the Losee roof before crime tape, cut short by a dead battery (04:12:40-04:12:54). CAVEAT, NOT PREVIOUSLY STATED: the record does NOT establish that this footage reaches back before the shot. Bagley's own post-shot timeline (~30 seconds on the stairs, the grassy area, the crowd push, the holster, the Losee climb, the roof) could consume most or all of 27:35. Whether the artifact covers the pre-shot co-location is itself an open question — and is the first thing to check if it is ever obtained. The defence has reviewed it.

SCOPE AND LIMITS.
- ROLE ONLY. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named here and none may be. No name appears at any of the five points in day1.txt where the team is mentioned. Bagley, Ms. Nestor and Judge Graf are named as public officials acting in public roles; the security team members are private parties referred to by role.
- NOTHING HERE IMPLIES FAULT, OMISSION OR NEGLIGENCE BY ANY MEMBER OF MR. KIRK'S SECURITY TEAM, OR BY OFFICER BAGLEY. No official has alleged any. The witness answered the question put to him and volunteered detail; nothing in the record supports reading his answer as evasive, and it must not be so characterised.
- A PRELIMINARY HEARING TESTS PROBABLE CAUSE FOR THE CHARGED OFFENCES. Security adequacy is an element of none of them. The thinness of the record on inter-agency communication reflects what this proceeding was for and what counsel chose to ask in 23 seconds of cross — it is a fact about the record, not a fact about the world, and may not be read as one.
- COUNTERWEIGHT, GIVEN ITS FULL WEIGHT. The record supplies real support for an ordinary, functioning arrangement: Utah is an open-carry state (02:46:25), so an armed civilian-clothed person is not per se anomalous; the Hall of Flags post existed and was manned; six officers were assigned, all armed (02:44:36, 02:45:03-06); and Bagley described the private team deployed in depth — one on the walkway beside him, several in the crowd and near Mr. Kirk. That is an observed layered posture, not an absence of one.
- SEPARATE CATEGORY, DO NOT MERGE. The armed civilian-clothed individual who accompanied Bagley to the Losee building (04:08:32-04:09:06) wore a badge, was of agency unknown to the witness, and appears only after the shooting. He is not established to be a member of the private team and must not be recorded as one.
- NOT RE-VERIFIED: day2-day5 transcripts, the State's exhibits, and whether any other banked artifact addresses UVU PD / private-team communication. This null is scoped to day1.txt.

verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES ON SUBSTANCE, OVERSTATED IN THREE MEASURABLE WAYS. I re-parsed both transcripts myself into speaker segments (day1: 380 'David Hull' segments L6308-L10916, not 379/L6296 — L6296 is McBride calling the witness and L6308 is the oath response "I do", not testimony; day2: 376 'Agent Hull' L392-L3906, exact match) and re-ran a much wider battery over all 756 answers under both U+FFFE readings.

WHAT CONFIRMS THE FINDING (logged explicitly, per the both-directions rule):
(1) LABEL INTEGRITY HOLDS FOR HULL. I tested for the Bagley failure mode directly: I scanned all 576 counsel-labelled segments inside day1's Hull span for answer-shaped content. All 34 answer-shaped hits are counsel addressing the judge ("No, Your Honor", "It is, Judge"), not Hull's answers misattributed. Day2's Hull span alternates cleanly. So restricting to the witness label does not lose Hull's answers here. Label drift DOES exist in the file (at day1 L6304 the oath is administered under the label "Kathy Nestor", who is defence counsel, not the clerk) — it simply does not fall on Hull's answers.
(2) SCOPE IS MORE CONSERVATIVE THAN NEEDED. Hull does not testify on days 3, 4 or 5 — zero Hull speaker-labels in any of them; "Hull" appears 4x in day3 as a third-party reference, 0x in day4, day5 and faumuina_condensed. The null over day1+day2 is therefore a null over the whole of Hull's testimony at this hearing.
(3) THE ONE PRE-SHOT SECURITY-TEAM PREMISE WAS NOT ADOPTED. At day2 01:58:06 (L2828) Ms. Nestor put to him "it showed a dead-on view of Mr. Kirk and his parts of his security team. Is that right?" Hull did not assent — he answered a different question ("You're referring to the UVU video in the breezeway?" / "We have that video, yes", L2832-L2840). Moments later, asked whether the area behind the tent was visible from the Losee building, he said flatly "I can't answer that question" (L2856). This strengthens the finding.
(4) NO NAMING. Confirmed independently: `guard` returns ZERO across all 756 answers; the only two private-team references (day1 L8878, L8902) are role-only and carry no personal identifier.
(5) GOFORTH VERIFIED AND MORE SHARPLY DATED than the finding states — sworn Spanish Fork PD, and the contact was ~12:30 AM on September 11th at Campus Drive and 800 South (day2 L1469-L1509), i.e. overnight scene security, not event security on the 10th.
(6) THE SBI/ARRIVAL LOCATOR VERIFIES at day2 L2079-L2099 as quoted.

WHERE IT OVERSTATES:
(A) THE STATED BATTERY IS NOT CAPABLE OF WHAT IT CLAIMS. The stem `securit` cannot match "secure", "secured" or "securing" — the exact words Hull used. Re-run with the true stem `secur`: 9 distinct Hull answers, not 3. Six were invisible to the finding's own battery (day1 L6812 "the campus was locked down and secured"; day2 L2160 "had been contained and had been secured by the on-campus officers", L2168 "a rooftop area that had been secured, and also an area off of the side of that building that had been secured by an officer", L2264 "attempts to secure the campus itself with a perimeter of officers", L3020 "and then it was secured", L3444 "actively trying to clear, secure, and ensure that the campus was safe"). All six are post-shot, so the conclusion survives — but the method claim as written does not.
(B) THE COUNT OF FIVE IS WRONG. `guard` contributes zero, and two of the finding's five ("one of the team's vehicles", Mr. Olsen's UVU 'team') are `team` hits, not securit/guard/detail hits. The true securit/guard/detail count is three answers: day1 L8878, day2 L1469, day2 L2448.
(C) "NO ACCOUNT OF THE PRE-SHOT SECURITY POSTURE AT ALL" IS TOO ABSOLUTE. Hull gave several T1 answers bearing on the pre-shot security CONDITION of the venue that the finding's patterns could not reach: day2 01:46:00-01:46:15 (L2336/L2344/L2352) "There were other firearms that were located on the scene, yes" / "a firearm found in a backpack that was accounted for during the day" / "It was a handgun"; L2376 "I know that a trooper was interviewed, having been on scene" and L2432 "Trooper Gonzalez included in his report that there was a gun, yes" (an off-duty sworn trooper present at the event, and a holster/gun recovered in the amphitheater area); L2720 (01:55:12) his understanding that two witnesses who filmed the roof "believed it was overwatch or some kind of a police overwatch for the event"; and day1 04:35:32 (L6844) "if you imagine there's 3000 people at an event" — Hull's own T1 attendance figure, which this library currently holds only at T3 from the timeline file. None of these describes the security ARRANGEMENT, but they are not nothing.

TWO SMALLER METHOD NOTES: the finding's "in either the join or hyphen reading of U+FFFE" is true but does no work — day1.txt and day2.txt contain ZERO U+FFFE characters, so the dual reading is a no-op on these two files (I ran it anyway; both are also NUL-clean, load() did not raise). And the SBI question was COMPOUND — "Does the SBI on occasion assist other agencies with preparing for big events like this or not? Is that's not typically something you do?" — and Hull answered only the personal half ("Not something that I've ever been involved with, no"). It establishes nothing about what the SBI does. The cleaner basis, which the finding missed twenty seconds earlier at L2071-L2075, is Nestor's "you were not engaged in any way with this event prior to getting a call after the shooting? Is that correct?" — "Correct." Both remain counsel's premises assented to, not Hull's own narration.

NO PRIVATE SECURITY PERSONNEL ARE NAMED ANYWHERE ABOVE; all named individuals are sworn officers, counsel of record, or institutional officials testified about in their public roles. No contamination exclusion was needed — the mis-banked gov-uscourts file sits in the parent artifacts directory, not in prelim-hearing-transcripts/, and I opened only the transcript files.
verdicts.corrected_form:
Agent David Hull gives no account of the security ARRANGEMENT in place around Mr. Kirk before the shot — no posting, no plan, no positions, no personnel — and is not a source on it in either direction. Over all 756 of his own answers across his entire testimony (day1 L6308-L10916, n=380; day2 L392-L3906, n=376; he does not testify on days 3-5), Mr. Kirk's private security team appears exactly TWICE, both post-shot and both role-only, never named: "Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid and they conducted what would be called a hasty transport to Timpanogos Hospital" (day1 05:58:03, L8878) and "he was thrown into one of the team's vehicles" (day1 05:58:49, L8902). Every other securit-stem answer is sworn police or institutional: an officer on a scene-security detail at Campus Drive and 800 South at ~12:30 AM on September 11th (Officer Goforth, Spanish Fork PD — day2 L1469-L1509); an officer standing crime-scene security on the Losee roof that night (day2 L2448); post-shot campus lockdown, cordon and clearing (day1 L6812; day2 L2160, L2168, L2264, L3444); and UVU's surveillance/operations team. When defence counsel put a pre-shot security-team characterisation to him — "a dead-on view of Mr. Kirk and his parts of his security team" (day2 01:58:06, L2828) — he did NOT adopt it, answering a different question instead, and he declined a related sight-line question outright: "I can't answer that question" (L2856).

The record supplies the reason, from cross: asked whether he "was not engaged in any way with this event prior to getting a call after the shooting", Hull answered "Correct" (day2 01:40:24-01:40:42, L2071-L2075); asked whether the SBI assists other agencies preparing for big events, he answered only for himself — "Not something that I've ever been involved with, no" (L2083) — which establishes nothing about the SBI as an agency; and he arrived on campus "shortly after 1:30" (L2091), roughly an hour after Mr. Kirk had been removed (counsel's framing, assented to: "Approximately, yes", L2099).

EXCEPTIONS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS NULL. Hull is not silent on the pre-shot security CONDITION of the venue, only on the arrangement. verdicts.corrected_form:
FINDING (T1 · High) — Agent David Hull gave no account of the security posture in place BEFORE the shot, neither for Mr. Kirk's private security team nor for the law-enforcement staffing of the event; and the record supplies a sworn reason why. Hull is not a source on that question in either direction, and no file may rest an answer about it on his testimony.

MEASURED, re-derived from the primary transcripts 2026-08-17. Hull's testimony runs day1.txt L6308–L10916 (ts 04:22:54–07:46:25; called at L6296, 04:22:36, by Mr. McBride) and continues day2.txt L392–L3906 (00:22:50–02:24:27; direct by Mr. Sturgill, cross by Ms. Nestor). Attributable segments: 380 + 376 = 756 (the day1 figure includes one continuation block, L9622 "Correct.", that a label-header count misses).

Across all 756:
• The stems securit/guard/detail appear in THREE answers — day1 L8878, the only one touching Mr. Kirk's private team and post-shot ("Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid... a hasty transport to Timpanogos Hospital"); day2 L1469 and L2448, both sworn police and both post-shot.
• ZERO hits, each confirmed individually over both days: guard, bodyguard, escort, flank, protective detail, counter-sniper, advance team, threat assessment, magnetometer, metal detector, bag check, roof access.
• The near-stem "secur" — which "securit" cannot reach — adds SIX further answers: day1 L6812; day2 L2160, L2168, L2264, L3020, L3444. Every one is post-shot scene security. They are recorded here because the both-directions rule requires it and because they run in the CONFIRMING direction: Hull describes on-campus officers having already contained and secured the known scenes, the amphitheater cordoned off, a rooftop area and an adjacent area secured by an officer, and "a large rapid response of law enforcement who were actively trying to clear, secure, and ensure that the campus was safe."
• Hull named no member of Mr. Kirk's private security team, and this file does not either. Every reference to that team is by role.

CATEGORY DISCIPLINE — the two sworn-police "security" answers must never be merged with the private team. Day2 L1469 is Officer Goforth, Spanish Fork Police, and Hull fixes the contact at "approximately 12:30 AM" on 2025-09-11 (L1497–L1509) — roughly twelve hours after the shooting. Day2 L2448 is an officer standing security at the taped Losee roof after dark that night. Officer Goforth is a named sworn officer acting in a public role and is nameable on that basis; individual members of Mr. Kirk's private team are not, and are not named anywhere in this file. Kurtis Olsen — the "team" at day1 L9702 — is UVU's surveillance-system custodian and an 1102 declarant, an institutional witness, not private security.

WHY THE SILENCE, STATED AFFIRMATIVELY RATHER THAN LEFT AS A GAP. On cross by Ms. Nestor, Hull agreed he "was not engaged in any way with this event prior to getting a call after the shooting" — "Correct" (day2 L2071–L2075, 01:40:24–01:40:42); that the SBI assisting other agencies in preparing for big events was "Not something that I've ever been involved with, no" (L2079–L2083, 01:40:54); and that he arrived on campus "shortly after 1:30", which counsel put as "approximately an hour after Mr. Kirk had already been removed" — "Approximately, yes" (L2087–L2099, 01:41:03–01:41:13). This is the expected silence of a witness with no pre-event role, not an unexplained omission.

WHAT THIS CANNOT CARRY. It establishes nothing about whether the security arrangement was adequate or inadequate. No official has alleged fault by anyone, no one is accused of anything, and nothing here may be read as insinuation about any security team member's conduct. Nor is the absence evidence about the world: a preliminary hearing tests probable cause on the charged offences, and the adequacy of a private protective arrangement is an element of none of them, so the proceeding had no occasion to develop it through this witness. The earlier gloss "the State simply never asked and the defence never pressed him on it" is withdrawn as a characterization of counsel the record does not carry; what is established is only that no question on pre-shot posture was put to him.

WHERE THE POSTURE ACTUALLY IS ON THIS RECORD: Officer Bagley's Day 1 cross (already banked at CR-E05) and the defence's 2026-08-11 preliminary-hearing briefing (CR-E07) — not Hull.

SURVIVES ON ITS CORE, OVERSTATED IN TWO PLACES.

SPEAKER AND CAPACITY VERIFIED BY CONTENT, NOT LABEL. The Rev labels at the passage read "Agent Hull" / "Mr. Sturgill", and content independently confirms both: at day2 ts 00:21:29 the judge says "I invite Agent Hull to return to the stand to resume direct examination... Mr. Sturgill?" and at 00:22:03 "Mr. Sturgill, your witness." Hull was sworn on day1 (ts 04:22:39–04:22:48) and identified himself as "under the State Bureau of Investigations, Major Crimes Division as an investigator", lead agency. So this is a sworn State witness on DIRECT by the State — not a cross-examination premise, not counsel's characterisation assented to, not a party brief. T1 is correct. (Contrast day1, where the same corpus carries the known defect: Officer Bagley's answers are labelled "Richard Novak", and Bagley identifies his employer as Spanish Fork PD — his employer at the time of testimony, having previously been UVU PD. That is the ONLY "Spanish Fork" in day1; Goforth is not in day1 at all, and the two officers must not be conflated.)

WHAT THE PRIMARY SOURCE ACTUALLY SAYS — all quotes read on the face at day2.txt:
- L1376 "Just until the reported shot was fired at 12:23:28."
- L1424 "It's 12:24:42 on the timestamp."
- L1432 "He then crosses Campus Drive and drops down into the wooded area on the far side of Campus Drive."
- L1448 "This is the intersection of Campus Drive and 800 South. There's a vehicle attempting to turn right onto Campus Drive."
- L1472 "When that vehicle was stopped, it actually made contact with an officer who was doing security detail." / L1480 "Officer Goforth." / L1488 "Spanish Fork Police."
- L1504 "It was approximately 12:30 AM." / L1512 "On September 11th, 2025."
- L1528 "...cop intuition, but there was something about the interaction that made him make a note of the license plate... he ran the information that he had obtained from the stop... he had in fact had contact with Mr. Robinson on the morning of September 11th, 2025."
All quoted material in the finding is verbatim and in context. Nothing is fabricated.

THE AM/PM PLACEMENT IS TRIPLE-LOCKED, NOT A SINGLE AMBIGUOUS ANSWER. I tested the obvious refutation — that "approximately 12:30 AM" answers a question about HULL'S CONVERSATION with Goforth rather than the roadside contact (the question at L1500 is "And what time was that interaction?", and counsel's follow-up at L1516 compounds "you talked to Officer Goforth about that contact on the corner... during the early morning hours of the 11th"). It fails: (a) the antecedent at L1492 is expressly "this interaction at that intersection"; (b) Hull states independently, in his own narrative answer at L1528, that Goforth "had in fact had contact with Mr. Robinson on the morning of September 11th, 2025"; (c) the Nest/Ring parking Hull placed at "approximately 038 hours on the morning of the 11th" is described at day1 L10251 as "a short period after" the law-enforcement interaction. Three independent locks.

CONFIRMATIONS LOGGED FOR THE FINDING (both-directions rule): Hull's own day1 taxonomy at L9621 supplies the missing predicate — "Mr. Robinson had been on campus approximately four times throughout the day, twice before the shooting, the time of the shooting, and then after the shooting later in the evening into the early hours of the 11th." A 12:30 AM 9/11 contact falls squarely in that fourth window. That is real support, and it is why the finding is not refuted.

OVERSTATEMENT 1 — "belongs to the fourth campus visit" is the file's mapping, not testimony. Hull never labelled the intersection clip a visit, and it does not depict campus: it depicts a vehicle at a perimeter intersection (Campus Drive and 800 South) that then "pull[s] away and head[s] east on 800 South." The mapping is a good inference from L9621 plus the 12:30 AM stamp — but the finding states it as established in the headline while its "Stated limits" never flags it. That is the specific shape this project's audits keep catching: an inference travelling in a headline.

OVERSTATEMENT 2 — "the Campus Drive crossing at '12:24:42'". 12:24:42 is given (L1420–1424) while Robinson is in the top-right quadrant having jumped from the roof and moving TOWARD Campus Drive. The crossing is narrated in the NEXT answer (L1432), with no timestamp attached. The jump is at 12:24:42; the crossing is after it.

FOUR SMALLER CORRECTIONS. (i) Hull said "the REPORTED shot was fired at 12:23:28" and had said moments earlier (L1328) "Around 12:23. I think the timestamp on the video is 12:22" — so 12:23:28 is a reported time carried alongside a 12:22 video timestamp; the ~12-hour arithmetic should say so, and should note it rests on Hull's own midday anchor "It's just afternoon, about 12:15" on "September 10th, 2025" (L1296–1304). (ii) "12:38 AM" is counsel's conversion: Hull said "approximately 038 hours", glossed it himself only as "Just after midnight", and assented to "At 12:38 AM?" with "In the morning, yes." (iii) "Ring/Nest" is correctly compounded but should say why — Hull calls it "Ring doorbell footage" (day1 L10131) while the admitted Exhibit 13 1102 statement, quoted by the court at day1 L10479, says "taken from our Nest doorbell videos." (iv) The "locked down and secured" support is weaker than deployed: Hull hedged it ("Eventually MY UNDERSTANDING is...") and anchored it to the afternoon of the 10th, when crime-scene processing began (day1 ts 04:34:23) — roughly twelve hours before the Goforth contact.
