verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES on its central claim, which is stronger than the finding itself argued — but it is OVERSTATED in five specific places, and one of its supporting props does not reach the time window it is used for.

WHAT I TRIED TO BREAK, AND FAILED TO BREAK.

The obvious attack is that Hull's "approximately 12:30 AM" is a misstatement for 12:30 PM on 9/10, since the intersection clip is narrated immediately after Robinson's 12:24:42 flight into the wooded area. I ran that counter-reading hard and it fails four independent ways, all T1:
1. day2 L1504–L1520: Hull says "approximately 12:30 AM"; Sturgill asks "On the 11th?"; Hull: "On September 11th, 2025"; Sturgill re-frames "during the early morning hours of the 11th?"; Hull: "Correct." Twice locked.
2. day1 L9621 (Hull, direct by McBride): "Mr. Robinson had been on campus approximately four times throughout the day, twice before the shooting, the time of the shooting, and then after the shooting later in the evening into the early hours of the 11th."
3. day1 L10251: "We know from the UVU footage that the person we believe to be Mr. Robinson had an interaction with law enforcement. And a short period after that, the vehicle comes to that house" — the house video being "a nighttime view" at "approximately 038 hours on the morning of the 11th" (L10171), confirmed "At 12:38 AM?" / "In the morning, yes" (L10183–10187).
4. Geography, from Bagley's own campus testimony (day1 L2845): the "horseshoe" neighbourhood "comes up off of 800 South" — so the Campus Drive/800 South intersection sits at the mouth of the block where the vehicle parked eight minutes later. The 8-minute gap is coherent only on the AM reading.

I ALSO FAILED TO BREAK THE "FOURTH CAMPUS VISIT" LABEL, which I initially flagged as the finding's own construction. It is the record's own term. day1 L10095–L10115 (McBride/Hull): "you testified that there were four visits to campus that day" — "Correct, yes"; "The fourth visit, well, the fourth visit too was captured by UVU surveillance video" — "Correct." Adopted again at day2 L864–868. Logged as a confirmation.

Two further affirmative supports the finding did not cite: Exhibit 12.1 (the un-enhanced twin of 12.4) is expressly a multi-day compilation — Sturgill: "On September 10th through the 11th, 2025?" / Hull: "Correct" (day2 L467–471) — which kills the "it must be 9/10 because it comes next in the video" objection outright; and day1 L9673, Hull: the video he watched "includes the 10th and then a very small portion, I think about 0:30, of the 11th."

WHERE IT IS OVERSTATED.

(1) "the roof departure and Campus Drive crossing at '12:24:42'". At L1424 the 12:24:42 timestamp is given while Robinson is in the top-right quadrant having jumped off the roof and "moving away towards Campus Drive." The crossing is narrated in the NEXT answer (L1432, "He then crosses Campus Drive"). 12:24:42 is the jump/approach, not the crossing.

(2) The headline "not to event security" outruns the finding's own stated limits, which concede Hull never said what the detail was securing. What the arithmetic carries is narrower: a contact roughly twelve hours after the shot cannot be a contact arising from the shooting-time event-security posture. It does not establish what Goforth's 00:30 assignment was, and it does not establish that he had no role in the 09-10 event coverage — the record is silent on that, and silence is not a finding here.

(3) The two props offered for the post-incident-perimeter inference are both day-of testimony that does not reach 00:30 on 9/11. day1 L6815 ("the campus was locked down and secured") is Hull answering "Do you know if the campus was deemed safe eventually?" about the immediate aftermath, in the context of getting techs in "to start processing crime scenes." day2 L2267 ("a perimeter of officers who were monitoring or preventing people coming and going") is likewise the 9/10 crime-scene-preservation cross. Neither witness was asked whether that posture persisted twelve hours.

(4) "This dovetails with the Ring/Nest doorbell footage" runs one direction only. On cross Hull agreed the residents "told you that the driver of the vehicle was bald" (day2 L3179–3183), agreed he had not mentioned that on direct (L3187–3191), and agreed "they also tell you there were three other people in the car" (L3195–3199). The dovetail is contested at exactly the identification link it depends on. An audit trail that records only the corroboration is a bias signal.

(5) "Goforth did not testify on day1 or day2" understates a null I measured as much wider. Using artifact_search.find across all 72 banked artifacts under BOTH U+FFFE readings (join and hyphen): "Goforth" returns 16 hits / 2 files — day2.txt and its condensed twin, i.e. one source, four real lines, all inside Hull's testimony. The stem "gofort" and the loose variant "go ?-?fo(u)?rth" return the same. Zero in day1, day3, day4, day5. "partial plate", "license plate" and "security detail" are likewise zero in day1/3/4/5. Positive control "Spanish Fork" returns 16 hits / 6 files, so the battery demonstrably reaches surnames and agency names in this corpus — the null is real. The mis-banked contaminant (dc28417731) returned zero for all three of Goforth / gofort / Spanish Fork, so no per-term exclusion was needed and none was applied. The State's announced witness list (day1 L520–528) is Bagley, Hull, Davis, Faumuina — Goforth is not on it. He did not testify at any of the five evidentiary days.

(6) Minor: "Ring/Nest" is correct but unexplained, and unexplained compounds are how metadata becomes content. Hull's testimony says "Ring doorbell footage" (day1 L10131, L10163); the residents' own Rule 1102 statement, State's Exhibit 13, read aloud by Judge Graf, says "I confirmed that the above files were taken from our Nest doorbell videos and are accurate" (day1 L10479). Both brands are in the record and they conflict; say so rather than eliding it.

(7) Unresolved and worth a caveat row: at day2 L639 Hull described Exhibit 12.4 as a compilation of UVU footage "for September 11th and September 12th," which conflicts both with 12.1's stated "September 10th through the 11th" coverage and with the 9/10 content he then narrated. It does not disturb this finding — every description includes the 11th — but it should not be silently smoothed.

MY LENS, ITEM BY ITEM.

(a) Names/identifies a private security individual? NO — passes clean. Officer Goforth is a sworn Spanish Fork Police officer acting in a public role, named on the face of the record by a testifying agent, and the finding both names the category and states why. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named, described, or made identifiable anywhere in it, and no employment, residence, family, physical or vehicle detail about any such person appears. One collateral privacy hazard the drafter must hold: the corroborating locator at day1 L10135 contains the full street address of a private residence belonging to uninvolved witnesses. The finding correctly omits it; the file must keep omitting it, and should cite the doorbell testimony by line number and by "a residence in the Orem 'horseshoe' neighbourhood" only. Likewise the second registered owner named at day2 L1568 is a private individual; the finding correctly says "two registered owners" without naming her, and should stay that way.

(b) Implies fault, negligence or complicity by security personnel? NO. If anything the finding is corrective — it pulls this contact out of the event-security category where it did not belong. The record affirmatively CREDITS the officer: his note of the partial plate is the act that produced the vehicle identification (day2 L1528). Two guards must nevertheless be written in, because the raw facts invite the insinuation and the file is the natural home for it: nothing in the record establishes the officer had any basis at the time to detain the driver, and nothing establishes that anyone regards the contact as a missed opportunity. Any "he had him and let him go" framing must be refused.

(c) Absence treated as evidence about the world? Mostly handled — but see (2) and (3). The finding should also carry the standing scope line: a preliminary hearing tests probable cause for the charged offences, and neither security adequacy nor the officer's assignment is an element of any of them, so the record's silence about what the 00:30 detail was securing is an artifact of what the proceeding was for, not evidence that the detail had no purpose.

(d) Regret converted into admission? Not applicable — no expression of regret appears in this passage.

TIER AND CONFIDENCE. T1 is right. High is now better supported than the finding claimed for the temporal placement, because it rests on three independent T1 passages rather than one. But the grade must be split: High for the placement (12:30 AM, 9/11, fourth visit, post-incident) and for what Hull said; the underlying Goforth account stays Medium-high as single-source hearsay inside sworn testimony, and the identification chain it feeds is contested on cross.

TIMESTAMP DISCIPLINE. The figures 12:23:28, 12:24:42, 12:30 AM and 12:38 AM are video/clock times testified to by the witness, not Rev stream offsets. The parenthesised ts values in the locator string are Rev stream offsets, ±5 min as clock times, used as locators only. The finding's locator format is fine; keep the distinction explicit.

REV LABEL DISCIPLINE. Every Hull passage I relied on carries the label "David Hull" or "Agent Hull" and is content-consistent (an agent narrating his own investigation under direct by McBride on day1 and Sturgill on day2). Separately, I confirmed the standing hazard on day1: the campus-geography answers at L2725–L2845 carry the label "Richard Novak" but are plainly the UVU officer witness's — Grunander closes the sequence with "Thank you, Officer. You can be seated" (L2849). Content wins; that passage is Bagley's, not defence counsel Novak's. Nothing in this finding depends on a label.

RESIDUAL SCOPE — WHAT I DID NOT RE-VERIFY. I did not open day3/day4/day5 beyond pattern sweeps. I did not read CR-E04 in full — I saw only its lines 86 and 161 via grep, which already record this contact at ~12:30 AM on 9/11 consistently with the finding (note that CR-E04 line 86 names the second registered owner; that is an existing-file question outside this task, not a defect introduced here). I did not read CR-E05, CR-E07, CR-E08 or the official-timeline file, so I did not test the coordinator's items 1, 2, 4–8. I did not attempt any source outside the banked corpus, so I have not tested whether the officer's assignment is documented anywhere off-docket.
verdicts.corrected_form:
NARROWER SUPPORTED FORM

FINDING (T1 · High for the placement and for what Hull said; Medium-high for the underlying account). The vehicle contact by Officer Goforth is a POST-INCIDENT event: it occurred at approximately 12:30 AM on 2025-09-11, roughly twelve hours after the shot, and belongs to what Hull himself called the fourth of Mr. Robinson's four campus visits — not to the security posture that covered the 2025-09-10 event.

RECORD, day2 (Agent David Hull, direct by Mr. Sturgill, narrating State's Exhibit 12.4). Hull put the reported shot at "12:23:28" (L1376) and, after Robinson jumped from the Losee roof and moved toward Campus Drive, gave the timestamp "12:24:42" (L1424); the crossing of Campus Drive is narrated in the following answer (L1432) and is therefore slightly later than 12:24:42. The narration then reaches a clip of "the intersection of Campus Drive and 800 South… a vehicle attempting to turn right onto Campus Drive," which "pull[s] away and head[s] east on 800 South" (L1448, L1464). Asked why he believed it was Robinson's vehicle: "When that vehicle was stopped, it actually made contact with an officer who was doing security detail" (L1472) — "Officer Goforth" (L1480), "Spanish Fork Police" (L1488). Asked the time: "It was approximately 12:30 AM" (L1504), "On September 11th, 2025" (L1512), re-confirmed as "the early morning hours of the 11th" (L1516–1520).

THE PLACEMENT IS CORROBORATED THREE WAYS WITHIN T1, WHICH IS WHY IT CARRIES High.
- day1 L9621 (Hull, direct by Mr. McBride): Robinson was "on campus approximately four times throughout the day, twice before the shooting, the time of the shooting, and then after the shooting later in the evening into the early hours of the 11th."
- day1 L10095–L10115: "you testified that there were four visits to campus that day" — "Correct, yes"; "The fourth visit, well, the fourth visit too was captured by UVU surveillance video" — "Correct." Re-adopted at day2 L864–868.
- day1 L10251: "We know from the UVU footage that the person we believe to be Mr. Robinson had an interaction with law enforcement. And a short period after that, the vehicle comes to that house" — the doorbell video being "a nighttime view" of a vehicle parking at "approximately 038 hours on the morning of the 11th" (L10171), i.e. 12:38 AM (L10183–10187).
Two structural supports: Exhibit 12.1, the un-enhanced twin of 12.4, is expressly a multi-day compilation covering "September 10th through the 11th, 2025" (day2 L467–471), so the clip's position in the video sequence does not date it to the 10th; and the "horseshoe" neighbourhood where the vehicle parked "comes up off of 800 South" (day1 L2845), making the eight-minute gap between the perimeter intersection and the parked vehicle geographically coherent.

HEARSAY POSTURE. Hull's account of the contact itself is what Goforth told him (day2 L1524–1528): "cop intuition, but there was something about the interaction that made him make a note of the license plate," and he later "ran a partial plate" (L1536) returning two registered owners, one of them the defendant (L1568) — the second registered owner is a private individual and is not named here. Goforth did not testify. Measured null, both U+FFFE readings, all 72 banked artifacts via artifact_search.find: "Goforth" 16 hits / 2 files, which are day2.txt and its condensed twin — one source, four real lines, all inside Hull's testimony; zero in day1, day3, day4 and day5; the stem "gofort" and the variant "go ?-?fo(u)?rth" return the same; "partial plate," "license plate" and "security detail" are also zero in day1/3/4/5. Positive control "Spanish Fork" returns 16 hits / 6 files, so the battery demonstrably reaches surnames and agency names in this corpus. The mis-banked contaminant (dc28417731) returned zero for all three terms, so no per-term exclusion was needed and none was applied. The State's announced witness list was Bagley, Hull, Davis and Faumuina (day1 L520–528). His account therefore reaches the record only through Hull.

CATEGORY DISCIPLINE. Officer Goforth is a sworn Spanish Fork Police officer acting in a public role and is properly nameable on that basis. He is NOT a member of Mr. Kirk's private security team, and the two categories must not be merged anywhere in the file. He is also not one of the six officers Officer Bagley described working the event: those were UVU officers, and Bagley testified he did not know whether any agency beyond Mr. Kirk's private team and his own six covered the event, so Spanish Fork Police presence at the event is unestablished either way. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named or described in this finding, and none may be.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH.
1. What Goforth's detail was securing. Hull never said, and no one asked. A preliminary hearing tests probable cause for the charged offences; neither the officer's assignment nor security adequacy is an element of any of them, so the silence is an artifact of what the proceeding was for, not evidence that the detail had no purpose or no relation to the event response.
2. That a post-incident perimeter posture was still in place at 00:30 on 9/11. The two passages that describe such a posture — "the campus was locked down and secured" (day1 L6815) and "a perimeter of officers who were monitoring or preventing people coming and going" (day2 L2267) — are both testimony about the afternoon of the 10th, given in answer to questions about deeming the campus safe and preserving the crime scene. Neither witness was asked whether it persisted twelve hours. The post-incident reading is the natural one; it is not testimony.
3. That Officer Goforth had no role in the 09-10 event coverage earlier that day. Nothing in the record speaks to his assignment before this contact. What the arithmetic establishes is only that a contact twelve hours after the shot cannot be a contact arising from the shooting-time event-security posture.
4. Whether "when that vehicle was stopped" means a traffic stop or a vehicle halted at an intersection. Hull did not resolve it and neither should the file — though note that he later used the noun "from the stop" (L1528), which leans toward a traffic stop while remaining his characterisation of another officer's account, not that officer's own word.
5. That the vehicle entered the campus on the fourth visit. Hull's narration has it attempting to turn right onto Campus Drive and then pulling away east on 800 South; he separately and repeatedly calls the fourth presence a "visit to campus." Record both; do not synthesise a route neither witness described.

VERIFY-IN-BOTH-DIRECTIONS, LOGGED.
- Confirmation for the record's own account: the officer's note of the partial plate is the affirmative investigative act that produced the vehicle identification. The record credits him. Nothing in it establishes he had any basis at the time to detain the driver, and no official has suggested the contact was a failure. 9. LENS (b) SUBSTANTIALLY CLEAN. The finding's own limits disclaim fault, and the disclaimer is correct on the record.

CONFIRMATIONS I LOGGED RUNNING THE OTHER DIRECTION (as required — an audit trail that only weakens one side is a bias signal):
10. ✅ The finding's limit "no other official at any of the four conferences echoes, endorses or elaborates on it" HOLDS, and I can now state it as MEASURED rather than asserted. The only other official ever asked the security question is Commissioner Beau Mason at the 2025-09-11 FBI/DPS briefing — a reporter asked point-blank "what were the security arrangements in place? Was that roof being monitored?" and Mason answered: "As far as the security, I cannot speak to that. Neither the Department of Public Safety nor the Federal Bureau of Investigation was involved in the planning or security of this event, and that'll have to be a question later for other agencies." He declines and disclaims — he does not echo, endorse, or elaborate.
11. ✅ AFFIRMATIVE T2 EVIDENCE OF COVERAGE THE FINDING DOES NOT CARRY, and it cuts against any inference of an uncovered base. At the charging press conference, County Attorney Jeff Gray stated on the record that "Police reviewed surveillance from the camera covering the roof" — i.e. the rooftop WAS under camera surveillance — and that the shooting position "is adjacent to an open, publicly accessible walkway," reachable only by climbing a railing and dropping "to the roof only slightly below." Read with Bagley's "open carry state" testimony and Long's "This was an open venue. This was outside," the record's own answer to the security question is substantial and must travel with any file quoting "we didn't".

WHAT IS WRONG ❌ (each measured, not argued)
A. "~2–3 HOURS AFTER THE KILLING" IS UNSOURCED AND IS PROBABLY AN UNDERSTATEMENT BY ~2 HOURS. The transcript carries NO clock time — only Rev stream offsets and the emcee's "Good afternoon." Nothing in the library establishes when this conference began. The best in-library anchor points the other way: the first question (line 74) is "The FBI director is posting that a suspect is in custody," and kirk-shooting-official-timeline.md places Patel's "subject in custody" post at 4:21 p.m. and the release announcement at 5:59 p.m. With the shot at 12:23 p.m., that puts the conference roughly FOUR to FIVE-AND-A-HALF hours after the killing. The figure must come out of the headline.
B. "FIVE MINUTES LATER HE DESCRIBES THE ARRANGEMENT AS JOINT AND ROUTINE" IS WRONG. ( 13:48 ) → ( 15:06 ) is 78 SECONDS of stream time, with exactly two intervening Q&A exchanges. (The ±5-min Rev caveat governs conversion to clock time, not intervals within one stream, so this measurement is sound.) The error cuts against the finding's own argument: the true proximity makes the tension it identifies STRONGER, not weaker.
C. "MASON... SAID ONLY 'Potentially from a roof'" IS AN INCOMPLETE QUOTATION IN THE ONE PLACE WHERE COMPLETENESS IS LOAD-BEARING. He said (lines 142–150): "The shot came from here on campus from a location at a—" … "Potentially from a roof, yes. A longer distance shot from a roof." The origin was partly established — on campus, a longer-distance shot, probably a roof. The hedge governs, but "said only" overstates the indeterminacy the finding is trying to demonstrate.
D. "BEFORE ANY REVIEW EXISTED" IS AN UNSCOPED ABSENCE CLAIM ABOUT THE WORLD. Nothing was searched for it. What IS supportable is the scoped, measured version: "review", "after-action" and "lesson" return ZERO in this transcript while "review" returns 5 in a sibling transcript — so the pattern is capable and the null is real about THIS transcript, not about the world.
E. THE STEELMAN WAS NOT RUN, AND THE STRONGEST READING AGAINST THE FINDING IS SITTING INSIDE ITS OWN BLOCK QUOTE, UNANALYSED. Immediately after "we didn't" comes "And because of that, we had this tragic incident." That is Long asserting a CAUSAL link between the non-coverage and the death — the single strongest textual basis for reading the sentence as more than generic regret. The finding quotes it and then passes over it, resolving to "the generic aspiration was not achieved" without engaging it. Project objectivity mechanic 6 requires the opposite order.
F. THE FINDING RESOLVES AN AMBIGUITY IT SHOULD LEAVE OPEN — the precise lens-(d) risk. "You try to get your bases covered and unfortunately today we didn't" admits two readings the finding does not separate: an OUTCOME reading (the effort did not succeed in preventing this), which is nearly tautological beside "because of that, we had this tragic incident" and beside "these things, unfortunately, they happen"; and a MEASURE reading (some specific base was left uncovered). The finding's "WHAT HE PRECISELY CONCEDED" adopts the measure reading, while its own stated limits ("does NOT establish that a security failure occurred, that any measure was omitted") presuppose the outcome reading. Those two cannot both stand.
G. NO MACHINE-TRANSCRIPT ACCESS-PATH CAVEAT ON THE WORDS THEMSELVES. The finding caveats the Rev TIMESTAMPS but not the Rev TRANSCRIPTION. This is a commercial Rev rendering, not a certified transcript, and this project has not checked it against the audio or video. Match on every particular, all from day1.txt: he was UVU PD on 2025-09-10 (Grunander at ( 23:50 ): "Officer Chris Bagley. He's now with Spanish Fork Police Department. T1 — The State's charging document characterizes the APPROACH to the shooting position as open and public, while the State's own sworn witness characterizes the ROOF ITSELF as restricted and off limits behind a barrier a person could step over. Both are the State's account, and they are consistent only once the approach and the roof are kept apart.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED (T1, High):
The 10-page Information filed 2025-09-16 (sworn to by Utah County Attorney Jeffrey S. Gray; its factual narrative expressly recited as evidence "submitted" by Brian Davis of the Utah State Bureau of Investigations) states verbatim at page 5: "The suspected shooting position is adjacent to an open, publicly-accessible walkway. To access the suspected location, a person must climb over a railing and then drop to the roof only slightly below. The UVU officer climbed over the railing and down onto the roof." It further states that surveillance recorded the individual "cross the railing from the public walkway and drop onto the roof at approximately 12:15 p.m." County Attorney Gray read this near-verbatim aloud at the 2025-09-16 charging conference, at ( 10:35 ) and ( 11:19 ), with the surveillance sentence at ( 12:02 ).

WHAT MUST BE STATED ALONGSIDE IT (T1, High) — the same State, through its own witness on direct:
Officer Christopher Bagley — UVU Police Department on 2025-09-10, since moved to Spanish Fork PD — testified at day1.txt ( 01:12:45 )–( 01:13:38 ) that the outdoor stairway south of the Losee building is "open to the public" ("Is that open to the public?" — "It is"), that it leads to a red pathway between the Losee Center and the computer science building, and that separating that pathway from the roof is "a little handrail, like a little guardrail, probably about a couple feet high that somebody could jump over." Asked directly, "Is that area restricted? Is it off limits?" he answered: "Yes, it is. There's a natural barrier with the guardrail. And from there on, there's no path. It's gravel roof, so it's not paved like everything else." Asked "But someone could hop over that railway?" — "Yes." He reached the roof the same way: "When I got on top, I hopped over the guardrail" ( 01:43:12 ).

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND WAS PREVIOUSLY OVERCLAIMED:
1. NOT INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION. Bagley IS the "UVU Officer" the Information describes — matching on elevated vantage point, rifle-by-sound inference, identification of the Losee roof, transit there, climbing the railing, and the gravel impressions. The Information's roof narrative is a summary of this officer's account. Two documents, ONE OBSERVER. Downgrade from "independently corroborated" to "the same officer's account, once summarized in a State filing and once given under oath."
2. NOT A STATEMENT AGAINST INTEREST. The charged aggravator concerns great risk of death to bystanders in the bullet's path, not the hardness of the firing position; the State had no evident incentive to call the position fortified, and in fact elicited "restricted"/"off limits" from its own witness. Strike the "with every incentive to characterize the position as concealed or fortified" framing.
3. NOT AN ESTABLISHED IDENTITY. "Public stairway" (Bagley) and "open, publicly-accessible walkway" (Information) are a reasonable but unverified equivalence; all 15 "walkway" uses in day1 refer to the Hall of Flags walkway, Bagley's own post, not the Losee approach. Both cited Bagley answers are one-word assents to counsel's leading premise, not his own volunteered measurement.
4. STRIKE ENTIRELY the prior limit "no locked door was defeated and no perimeter was breached, because the record describes none there." The record describes a barrier and a restricted area; that null was never run against the testimony.

DISCREPANCY TO REGISTER — THE BARRIER HAS THREE DESCRIPTIONS IN THREE STATE DOCUMENTS: "a railing" (Information, 2025-09-16); "a short concrete wall that separates the common area from the rooftop" (PC affidavit sworn by Brian Davis, 09/12/2025); "a little handrail, like a little guardrail, probably about a couple feet high" (Bagley, sworn, day1 ( 01:13:08 )). Attendant time discrepancy: the Information places the crossing/drop at "approximately 12:15 p.m."; the affidavit places the Suspect on the stairs at ~1215 and over the short wall at ~1217, having entered the building "through a set of doors on the southeast corner."

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT BEAR ON: it establishes that reaching the firing position required stepping over a knee-to-waist-high barrier from a public approach, with no lock, no door and no staffed perimeter described anywhere in these three documents (capable patterns lock/door/barrier/perimeter/restrict/trespass/alarm/guard run against the Information, both readings: all zero except one "locked down" in a quoted text message and one "fencing" describing the crowd barrier at Mr. Kirk's canopy). It establishes NOTHING about whether leaving that position uncovered was unreasonable, nor about anyone's professional conduct. The one sworn answer on point remains Bagley's on cross ( 02:45:43 )–( 02:45:55 ): asked whether anyone ever discussed covering the Losee building or assigned it to him before the shooting — "No"; asked who was assigned it — "I don't." Whether a six-officer detail should have posted that roof is a judgment nobody in this record makes.

TRANSCRIPT CAVEATS: every Bagley answer in day1.txt carries the Rev label "Richard Novak," a defence attorney's name — CONTENT WINS. Speaker basis: the witness spells his own name under oath at ( 44:50 ), "Christopher Bagley. Last name spelling B-A-G-L-E-Y"; Grunander calls him at ( 43:27 ); Judge Graf swears him by name; Nestor opens cross at ( 02:43:01 ) addressing "Officer Bagley." Rev timestamps are stream offsets, ±5 min as clock times, and are NOT converted to times of day here. Both transcripts garble "railing" to "railway" (day1 ( 01:13:36 ); Gray transcript ( 13:41 )).

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a UVU PD event plan or post-order for 2025-09-10; the State's Exhibit 2/3 series showing the barrier's actual height and construction; testimony from the officer or surveyor who measured it; expert testimony on campus-event standards.

CONFIDENCE: High for the verbatim filing text and for Bagley's sworn characterization. Medium-high for the identification of Bagley as the Information's "UVU Officer" (content-based, six matching particulars, no contrary candidate found in day1). All persons named are public officials acting in public roles.

split.label: The affirmative Tier 1 law-enforcement posture, in the officer's own words — what the arrangement DID include, logged as squarely as what it did not.

verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES IN SUBSTANCE, OVERSTATED IN FIVE PLACES — one of which is affirmatively contradicted by the same cross-examination.

SPEAKER ATTRIBUTION — VERIFIED FROM CONTENT, NOT LABELS. Every passage the finding cites is labelled "Richard Novak" (a defence attorney of record, appearance entered at 08:27, L232). The attribution to Officer Bagley is sound on CONTENT: the labelled-"Richard Novak" speaker at 44:50 answers "state your name for the record and spell your last name" with "Christopher Bagley. Last name spelling B-A-G-L-E-Y." Corroborated by Grunander's call at 43:27 ("the state calls Officer Chris Bagley"), the judge addressing "Officer Bagley" at 43:32, and the State's witness preview at 23:50 ("Officer Chris Bagley. He's now with Spanish Fork Police Department. He was with Utah Valley University Police Department"). The label is worthless; the content is decisive. Bagley = named sworn police witness in a public role, properly named. Chief Long = named agency chief, properly named. No private-security individual is named or profiled anywhere in the finding — the standing constraint is respected.

HAZARD CLEARANCE. artifact_search.audit on day1.txt returns nul=0, U+FFFE split=0, ligature=0 — both readings of every word are therefore IDENTICAL in this file, and no false null or false hit can arise from either extraction defect here. I confirmed this by running find() (which tests both readings) on "overtime", "magnetometer", "Bagley", "body cam", "27 minute" — every count is exactly 2x the single-reading count, the signature of a defect-free file. The mis-banked contaminant (gov-uscourts-utd-165286) was not used. Rev stream offsets were never converted to clock times; the clock times in the finding ("11 o'clock", "12:23", "1:01/1:03") are the WITNESS'S OWN spoken clock times, which is correct usage.

VERIFIED VERBATIM (opened and read, not counted): 44:50/45:08/45:14/45:23/46:20/46:28/47:03/47:21 credentials — all exact, including "26 years", "about 600 hours", "Five years", "senior officer", "Utah County Sheriff's Office for 13 years... Springville City Police Department for six years... Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office for a year", "Varies. I did K-9, I did SWAT, I did motors. Senior officer, FTO officer, detectives." 47:44 desktop + "wall full of camera systems"; 48:04 maps for dispatch; 48:30 "Every day." 01:02:29 "about 11 o'clock in the morning." 01:02:41 the Hall of Flags assignment, exact. 01:37:58 "several thousand people," his OWN estimate, exact. 01:39:26 "I was informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody," exact. 01:40:24 "my chief, Chief Long, that was right next to me," exact. 02:32:47 "I have it in my notes," exact. 02:43:21 overtime shift, exact. 02:44:31 "Employ, there was 15," exact. 02:44:49 "Had an idea," exact. 02:45:06 "Glock pistols," exact. 02:45:30 no magnetometers, exact. 02:54:15 no UVU drone capability, exact. 02:54:56 "Within 30 seconds maybe," exact. Direct-exam endpoint 02:42:15 = "State will pass the witness, Judge" — correct.

DEFECT 1 — THE BODY CAMERA. REFUTED OUTRIGHT. "Recording: body camera active on his chest throughout (04:08:28)." The word "throughout" comes from COUNSEL'S PREMISE, not the witness: Ms. Nestor at 04:08:16 — "correct me if I'm wrong, but the whole time that this going on, you had an active body camera on your, I guess your collar, is that right?" The witness's own words at 04:08:28 are only "That was right. On my chest" — he corrects the LOCATION and assents to the premise. Four minutes later the SAME counsel establishes the opposite: 04:12:10 "Your body cam footage that I reviewed appears to end while you're still on the roof. Do you know why that is?" — 04:12:23 "I think the battery went dead. It was just right at that moment." 04:12:35 "Usually dock it, but no, I didn't go back. It was too chaotic running around." 04:12:40 "that 27 minute and 35 second body cam that starts when you're at the Hall of Flags and ends while you're still on the roof but haven't put the crime tape up yet, that's the only body cam you have that day?" — "Yes" (04:12:54). The recording is a SINGLE clip that DIED ON THE ROOF, before the tape went up, before he went to the PD to review video, before he secured the northeast side. This is the finding's own declared lens hazard — counsel's characterisation assented to by a witness is not the witness's measurement — committed on the witness's own recording. (CR-E05 v1.3 already grades the 27:35 figure exactly this way and records the battery death; the finding under review contradicts the library's own held position.)

DEFECT 2 — "COMMUNICATIONS, WHICH FUNCTIONED AND FUNCTIONED FAST." Half-true and one-directional. Speed is established (30 seconds, 02:54:56). ACCURACY IS AFFIRMATIVELY DISESTABLISHED by the same witness: the radio traffic reported a person in custody "[r]ight down by where Charlie Kirk was sitting by his tent" (02:55:16), i.e. in the courtyard — and Bagley later testifies at 02:33:44 "Then I realized that we probably didn't have our shooter in custody from that moment." At 02:55:08 he says "that's why I was quite surprised"; at 02:56:07 "I figured those guys saw something I didn't see... I thought that was him." Logging a fast-but-wrong transmission as an affirmative capability, in the very finding that exists to be the both-directions confirmation, is the one-directional audit trail the project rules name as a bias signal — running in the OTHER direction than usual, but the same defect.

DEFECT 3 — "BEHIND A PRE-PLACED PHYSICAL BARRIER." Three unsupported words. (a) "pre-placed": the testimony at 01:03:13 is "That was some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk" — past tense, undated; nothing establishes WHEN it was placed or that it was placed for this event. (b) "behind": he says "I was sitting right by those flower pots, plants that were by the Fugal on the south end" — he never places himself behind the barrier. (c) The identification itself is hedged BY THE WITNESS: "And there's some ... Actually, it looks like yellow crime scene tape." He is reading State's Exhibit 1, a photograph whose date and authorship were never established (CR-E05 §2.1), so whether that yellow object is a pre-shooting barrier or post-shooting crime-scene tape rests on his identification alone. And the surrounding record cuts against reading it as an effective control: at 02:43:36 he testifies that on the morning in question "there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent," which is why he was posted there at all. A barrier being breached that morning is not an affirmative posture item without that qualification.

DEFECT 4 — QUOTE RECONSTRUCTION AT 02:44:36. The finding renders it as "There was six of us that were... assigned to cover it." The actual answer is "That were assigned to cover it? There was six of us that were, there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief." The phrase "assigned to cover it" PRECEDES "There was six of us" and is the witness ECHOING COUNSEL'S QUESTION back. The ellipsis inverts word order and converts an echo of the question into part of the answer. The substance (six assigned) survives; the quotation as printed does not exist in the transcript.

DEFECT 5 — LOCATOR DRIFT ONTO COUNSEL'S LINES. Three cited timestamps resolve to Grunander's QUESTIONS, not the witness's words. "asked dispatch to get on the camera system" is cited to 02:34:17 — that timestamp is Grunander's "Were you advised of anything?"; the quoted phrase is at 02:33:44. "advised other officers that I needed the Losee building secured, searched" is cited to 02:37:09 — that is Grunander's "Where is the police department located?"; the phrase is at 02:36:46. "[e]very day" is placed inside the range 47:44–48:28 — 48:28 is Grunander's question; the answer is at 48:30. Separately, the content dispatch came back with (02:34:19) was expressly received by the magistrate NOT for the truth of the matter asserted (ruling at 02:36:05); the finding is right to claim only that an answer came back, but the limiting ruling belongs in the record.

SMALLER: "40% of the department" is PROJECT ARITHMETIC (6/15), not testimony, presented inside the "Record says" layer; and the composition of the six is ambiguous on its face — "patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief" leaves it unresolved whether Chief Long is inside or outside the six. "Staffing augmented above normal duty" is an INFERENCE (supported directionally by the overtime sign-up plus "the two officers that were on duty" at 02:43:36, but not stated by the witness). "Command present" is carried by 01:40:24, which places Chief Long beside him only AFTER the shot during scene-clearing; pre-event command presence is supported instead by 02:43:36 and 02:44:36, which the finding does not cite for it. The CCTV/maps testimony (47:44–48:30) is FOUNDATION testimony about his general UVU-era familiarity, not a description of what was deployed for this event — it becomes event-relevant only through his actual use of dispatch's cameras at 02:33:44.

CONFIRMED AGAINST THE "ONLY" CLAIM: I re-ran a CAPABLE pattern for the notes claim — \bnotes?\b and \bnotebook over Bagley's entire stint (43:27 to 04:35:00), which demonstrably matches the target term (it returns the 02:32:47 hit plus judge/Hull uses outside the stint). Exactly ONE witness use of "notes" by Bagley: 02:32:47. The "only" holds for notes. It should be qualified, though: his POLICE REPORT was physically in front of him during cross ("I do, as a matter of fact," 02:50:34) and he was walked through it from 02:49:19 onward.

NET: the composite claim — that the arrangement affirmatively included an overtime-augmented shift, six of fifteen officers, Glock-armed, an anticipated large crowd, an elevated post overlooking the tent, a chief on scene, functioning radio and dispatch, daily-used campus CCTV he had personally mapped, and a body camera — survives direct reading of the primary source. Refuting it wholesale would destroy a large body of verbatim, correctly attributed Tier 1 content. It is narrowed rather than refuted.
verdicts.corrected_form:
THE AFFIRMATIVE TIER 1 LAW-ENFORCEMENT POSTURE, IN THE OFFICER'S OWN WORDS (narrowed 2026-08-17 on direct re-reading of day1.txt).

Witness: Officer Christopher Bagley — a NAMED PUBLIC OFFICIAL testifying in a public role, properly named. His answers throughout carry the Rev label "Richard Novak," a defence attorney of record; the attribution rests on CONTENT (at 44:50 the labelled-"Novak" speaker gives his own name and spells it "B-A-G-L-E-Y"), corroborated by the State's call at 43:27, the court's address at 43:32, and the State's witness preview at 23:50. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named or characterised anywhere below.

AGENCY AND STATUS (44:50–47:21, all verbatim). UVU Police Department in September 2025, senior officer, five years there; 26 years a police officer; Utah POST Academy, "about 600 hours," certified; prior service — Utah County Sheriff's Office 13 years, Springville City PD 6 years, Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office 1 year — across which he held, without per-department attribution, "K-9... SWAT... motors. Senior officer, FTO officer, detectives." He has since moved to Spanish Fork PD (about five months as of testimony).

SHIFT. He knew of the event in advance and "signed up for an overtime shift... For the special event" (02:43:21 — the sole use of "overtime" in his testimony, capable-pattern verified), checking in "about 11 o'clock in the morning" (01:02:29). PROJECT INFERENCE, MARKED AS SUCH: read with "the two officers that were on duty" (02:43:36), this indicates staffing above normal duty strength; the witness does not say so.

STRENGTH (02:44:31–02:44:36). "Employ, there was 15" UVU officers normally. Asked how many were assigned to the event: "That were assigned to cover it? There was six of us that were, there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief." [Quoted in full because the answer OPENS by echoing counsel's question; any ellipsis that moves "assigned to cover it" after "six of us" fabricates word order.] PROJECT ARITHMETIC, NOT TESTIMONY: 6/15 = 40%, valid only if the six are drawn from the fifteen and the chief's position relative to the six is resolved — the answer leaves it ambiguous whether Chief Long is inside or outside the count.

ANTICIPATION. Counsel's compound question — "Did you all have an idea there were going to be thousands and thousands of people there or was that a surprise to you?" — answered "Had an idea" (02:44:49). His OWN independent estimate from the overwatch, unprompted by any figure in the question: "several thousand people" (01:37:58).

ARMING. "of those six officers, are you all armed? Do you carry weapons?" — "Yes" (02:45:03); "Glock pistols" (02:45:06).

POST. "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end. So we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area" (01:02:41) — an elevated position overlooking the tent. A barrier existed on that walkway, which he identified in State's Exhibit 1 as "some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk" (01:03:13). THREE QUALIFICATIONS THE EARLIER FORM OMITTED: nothing dates the barrier's placement, so "pre-placed" is unsupported; he places himself "right by those flower pots," not behind it; and he HEDGED THE IDENTIFICATION HIMSELF — "Actually, it looks like yellow crime scene tape" — on an exhibit whose date and authorship were never established (CR-E05 §2.1). Read alongside 02:43:36, the same morning had "people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent," so the barrier was being breached at the time he was posted to it. His posting is RESPONSIVE security activity, not evidence of pre-event elevated-threat planning.

COMMAND. Chief Long was engaged that morning — he received the report of people above the tent and diverted the two on-duty officers (02:43:36); the six covering the event were "patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief" (02:44:36). Separately, AFTER the shot, during scene-clearing on the courtyard grass: "my chief, Chief Long, that was right next to me" (01:40:24). The first two citations carry pre-event command presence; 01:40:24 does not.

COMMUNICATIONS — FAST, AND ON THE FIRST TRANSMISSION WRONG. Radio traffic reached him at the bottom of the stairs: "I was informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody" (01:39:26), "[w]ithin 30 seconds maybe" (02:54:56). THE SPEED IS ESTABLISHED; THE ACCURACY IS DISESTABLISHED BY THE SAME WITNESS — the person detained was "[r]ight down by where Charlie Kirk was sitting by his tent" (02:55:16), and Bagley later testifies "Then I realized that we probably didn't have our shooter in custody from that moment" (02:33:44), having said at the time "Oh, that was kind of fast" (01:39:26) and "that's why I was quite surprised" (02:55:08). What the record supports is that the radio net MOVED INFORMATION FAST, not that it moved correct information. He also used dispatch actively: "I asked dispatch to get on the camera system and to see if anybody was on top of the Losee building during the time of the incident" (02:33:44 — NOT 02:34:17, which is counsel's question), and "Dispatch came back and advised me" (02:34:19) — the CONTENT of that answer was expressly received by the magistrate NOT for the truth of the matter asserted (ruling at 02:36:05), so only the fact of a response is carried here. He directed responding units: "I advised other officers that I needed the Losee building secured, searched" (02:36:46 — NOT 02:37:09, which is counsel's question).

SURVEILLANCE. Foundation testimony as to his UVU-era familiarity, not a description of event-day deployment: campus CCTV reachable from station desktops and from a dispatch "wall full of camera systems" (47:44), used "[e]very day" (48:30 — the range end 48:28 is counsel's question), and he had personally made maps "so it was easier for dispatch... to click on an area... and get a faster response" (48:04). It becomes event-relevant through his actual use of it at 02:33:44 and his own review of the footage at the campus PD, "level three" of the Gunther Trade Building, "to verify for myself" (02:37:11–02:37:31).

RECORDING — CORRECTED, THE PRIOR FORM WAS WRONG. He wore an active body camera "On my chest" (04:08:28). THE WORD "THROUGHOUT" IS WITHDRAWN: it came from counsel's premise at 04:08:16 ("the whole time that this going on"), and the same cross establishes the opposite at 04:12:10–04:12:54 — the recording "appears to end while you're still on the roof," "I think the battery went dead," he never restarted it ("no, I didn't go back. It was too chaotic"), and it was a single clip, characterised by counsel and assented to by him as "27 minute and 35 second," starting at the Hall of Flags and ending on the roof BEFORE the crime tape went up — "that's the only body cam you have that day?" — "Yes." Per CR-E05 v1.3, the 27:35 duration is counsel's characterisation assented to, not a measurement.

NOT INCLUDED. No magnetometers (02:45:30). No UVU drone capability at all (02:54:15); the drones that later flew were Provo PD's (02:54:06).

TIER AND CONFIDENCE. T1 · HIGH as to what this named sworn witness said under oath, for every item above marked verbatim. NOT a finding that the arrangement was adequate, nor that it was inadequate; this project has independently verified no fact about UVU PD's staffing decisions, and adequacy is a normative question this record does not answer. Nothing here bears on the conduct of any individual member of Mr. Kirk's security team, and no such inference is available from it.

RESIDUAL SCOPE AND LIMITS. Every figure is one witness's recollection ten months on. Capable-pattern check (\bnotes?\b, \bnotebook over 43:27–04:35:00, method self-validated by its non-Bagley hits): he consulted "my notes" exactly ONCE, for the 1:01/1:03 roof-release time (02:32:47) — but his POLICE REPORT was in front of him during cross ("I do, as a matter of fact," 02:50:34) and he was taken through it from 02:49:19. Three of the previously cited locators pointed at counsel's questions rather than the witness's answers and are corrected above; readers should re-derive locators, not inherit them. day1.txt carries zero NUL bytes and zero U+FFFE splits (artifact_search.audit), so both readings are identical and no extraction-defect false null is possible in this file. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: UVU PD's own event documentation, the CAD/radio log, the body-camera file itself (which would settle both the 27:35 duration and the coverage window), or testimony from any of the other five officers or from Chief Long.

verdicts.reason:
REFUTED AS WRITTEN — the affirmative core is real and largely verified, but five load-bearing elements fail against day1.txt, two of them flatly. Method note: every search was run through artifact_search.find(), which tests both U+FFFE readings; day1.txt carries 0 U+FFFE and 0 NUL bytes (audited), so the two readings are byte-identical here — I checked both and say so. Searches were scoped to day1.txt alone, so the mis-banked contaminant (gov-uscourts-utd-165286) never entered the search space; no per-term exclusion was needed. Rev speaker labels were ignored: every answer attributed here to the witness carries the label "Richard Novak" (defence counsel's name) and is attributed to Officer Bagley from CONTENT — he states "Christopher Bagley. Last name spelling B-A-G-L-E-Y" (44:50) under that label, the prosecutor calls "Officer Chris Bagley" (43:27), and the judge and Ms. Nestor address him as Officer Bagley. The oath at 44:10 is labelled "Kathy Nestor" and is almost certainly the clerk — a further label defect, not relied on. Timestamps are used as stream offsets only; no conversion to clock time was made.

FAILURE 1 — FALSE, not merely overstated. "Recording: body camera active on his chest throughout (04:08:28)." The word "throughout" is contradicted by the same witness four minutes later on the same cross. At 04:12:10 Ms. Nestor: "Your body cam footage that I reviewed appears to end while you're still on the roof. Do you know why that is?" — 04:12:23: "I think the battery went dead. It was just right at that moment." 04:12:25, did he restart it — 04:12:35: "Usually dock it, but no, I didn't go back. It was too chaotic running around." 04:12:40: "that ... body cam that starts when you're at the Hall of Flags and ends while you're still on the roof but haven't put the crime tape up yet, that's the only body cam you have that day?" — 04:12:54: "Yes." The 04:08:28 answer ("That was right. On my chest.") answers a question whose "the whole time that this going on" framing is COUNSEL'S, covering the segment then under discussion, and it cannot carry "throughout the day." The camera was running at the Hall of Flags, died on the Losee roof before the crime tape went up, and was never restarted. Logging it as an affirmative posture item without the death of the battery is a one-directional log in the pro-adequacy direction — the mirror image of the bias the finding says it exists to prevent.

FAILURE 2 — an adequacy judgment the finding's own limits disclaim, and its lead exemplar cuts the other way. The heading "Communications, which functioned and functioned fast" is analyst-layer characterization, not testimony. Its first exemplar is the ~30-second radio report of a shooter in custody (01:39:26; "Within 30 seconds maybe" at 02:54:56 ✓ verified, in answer to "how long do you think between the shot being fired did you hear that?"). That report was WRONG, and the witness says so: at 02:33:44, on the Losee roof, "Then I realized that we probably didn't have our shooter in custody from that moment"; at 02:55:31 the detained person was "up on the top level"/by the tent, not at the firing position; at 02:56:07, "I figured those guys saw something I didn't see... I thought that was him." Fast traffic carrying a mistaken belief is not "functioning" communications; it is fast communications, full stop. The second exemplar (dispatch camera answer, 02:34:19) genuinely did function. The third (advising officers to secure the Losee building) is an instruction he gave; the cited passage establishes nothing about whether it was executed. The finding's Stated limits say "It is NOT a finding that the arrangement was adequate" — this heading is exactly such a finding, and it breaks the file's own rule.

FAILURE 3 — a spliced quotation, i.e. a recording-layer fidelity defect. The finding prints: "There was six of us that were… assigned to cover it" (02:44:31–02:44:36). The witness's actual words at 02:44:36 are: "That were assigned to cover it? There was six of us that were, there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief." The ellipsis reverses the order and turns his echo of counsel's question into the tail of his own sentence. He never spoke that sequence. Under the prime directive, fidelity to the claim is the recording layer's whole standard.

FAILURE 4 — reintroduces a reading this library already corrected. "Post: ... behind a pre-placed physical barrier." CR-E05 v1.1 (2026-08-01), verified against day1.txt, corrected precisely this: "the posting was a response to a disturbance already under way, not a pre-planned post." Day1.txt confirms it — at 02:43:36 Chief Long got "a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent," sent the two on-duty officers down, and Bagley followed once in uniform; at 02:48:12, "it started getting hectic, so we were trying to get down there to secure the area and push people away from the top of the tent." The barrier answer itself (01:03:13) fixes no time: "there's some ... Actually, it looks like yellow crime scene tape. That was some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk." He first calls it what looks like crime-scene tape; "pre-placed" is the finding's word, and the record does not date the placement. Nor is "behind" supported — he says only "I was sitting right by those flower pots." Re-asserting a superseded reading without a supersession row is the defect the corrections-in-place rule exists to stop.

FAILURE 5 — a mis-stated absence. "given without notes on most points (he consulted 'my notes' only for the 1:01/1:03 roof-release time, 02:32:47)." The "notes" half is right: a stem search for /\bnotes?\b/ over day1.txt returns 18 distinct hits and exactly ONE falls inside Bagley's span (02:32:47, "Oh, I have it in my notes"); the rest are Agent Hull (04:36:38, 05:42:46, 05:59:41, 06:58:52) or the judge's "I note." But the pattern cannot reach the thing actually claimed absent. He was cross-examined FROM HIS OWN CONTEMPORANEOUS POLICE REPORT, which he had in front of him: 02:48:26 he prepared a supplement; 02:50:22 "It looks like it was done the next day. Either that day or the next day, because I wanted to make sure that I had it done where everything was fresh on my mind"; 02:50:34 "I do, as a matter of fact" (has a copy in front of him); 02:51:13 he reads the 12:23 shot time off it. So the recollection was not unaided, and the limit as written understates the record's corroboration.

OVERSTATEMENTS, short of failure. (i) "staffing augmented above normal duty" is an inference, not testimony; /overtime/ returns exactly two distinct hits in day1.txt, both inside his single answer at 02:43:21, which establishes only that HE worked an overtime shift. The support for departmental augmentation sits at 02:43:36 ("the two officers that were on duty"), which the finding does not cite. (ii) "i.e. 40% of the department" is the project's arithmetic on two figures with different bases — 15 is what UVU "employ[s]... normally" (02:44:31), 6 is the event assignment "there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief" (02:44:36, which may or may not include the chief). The finding concedes in its own limits that "the 'six' figure is not clean," then computes a two-significant-figure percentage from it. (iii) Minor locator slips: "Every day" is at 48:30, outside the cited 47:44–48:28; "asked dispatch to get on the camera system" is at 02:33:44, not 02:34:17 (which is the question); "advised other officers that I needed the Losee building secured, searched" is at 02:36:46, not 02:37:09; the "Yes" to "are you all armed?" is at 02:45:03, not 02:45:06. (iv) The opening reads as though UVU is his agency; at the time of testimony he is five months into Spanish Fork PD (45:08) and identifies that as his employer (44:56). (v) His own service arithmetic does not close — 5 + 13 + 6 + 1 = 25 years plus five months against a stated "26 years" — which supports, rather than undermines, the recollection caveat.

WHAT SURVIVES INTACT, verified word-for-word against day1.txt: 26 years a police officer (45:14); Utah POST Academy, "about 600 hours" (45:23), certified (45:45); UVU PD in September 2025 (46:12) for five years (46:20) as "A senior officer there" (46:28); Utah County Sheriff's Office 13 years, Springville City PD six years, Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office one year (47:03), positions "Varies. I did K-9, I did SWAT, I did motors. Senior officer, FTO officer, detectives" (47:21 — note he does not map any assignment to a specific agency); campus CCTV from station desktops and a dispatch camera wall (47:44), his own navigation maps for dispatch (48:04), used "Every day" (48:30); knew of the event in advance and "signed up for an overtime shift, so yes. For the special event" (02:43:21); shift started "about 11 o'clock in the morning" (01:02:29); "Employ, there was 15" (02:44:31); "Had an idea" thousands would attend (02:44:49); "several thousand people" from the overwatch (01:37:58); armed, "Glock pistols" (02:45:06); the assignment quote at 01:02:41 verbatim; "my chief, Chief Long, that was right next to me" (01:40:24); PD on level three of the Gunther Trade Building where he reviewed the footage himself (02:37:11–02:37:31); notes consulted for "almost one o'clock, about 1:03, 1:01" (02:32:47); one shot heard, report timed 12:23 (02:51:13).

MY LENS, item by item.
(a) NAMING — CLEAN, and the corrected form must stay clean. The finding names no member of Mr. Kirk's private security team and carries no employment, residence, family, social-media, physical or vehicle detail about any of them. It names two people, both correctly categorised: Officer Christopher Bagley, a sworn police officer testifying in open court in his public capacity, named on the record by the prosecutor at 43:27 and by himself at 44:50 — properly named; and Chief Long, the UVU PD chief, a named agency head acting in a public role — properly named. Ms. Nestor, Mr. Grunander and Judge Graf are counsel of record and the judge — properly named. STANDING WARNING for whatever file receives this: the surrounding transcript contains material that must NOT be pulled across. At 02:46:55 the witness describes "one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags right next to me" and at 02:47:07 "I was aware he was armed" — that person is referable ONLY by role. At 04:08:32–04:09:02 an unidentified man in civilian clothes with a badge and a handgun accompanied him up; he says "I don't know who he was exactly" — no agency, no identity, and none may be supplied. And at 02:52:45–02:53:45 there is an empty concealed pistol holster left on the grass, uncollected and unfingerprinted, with no markings noticed and no owner established ("I have no idea" twice). That holster is the single most likely site of insinuation in this entire record. It must never be linked, by juxtaposition or otherwise, to Mr. Kirk's security team: the record establishes no owner, Utah is an open-carry state on the witness's own testimony (02:46:25), and at 02:55:31 the person detained was not near it.
(b) IMPLIED FAULT — no accusation against any security personnel appears, and none may be added. But the finding makes adequacy judgments in BOTH directions that the record does not license: "functioned and functioned fast" (pro-adequacy, refuted above) and a bare "NOT included" list (anti-adequacy by placement). The magnetometer and drone answers are DEFENCE-ELICITED on cross, not volunteered, and no legal or professional standard requiring either at an outdoor event on a public campus is in this record. The finding also omits, from a section whose whole purpose is both-directions logging, the record's own answer sitting eleven lines away: "It's an open carry state, so yes" (02:46:25) and "I did not see" anyone armed other than law enforcement (02:46:35). That omission is itself a one-directional log.
(c) ABSENCE-FROM-RECORD — two of the three absence claims SURVIVE, and I say which pattern reached what. "No magnetometers" survives: it is an affirmative "No" (02:45:30) to a fully specified question, and /magnetometer\w*/ returns exactly one distinct occurrence in day1.txt, so nothing elsewhere qualifies it. "No UVU drone capability at all" ALSO survives, and I expected to refute it: it does not rest on the knowledge-limited "Not that I know of" at 02:45:39 (which concerns drones flying that day) but on 02:54:10 — "Did you guys even have drone capability? Did you have a drone on campus that you used?" — "No," reinforced at 02:54:09 ("So it wasn't UVU?" — "No") and 02:54:24 ("someone would've had to bring one after the shooting onto campus because you wouldn't have had one there" — "True"). The question was compound; the answer is nonetheless a positive statement of departmental capability, not an absence inference. The third absence claim (no notes) fails, above. The GENERAL (c) risk is real and the corrected form must state it as a hard rule: this is a preliminary hearing testing probable cause for the charged offences, and security adequacy is an element of none of them, so nothing here supports an inference about what arrangements existed beyond ONE officer's knowledge. Six of his most posture-relevant answers are expressly knowledge-limited — whether any security meeting occurred at all, "I don't know" (02:44:18); whether any other agency covered the event, "I don't know" (02:47:28); who was assigned the Losee building, "I don't" (02:45:55); drones flying that day, "Not that I know of" (02:45:39); the holster's fate and whether it was fingerprinted, "I have no idea" (02:53:29, 02:53:45).
(d) REGRET-TO-ADMISSION — CLEAN. The finding converts nothing. Two nearby exchanges are the standing temptation and neither is used, nor may be: "No, apparently not" (02:51:24, on the direction of the shot being absent from his report) and "During the chaos moment, no. They said they had a person in custody. I figured those guys saw something I didn't see" (02:56:07). Both are answers to leading questions on cross about what he did not do; neither is a concession that anything was done wrongly, and the presumption of innocence and the absence of any accusation against him or anyone else govern.

COLLATERAL DEFECT FOUND IN A VERIFIED FILE, reported because it is a false null of exactly the kind the standing hazards name. CR-E05 v1.2 (2026-08-14) WITHDREW the 27-minute-35-second body-camera duration on the stated basis that "/27 minutes/, /twenty-seven/, /35 seconds/ and /minutes and 35/ all return ZERO over day1.txt" and diagnosed the figure as "a LOCATOR READ AS A MEASUREMENT." That diagnosis is wrong and the null is false. The string is in day1.txt at 04:12:40, in Ms. Nestor's own question on cross: "So that 27 minute and 35 second body cam that starts when you're at the Hall of Flags and ends while you're still on the roof but haven't put the crime tape up yet, that's the only body cam you have that day?" — answered "Yes" (02 lines later, 04:12:54). The battery could not reach it because every pattern used the PLURAL ("27 minutes", "35 seconds", "minutes and 35") and the transcript renders it singular ("27 minute and 35 second"). I re-ran the battery under both U+FFFE readings: /27 minutes/ 0, /twenty-seven/ 0, /35 seconds/ 0, /minutes and 35/ 0 — but /27 minute/ 1 and /and 35 second/ 1, both the same 04:12:40 line. A null battery cannot test what its patterns cannot reach; here the reach failure was a single letter. CR-E05 §3.5, §8 item 3, its v1.2 revision row, and QUEUE.md Q-53 need correcting. Separately and importantly, the figure's evidentiary weight is NOT restored by this: it is defence counsel's assertion inside a compound question, adopted by the witness only through an unqualified "Yes," and it should be recorded at that weight — T1 as to what counsel put and the witness accepted, not as an independently established duration.

RESIDUAL SCOPE, stated because unstated scope reads as coverage that does not exist. I read only the passages of day1.txt listed in what_i_opened plus targeted pattern searches over the whole of day1.txt. I did NOT read day2.txt, CR-E04, CR-E07, CR-E08, CR-E16, the 2026-02-02 proffer, SEC-E02, or kirk-shooting-official-timeline.md, and I did not test the finding's "the next finding" cross-reference about the six figure. I did not re-verify Bagley's testimony outside the cited spans, nor anything about Agent Hull. Nothing here bears on Mr. Robinson's guilt or innocence; the presumption of innocence is absolute and the preliminary hearing is unfinished, with 2026-09-01 remaining as argument only on a closed evidentiary record.
verdicts.corrected_form:
NARROWER SUPPORTED FORM — the affirmative Tier 1 law-enforcement posture in one officer's own sworn words, logged as a both-directions confirmation.

WHO, AND WHY HE MAY BE NAMED. Officer Christopher Bagley, a sworn police officer giving public testimony in open court in his public capacity — named on the record by the prosecutor ("the state calls Officer Chris Bagley," 43:27) and by himself under oath ("Christopher Bagley. Last name spelling B-A-G-L-E-Y," 44:50). Public officials acting in public roles are nameable; no member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named, described or made identifiable anywhere in this entry, and none may be added.

SPEAKER-ATTRIBUTION BASIS. Rev labels every one of his answers "Richard Novak," a defence attorney's name. Attribution here is from CONTENT: the witness gives his own name at 44:50 under that label, and the judge and both counsel address him as Officer Bagley. Where label and content disagree, content wins.

TIMESTAMPS. All figures below are Rev stream offsets used as locators only. No offset is converted to a clock time. Clock times that appear ("about 11 o'clock," "1:03, 1:01," "12:23") are the witness's own spoken times, not conversions.

AGENCY AND STATUS. In September 2025 he was with the Utah Valley University Police Department (46:12), where he had served five years (46:20) as "A senior officer there" (46:28), full-time (46:56), duties described as campus patrol, investigations and community-oriented policing (46:38). At the time of testimony he had been with the Spanish Fork Police Department about five months (44:56, 45:08). Twenty-six years a police officer (45:14); Utah POST Academy, "about 600 hours" (45:23), POST-certified with testing (45:45–46:04). Prior service: Utah County Sheriff's Office 13 years, Springville City Police Department six years, Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office one year (47:03). Asked what his positions were "with those departments," he answered "Varies. I did K-9, I did SWAT, I did motors. Senior officer, FTO officer, detectives" (47:21) — he did NOT map any assignment to a particular agency, and this file does not either. (Note against his own precision: 5 + 13 + 6 + 1 = 25 years plus five months, against a stated 26.)

SHIFT. He knew of the event in advance: "I did. I signed up for an overtime shift, so yes. For the special event, I signed up for the overtime shift" (02:43:21 — the only two occurrences of "overtime" in Day 1, both in this answer). His shift started "about 11 o'clock in the morning" (01:02:29). LIMIT: this establishes that HE worked overtime for the event. It does not by itself establish that departmental staffing was augmented above normal. The support for that lies at 02:43:36, where the chief "sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area" — implying an on-duty complement of two against six assigned. That is the project's inference from two answers, graded Medium, not the witness's testimony.

STRENGTH. UVU "employ, there was 15" officers normally (02:44:31). Asked how many were assigned to cover the event: "That were assigned to cover it? There was six of us that were, there was patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief" (02:44:36). Counsel and witness then settle on six including him (02:44:50–02:44:56), and counsel later refers to "your six officers, including you" (02:47:08). NO PERCENTAGE IS COMPUTED HERE. The two figures have different bases — 15 is normal total employment, six is the event assignment and may or may not count the chief — and the six figure is itself unclean on its face. Any ratio drawn from them is arithmetic, not testimony, and would be the project's own.

ANTICIPATION. "Did you all have an idea there were going to be thousands and thousands of people there or was that a surprise to you?" — "Had an idea" (02:44:49). His own estimate from the overwatch: "several thousand people," with the grass "jam packed," people standing on the cement behind, and people on the second levels by the Sorenson and Woodbury buildings (01:37:58).

ARMING. "And of those six officers, are you all armed? Do you carry weapons?" — "Yes" (02:45:03); "Glock pistols" (02:45:06).

POST. His assignment on arrival: "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end. So we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area. So I was put up on top of the Hall of Flags on the south end" (01:02:41). An elevated position on the rooftop walkway overlooking the tent, and he sat "right by those flower pots, plants that were by the Fugal on the south end" (01:03:13). Identifying State's Exhibit 1 he pointed to what "looks like yellow crime scene tape" and said "That was some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk" (01:03:13). ⚠ CORRECTION CARRIED FORWARD, NOT RE-OPENED: CR-E05 v1.1 (2026-08-01) already corrected the reading that this was a pre-planned post, and day1.txt confirms the correction. The posting was REACTIVE — Chief Long received "a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent," sent the two on-duty officers down, and Bagley joined once in uniform (02:43:36); "it started getting hectic, so we were trying to get down there to secure the area and push people away from the top of the tent" (02:48:12). The barrier is described without a placement time, and he first called it what looks like crime-scene tape; whether it was in place before the event is NOT established on this record. Nothing here evidences pre-event elevated-threat planning, and none is asserted.

COMMAND PRESENT. Moments after the shot, clearing the courtyard grass to preserve the scene: "my chief, Chief Long, that was right next to me" (01:40:24). Chief Long is a named agency head acting in a public role and is properly named.

RADIO AND DISPATCH — SPEED ONLY, NO QUALITY JUDGMENT. Reaching the bottom of the stairs he "was informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody" (01:39:26), which he put at "Within 30 seconds maybe" from the shot (02:54:56). ⚠ THE CONTENT OF THAT REPORT WAS MISTAKEN, and the witness says so: on the Losee roof, "Then I realized that we probably didn't have our shooter in custody from that moment" (02:33:44); the person detained was by the tent, not at the firing position (02:55:16–02:55:31); "I figured those guys saw something I didn't see... I thought that was him" (02:56:07). The record therefore supports SPEED and does not support a characterization that communications "functioned." Two further items stand on their own terms: he "asked dispatch to get on the camera system and to see if anybody was on top of the Losee building during the time of the incident" (02:33:44) and dispatch came back with a substantive answer — a male individual on the roof at the time of the shooting, running west/southwest, dropping prone, then running northeast (02:34:19–02:34:40); and he "advised other officers that I needed the Losee building secured, searched" (02:36:46), though whether that instruction was executed is not established in the cited passage.

SURVEILLANCE. Campus CCTV was available "at our desktop where our police station is" and on a dispatch "wall full of camera systems" (47:44); he was "Very familiar" with it (47:59), used it "Every day" (48:30), and had built navigation maps so dispatch "could... click on an area in this campuses, where the buildings were, and be able to click a little bit easier and get a faster response" (48:04). After the roof, he reviewed the footage himself at the campus police department, level three of the Gunther Trade Building south of the Losee (02:37:11–02:37:31).

BODY-WORN CAMERA — CORRECTED. He wore an active body camera on his chest, which was on (04:08:28–04:08:31). ⚠ IT DID NOT RUN THROUGHOUT. On the same cross: "Your body cam footage that I reviewed appears to end while you're still on the roof. Do you know why that is?" — "I think the battery went dead. It was just right at that moment" (04:12:23); he did not restart it — "Usually dock it, but no, I didn't go back. It was too chaotic running around" (04:12:35); and it is his only footage from that day (04:12:54). The recording therefore begins at the Hall of Flags and ends on the Losee roof before the crime tape went up. Its length is stated only in defence counsel's question — "that 27 minute and 35 second body cam" (04:12:40) — and adopted by the witness through an unqualified "Yes" to a compound question. That is its weight: counsel's figure accepted on the stand, not an independently established duration. (This corrects CR-E05 v1.2, which withdrew the figure on a false null: its patterns were plural — "27 minutes," "35 seconds," "minutes and 35" — and the transcript renders it singular.)

WHAT THE DEFENCE ELICITED ON CROSS THAT THE POSTURE DID NOT INCLUDE. Recorded as answers to defence questions, not as deficiencies, because this record establishes no standard against which they would be measured: no magnetometers in use on campus that day, "No" (02:45:30); UVU had no drone capability and no drone on campus it used, "No" (02:54:15), the drones that later flew were put up by Provo Police (02:54:06), and "someone would've had to bring one after the shooting onto campus because you wouldn't have had one there" — "True" (02:54:24). THE RECORD'S OWN COUNTERWEIGHT, IN THE SAME PASSAGE AND CARRYING EQUAL WEIGHT: asked whether a Utah campus is a gun-free zone, "It's an open carry state, so yes" (02:46:25); and he saw nobody armed that day other than law enforcement, "I did not see" (02:46:35). An event held outdoors on an open public campus in an open-carry state is the record's own answer to the magnetometer question, and it is logged here for that reason.

TIER AND CONFIDENCE. T1 · High — as to WHAT A NAMED SWORN POLICE WITNESS SAID UNDER OATH, verified word-for-word against day1.txt at the locators given. NOT a finding that the arrangement was adequate. NOT a finding that it was inadequate. This project has independently verified no fact about UVU PD's staffing or planning decisions; adequacy is a normative question and this record does not answer it. No security personnel, public or private, is accused of anything by anyone here, and nothing in this entry may be read as insinuation.

THE PRELIMINARY-HEARING LIMIT, AS A HARD RULE. This is testimony at a preliminary hearing testing probable cause for the charged offences. Security adequacy is an element of none of them. Nothing absent from this record is thereby absent from the world, and nothing here supports an inference about what arrangements existed beyond THIS ONE OFFICER'S KNOWLEDGE. His most posture-relevant answers are expressly knowledge-limited: whether any security briefing or meeting occurred at all — "I don't know" (02:44:18); whether any other agency covered the event — "I don't know," and he saw none "not until the response came in" (02:47:28–02:47:31); who was assigned the Losee building — "I don't" (02:45:55); drones flying that day — "Not that I know of" (02:45:39).

RELIABILITY. Every figure is one witness's recollection roughly ten months after the event (shooting 2025-09-10; Day 1 2026-07-06). CORRECTED LIMIT: it was not unaided. He consulted "my notes" once on the stand, for the roof handover time — "Oh, I have it in my notes. It would be when I left that area, it was almost one o'clock, about 1:03, 1:01" (02:32:47), the only "notes" reference inside his testimony out of 18 distinct occurrences in Day 1 — AND he was cross-examined from his own contemporaneous police report, which he had in front of him (02:50:34), which he prepared "that day or the next day, because I wanted to make sure that I had it done where everything was fresh on my mind" (02:50:22), and from which the 12:23 time of the shot is taken (02:51:13).

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. UVU PD's own event documentation or assignment sheet; the CAD and radio logs; the body-camera file itself and its true duration; testimony from any of the other five officers or from Chief Long; any pre-event plan or briefing material, whose existence is unknown on this record rather than disproved by it.

LOGGED DELIBERATELY AS A BOTH-DIRECTIONS CONFIRMATION — with the corrections above kept inside it, because a log that runs only toward "adequate" is as much a bias signal as one that runs only toward "inadequate."
