verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES BUT IS MATERIALLY OVERSTATED ON TWO OF ITS THREE LIMBS. Every underlying artifact says what the finding says it says; the two connective characterisations that make it a "finding" do not hold.

WHAT VERIFIED, BY DIRECT READING.
(1) The Information quotation is verbatim. Read on the document's own face: it sits under the heading "PROBABLE CAUSE STATEMENT: Brian Davis of the Utah State Bureau of Investigations... submitted the following evidence in support of the filing of this Information", sub-heading "The Shooting", and the document closes "Sworn to by: JEFFREY S. GRAY Utah County Attorney". Correction to the locator: "Hall of Flags" appears ONCE, not twice. The finding's "2 hits" is the sum of the two U+FFFE readings that find() returns — a systematic double-count that infects every count the finding states (see (2)).
(2) THE DEFENCE NULL IS REAL AND I RE-RAN IT WITH CAPABLE PATTERNS, both readings, both banked extractions. Zero: "hall of flags", "flag" (stem), "hall", "Fugal", "plaza", "overlook", "balcon", "bridge". Positive controls in the SAME battery on the SAME files, per reading: amphith 7, elevat 6, Bagley 6, above 5, walkway 4, window 4, courtyard 3, breezeway 1, glass 1, "great risk" 26, "grave risk" 15. The battery demonstrably reaches this brief's campus-geography vocabulary, so the null is capable and real. (The finding's stated controls — walkway 8, Bagley 12, securit 8, breezeway 2, window 8, glass 2 — are exactly 2x mine; halve them all.) I opened all four distinct "walkway" hits: all four are the Losee/computer-science walkway. Confirmed.
(3) Bagley's three quotations are verbatim at 01:02:41, 01:03:13 and 02:43:36. SPEAKER AND CAPACITY, inferred from content and confirmed by direct address on the record, not from the Rev label: Grunander at 01:02:02 — "Thank you, Officer... Officer Bagley, I'm going to take you back to the date of September 10th, 2025"; Nestor at 02:43:01 — "Officer Bagley, my name is Kathy Nester." He is a sworn UVU police officer testifying to his own overtime shift, his own post and his own chief — a named public official in a public role, properly nameable. His answers carry the Rev label "Richard Novak"; the brief's signature block independently confirms Richard G. Novak is one of Mr. Robinson's attorneys of record, which is the hazard itself. Direct by Chad Grunander, cross by Ms. Nester — both as the finding states.
(4) Hull's "The breezeway underneath the Hall of Flags" (day2 02:17:51) is verbatim, given to Mr. Sturgill on redirect. It is doubly sourced: day1 05:40:46, Hull to Mr. McBride — "under the Hall of Flags there is a, I'll refer to it as a breezeway... And I know there was a camera situated in that location" — asked specifically about video "from there behind where Mr. Kirk was seated at the time that he was shot". The finding's inference stands.

WHAT FAILS.
(A) "PLEADED PILLAR" IS WRONG ON THE FACE OF THE DOCUMENT. Count 1 pleads only the statutory circumstance — "(iii) the defendant knowingly created a great risk of death to another individual other than Charlie Kirk and the defendant". The Information's own closing gloss — "Count 1: Aggravated Murder pertains to Robinson's shooting and killing of Charlie Kirk in a manner that exposed others, in addition to Mr. Kirk, to a great risk of death" — does not mention the Hall of Flags. The sentence is one recital in a probable-cause narrative that lists several proximity facts in a row (team members close on his right and left and behind the canopy; the crowd on three sides; temporary metal fencing "by only a matter of feet"; the questioner directly in front; children visible). A recital in a PC statement is not a pleaded element, and "pillar" is the analyst's word, not the document's.
(B) THE STATE'S 2026 THEORY, AS THE HELD RECORD SHOWS IT, DOES NOT REST ON THE HALL OF FLAGS — so the defence's silence is probably not a gap. The defence brief quotes the State's 2026-07-28 brief directly and repeatedly: "created a great risk of death to everyone near Mr. Kirk" (StBr:14); "[a]t least two individuals were standing under the tent where Mr. Kirk was seated" (StBr:16); "a zone of danger encompasses everyone near a shooting victim" (StBr:16-17); "a few feet" as to the questioner (StBr:12). NOT ONE quoted State position invokes the Hall of Flags. The finding offered "the State's brief may not have pressed it" as a speculative steelman; the record we hold actively supports it. A reply brief that tracks its opponent's opening is not ignoring a pillar.
(C) "INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHES PEOPLE WERE GATHERED THERE" — WRONG WALKWAY AND WRONG TIME, so it is not corroboration of the Information's sentence at all. WRONG WALKWAY: Bagley expressly distinguished two at 51:19 — "An inside one and an outside one" — and at 01:00:31 identified "the red brick walkway... the Hall of Flags, the outside top of it." His post and the gathering he described were on the OUTSIDE TOP. The Information's sentence is about "an indoor walkway... with floor-to-ceiling glass windows." Two different spaces on one structure. The finding's limits note the distinction, then its headline erases it. WRONG TIME: the Information says people were in the walkway "at the time of the shooting"; Bagley's civilians are from the morning, before he put his uniform on — "that morning when I got there... Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent." I searched all five transcript days under both readings ("hall of flags": day1 49, day2 1, days 3/4/5 zero; "breezeway": day1 5, day2 4, days 3/4/5 zero) and opened every occurrence: NO witness places any civilian on either Hall of Flags walkway at 12:23 p.m. NO NUMBER: Bagley said "people" and "individuals". "In numbers" imports a quantity nobody testified to.

CONFIRMATION RUNNING THE OTHER WAY, WHICH THE FINDING DOES NOT LOG. Read whole, this passage is at least as much evidence that the security arrangement worked as that it failed, and the finding presents it only as an unengaged State-side fact. UVU police identified the gathering themselves; the chief acted on a report within minutes; two on-duty officers were dispatched to secure the area; a physical barrier went up — "it looks like yellow crime scene tape. That was some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk"; and an overtime officer was posted there for the duration. Bagley's "no briefing" answer is likewise not a bare admission of disorganisation: his stated reason is that officers were handling a live disturbance when he walked in. The one person the record places on the Hall of Flags near the shot besides Bagley is a member of Mr. Kirk's security team, standing next to him before the shooting, whom Bagley understood to be armed — lawful in an open-carry state. He is referred to by role only. Nothing in this record implies anything whatever about his conduct, and nothing here may be read to.

ACCESS-PATH CAVEAT THE FINDING OMITS. These are Rev machine transcripts of sworn testimony, not the certified record. The parties cite paginated certified transcripts we do not hold ("PH1:46-47", "PH2:29", "PH4:91-92"), so our stream offsets cannot be cross-walked to the citations the court will use on 2026-09-01.

RESIDUAL SCOPE. I did not open CR-E04, CR-E05, CR-E07, CR-E08, the kirk-shooting-official-timeline, or the dkt368 proffer; I did not re-verify CR-E05's Bagley summary. I did not obtain the State's 2026-07-28 brief — every statement about its contents above is the DEFENCE'S characterisation of it, recording layer only.

Gray — as one of a series of proximity facts: "Directly above and behind Mr. Kirk was the UVU Hall of Flags, an indoor walkway spanning several hundred feet with floor-to-ceiling glass windows which overlook the plaza where Mr. Kirk was seated. People were in the walkway at the time of the shooting." The defence's 2026-08-11 preliminary-hearing brief never mentions it: "hall of flags", "flag" (stem), "hall", "Fugal", "plaza", "overlook", "balcon" and "bridge" all return zero across both banked extractions under both U+FFFE readings, against same-run positive controls of amphith 7, elevat 6, Bagley 6, walkway 4, courtyard 3, breezeway 1, "great risk" 26 (per reading). None of the State's quoted 2026 formulations invokes the Hall of Flags. On the record held, the State's zone-of-danger theory as briefed for argument rests on proximity under and beside the tent, not on the elevated walkway. So the defence engages the underside of the structure and not its top.

SEPARATELY, AND NOT AS CORROBORATION OF THE INFORMATION'S SENTENCE: Officer Bagley, a sworn UVU officer, testified (direct by Mr. Grunander, day1 ~01:02:41) that his 11:00 a.m. assignment "was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end. (iii) NO NUMBER was ever given; "individuals" and "people" is all the testimony supplies.

verdicts.reason:
REFUTED as framed; a much narrower core survives. Seven grounds, all from direct reading.

(1) "PLEADED PILLAR" IS NOT IN THE RECORD — IT IS AN ANALYST CONSTRUCTION PRESENTED AS A RECORD FACT. "Hall of Flags" occurs ONCE in the Information, not twice (the locator's "2 hits" is the artifact_search double-reading count; both readings return the same single sentence — a counting error of exactly the kind this library's hazard-5 rule forbids). It sits inside a descriptive run of the probable-cause narrative alongside "The large crowd surrounded Mr. Kirk on three sides" and "Temporary metal fencing separated attendees from Mr. Kirk by only a matter of feet." The Information pleads the KGRD aggravator in its own terms — "knowingly created a great risk of death to another individual other than Charlie Kirk and the defendant" — and its actual risk sentence is a different one: "The bullet's trajectory passed closely to several other individuals beside Mr. Kirk, including the questioner who was standing directly in front of Mr. Kirk." The Information nowhere connects the Hall of Flags to the aggravator. Nothing makes it a "pillar."

(2) THE FINDING COMPARES THE WRONG TWO DOCUMENTS. The 2026-08-11 brief is a reply to the State's 2026 preliminary-hearing brief, which it cites seven times as "StBr" and quotes on this very point: "a zone of danger encompasses everyone near a shooting victim" (StBr:16-17); "[a]t least two individuals were standing under the tent where Mr. Kirk was seated" (StBr:16); "a few feet" (StBr:12). The brief itself enumerates what it is answering: "The State offers two interrelated theories of KGRD" — a "line of sight" theory as to the questioner, and an "everyone near" theory. Neither is a Hall of Flags theory. The State's brief is NOT held in this library. On the evidence actually held, the leading explanation of the null is that the State's own 2026 argument did not press the Hall of Flags — the finding lists this only as a steelman alternative when the seven StBr citations make it the primary reading.

(3) "THE DEFENCE BRIEF DOES NOT ENGAGE" IS FALSE AS TO THE SPACE. The brief affirmatively litigates the area behind Mr. Kirk under that structure: "there was no one under the tent on the side that Mr. Kirk was struck or behind him in the breezeway"; it recites State's Exhibit 9 — which Agent Hull identified as "The breezeway underneath the Hall of Flags" (day2 ~02:17:51) — and states "no one is immediately behind the center of the 'American Comeback' pop-up tent when the shot occurred. PH2:69." It argues the vertical geometry head-on: "the single bullet came from above"; "the bullet travelled above, not through, the crowd." And Ms. Nestor cross-examined Hull on the breezeway clip at the moment of the shot (day2 ~01:58:06–02:01:18), extracting "There's no one stood in the middle behind the tent. No." The brief also names almost no campus building — "Fugal" returns 0 hits, "Sorensen" 1 — so the missing name sits inside a general pattern of naming only what the two legal arguments require, not a targeted avoidance.

(4) THE SWORN TESTIMONY DOES NOT CORROBORATE WHAT THE INFORMATION PLEADED — WRONG PLACE AND WRONG TIME. Officer Bagley expressly testified there are two walkways: "An inside one and an outside one" (day1 ~51:19), and described the inside one as having "chairs where people sit down and relax with windows" — that is the Information's "indoor walkway... floor-to-ceiling glass windows," occupied "at the time of the shooting." Every passage the finding relies on is about the OUTSIDE top: "the red brick walkway... is going to be the Hall of Flags, the outside top of it" (~01:00:31); the gathering was "that morning when I got there," before his ~11:00 a.m. check-in and ~80 minutes before the 12:23 p.m. shot. NO witness across day1–day5 testified to anyone inside the glass walkway, and no witness placed anyone on the outside top at the time of the shot; searching day1–day5 for "indoor" and for "inside" adjacent to "hall" returns zero. The headline's "independently establishes people were gathered there" therefore mismatches both location and time against the pleaded fact it is offered to corroborate — a mismatch the finding concedes in its limits while asserting the opposite in its headline.

(5) THE CONFIRMATION RUNNING THE OTHER WAY IS NOT LOGGED (objectivity mechanic 1). The same testimony records a police response that took effect: the chief diverted "the two officers that were on duty" to the area, Bagley joined them once in uniform, and a barrier went up — "That was some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk" (~01:03:13). On the record held, the top of the Hall of Flags was secured and taped before the event. That is evidence the area was MANAGED, and it cuts against, not for, an inference that it was occupied at 12:23 p.m. A finding resting on occupancy must carry it.

(6) "IN NUMBERS THAT REQUIRED POLICE MANAGEMENT" IS NOT TESTIFIED. The record says "people" and "individuals." No count appears — I searched numerals and number-words in the passage and found none. Three officers attended. "Numbers" imports a quantity no witness gave.

(7) LENS (b) AND (c) BOTH BITE. "On cross (~02:43:36), explaining why no briefing occurred" asserts as established that no briefing occurred and supplies its cause. Bagley testified only that HE attended none, and when asked "Do you know if there was such a meeting?" answered "I don't know" (day1 ~02:44:16-18). CR-E05 §3.5 already records it in the correct form; the finding is looser than the library's own existing standard. Stating it this way converts one officer's non-attendance into an organisational security-planning failure the record does not establish — precisely the insinuation the governing constraint forbids in a file about an assassination — and it imports the security-adequacy cross into a finding whose subject is a charging document's geography. On lens (c): security adequacy is an element of no charged offence and a preliminary hearing tests probable cause, so neither the brief's silence nor the hearing's is evidence about the world; it is evidence only about the shape of the parties' 2026 arguments.

WHAT SURVIVES INTACT. The measured null is real and the method is demonstrably capable: "Hall of Flags" 0, bare "\bhall\b" 0, "flag" 0 across BOTH banked extractions under BOTH U+FFFE readings, against positive controls in the same run on the same files — "Losee" 17, "information" 17, "StBr" 7, "walkway" 4, "window" 4, "securit" 4, "breezeway" 1, "glass" 1, "above and behind" 1, "atrium" 1, "Sorensen" 1 (all counts de-duplicated for the double-reading). Every quotation the finding attributes to the Information, to Bagley on day1 and to Hull on day2 is verbatim accurate. Speaker identification is sound: Grunander addresses the witness on the record as "Officer Bagley" (day1 line 1532) and Nestor opens cross the same way (line 4718), so the Rev label "Richard Novak" is correctly overridden by content. The brief's argument body is 34 numbered pages.

LENS (a): CLEAN. The finding names only Officer Bagley, Agent Hull, Mr. Grunander and Ms. Nestor — sworn police witnesses and counsel of record, all acting in public capacities, all nameable. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named, described, or made identifiable, and no compilable personal detail appears. The corrected form preserves this and must not reach for the individual Bagley described as posted next to him. LENS (d): not engaged — no expression of regret appears anywhere in the material relied on.
verdicts.corrected_form:
The Information's Hall of Flags sentence is a single descriptive line in the probable-cause narrative, not a pleaded element of the aggravator; the defence's 2026 brief never uses the building's name, but does litigate the space beneath it — and the sworn testimony describes a different walkway at a different hour, which police secured.

RECORDING LAYER — STATE (Information, dkt of 2025-09-16, read directly). One occurrence of "Hall of Flags," inside the PROBABLE CAUSE STATEMENT: "Directly above and behind Mr. Kirk was the UVU Hall of Flags, an indoor walkway spanning several hundred feet with floor-to-ceiling glass windows which overlook the plaza where Mr. Kirk was seated. People were in the walkway at the time of the shooting." It sits in a run of scene-setting sentences (crowd on three sides; temporary metal fencing). The same document pleads the aggravator separately — "knowingly created a great risk of death to another individual other than Charlie Kirk and the defendant" — and states its risk proposition in a different sentence: "The bullet's trajectory passed closely to several other individuals beside Mr. Kirk, including the questioner who was standing directly in front of Mr. Kirk." The Information nowhere ties the Hall of Flags to the aggravator. T1, High.

MEASURED NULL — DEFENCE BRIEF, 2026-08-11. "Hall of Flags" 0, bare "hall" 0, "flag" 0 across both banked extractions under both U+FFFE readings. Positive controls, same run, same files, de-duplicated for the double-reading: Losee 17, "information" 17, "StBr" 7, walkway 4, window 4, "securit" 4, breezeway 1, glass 1, "above and behind" 1, atrium 1, Sorensen 1. The pattern is capable; the null is real. T1, High.

WHAT THE NULL DOES AND DOES NOT SUPPORT.
(a) It does NOT show the defence declined to engage a State theory. The brief is a reply to the State's 2026 preliminary-hearing brief, cited seven times as "StBr" and quoted on the point — "a zone of danger encompasses everyone near a shooting victim" (StBr:16-17); "[a]t least two individuals were standing under the tent" (StBr:16). The brief itself enumerates what it answers: "The State offers two interrelated theories of KGRD" — "line of sight" as to the questioner, and "everyone near." Neither is a Hall of Flags theory. THE STATE'S 2026 BRIEF IS NOT HELD IN THIS LIBRARY, so the best-supported reading of the null on the evidence held is that the State's own 2026 argument did not press the Hall of Flags either. Medium.
(b) It does NOT show the defence ignored the structure. The brief argues: "there was no one under the tent on the side that Mr. Kirk was struck or behind him in the breezeway"; recites State's Exhibit 9 — which Agent Hull identified as "The breezeway underneath the Hall of Flags" (day2 ~02:17:51) — as showing "no one is immediately behind the center of the... pop-up tent when the shot occurred. PH2:69"; and argues the vertical geometry directly: "the single bullet came from above," "the bullet travelled above, not through, the crowd." Ms. Nestor examined Hull on that clip at the moment of the shot (day2 ~01:58:06–02:01:18): "There's no one stood in the middle behind the tent. No." T1, High.
(c) It is a fact about the shape of the parties' 2026 arguments only. It is not evidence about who was where on 2025-09-10. Security adequacy is an element of no charged offence and a preliminary hearing tests probable cause; silence in a brief, and silence in a probable-cause record, are evidence of neither presence nor absence.

WHAT THE SWORN TESTIMONY ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES — AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Officer Bagley (UVU PD, sworn police witness testifying in a public capacity; his Rev label reads "Richard Novak," a defence attorney's name, and is overridden by content — both counsel address him on the record as "Officer Bagley," day1 lines 1532 and 4718) testified that the structure carries two walkways, "An inside one and an outside one" (~51:19), the inside one having "chairs where people sit down and relax with windows." Every passage relied on here concerns the OUTSIDE top — "the red brick walkway... the outside top of it" (~01:00:31). On direct (~01:02:41) his assignment "was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end. So we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area." On cross (~02:43:36): "that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags... The Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent. Therefore, he sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area." T1, High as to what was said.

FOUR LIMITS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THAT TESTIMONY.
1. WRONG WALKWAY. The Information pleads the INDOOR glass walkway; the testimony is about the OUTSIDE top. Bagley himself drew the distinction; neither party has resolved it and this file does not.
2. WRONG HOUR. The gathering was "that morning," before his ~11:00 a.m. check-in and roughly eighty minutes before the 12:23 p.m. shot. The Information's claim is about "the time of the shooting."
3. NO OCCUPANCY AT THE SHOT, EITHER WALKWAY. Searching day1–day5 for the indoor walkway returns nothing, and no witness placed any member of the public on the outside top at 12:23 p.m. Bagley's own account of the moment is that he "left my post, which was right there on the south end of the Hall of Flags."
4. NO NUMBER. The record says "people" and "individuals." No count appears in words or numerals. Three officers attended.

CONFIRMATION LOGGED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION (objectivity mechanic 1). The same testimony records a security response that took effect before the event: the chief diverted the two on-duty officers, Bagley joined them, and a physical barrier went up — "That was some of our barrier that we put up so people wouldn't go above that and walk" (~01:03:13). On the record held, the top of the Hall of Flags was secured and taped off in advance. This is evidence the area was managed, and it weighs against, not for, any inference that it was occupied when the shot was fired.

NO FAULT IS ALLEGED OR IMPLIED. Nothing here is a finding about the adequacy of anyone's security work. Bagley did not testify that no briefing occurred: he testified that HE attended none, and answered "I don't know" when asked whether one had taken place (~02:44:16-18). His non-attendance is not an organisational failure, and this file asserts none. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named, described or made identifiable anywhere in this entry, and none is accused of anything by anyone. Utah is an open-carry state; the event was outdoors on a public campus; responsibility was split across at least three bodies.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS. The State's 2026 preliminary-hearing brief (unheld — the single most consequential gap here): if it presses the Hall of Flags, the null becomes a defence choice rather than an artifact of what the State argued. Any testimony or exhibit fixing whether either walkway was occupied at 12:23 p.m. and where its occupants stood relative to the bullet's path. The 2026-09-01 argument transcript, the hearing's last day, argument only, on a closed evidentiary record — Mr. Robinson HAS NOT BEEN BOUND OVER and the presumption of innocence is absolute.

METHOD NOTES. Rev offsets are stream positions, ±5 minutes as clock times, and are not converted to times of day. All searches ran through artifact_search.find(), which tests both the joined and hyphenated readings of the U+FFFE line-break defect; every count above is stated de-duplicated for that doubling. The mis-banked federal artifact 2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286-1-4-1 was not implicated: none of the terms searched here were run against it, and no count above draws on it.

RESIDUAL SCOPE. Not re-verified: CR-E04, CR-E07, CR-E08, the official-timeline file, and the Faumuina/day3–day5 testimony except for the targeted Hall-of-Flags and indoor-walkway sweeps reported above. The State's 2026 brief was not read because it is not held. State's Exhibits 1, 7, 8 and 9 were not viewed; all statements about their content are what witnesses and counsel said about them.

TIER: T1 for the document and transcript quotations; the reading of the null in (a) is Medium and turns on an unheld document. CONFIDENCE: High that the Information contains one descriptive Hall of Flags sentence and that the defence brief contains none; High that the brief litigates the breezeway and the overhead geometry; High that no witness placed anyone on either walkway at the time of the shot; Medium on why the brief is silent.

split.label: Agent Hull affirmatively placed a person behind the tent and expressly disclaimed knowledge of anyone out of frame — the defence brief's narrow citation is faithful, but its concluding sentence overstates that testimony

verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES on its core, with one link corrected and a significant completeness gap that cuts the finding's own way.

WHAT I CONFIRMED AT THE PRIMARY SOURCE. Every quotation in the finding is verbatim accurate at day2.txt lines 2846–2958 (Rev offsets ~01:58:51–02:01:21) and in the brief at lines 574–580 and 908–913. Hull did affirmatively place a person behind the tent ("Yes. There's a videographer who stood behind the tent"; and to Nestor's attempt to relocate him, "To the right?" — "Yes, behind the tent"), did expressly disclaim out-of-frame knowledge ("I can only see as far as the video allows me to. So I can't speak to whether there's anybody out of frame who could have been behind the tent"), and only then, to the re-narrowed centre-scoped question, said "There's no one stood in the middle behind the tent. No."

SPEAKER VERIFIED FROM CONTENT, NOT LABELS. (1) Day1 line 6298 "The state calls David Hull"; 6346 "David Hull, H-U-L-L"; 6362 "I'm employed by the Department of Public Safety"; 6434 State Bureau of Investigation, Major Crimes; day1 427–439 names him one of two case agents exempted from the exclusionary rule. He is therefore a NAMED PUBLIC OFFICIAL in a public role (sworn state police case agent) — nameable under the task's own category rule. (2) Day2 line 378, the Judge: "I invite Agent Hull to return to the stand to resume direct examination. And Agent Hull, you are still under oath." (3) The examining counsel is fixed by the Judge himself, who addresses her as "Ms. Nester" at lines 2870 and 2894 — 40 seconds to two minutes before the disputed answers — and again by Mr. Sturgill at line 3591, "that Ms. Nester pulled up on the screen." Two independent content anchors, no reliance on the Rev labeller. (4) The passage sits inside cross: the Judge at line 2013 breaks to "resume with cross-examination of Agent Holt" (Rev garble of Hull), and line 3422 marks "Redirect by the State." I confirmed the day2 label census is unreliable in the stated way (labels: "Michael Burt" 455, "Ms. Bakker" 407, "Agent Hull" 376, "Richard Novak" 19, "Kathryn Nester" 3), and I observed the day1 hazard directly — Officer Bagley's answers about the campus photograph carry the label "Richard Novak" at ~01:06. Rev timestamps used only as locators; none converted to a clock time.

EXHIBIT ATTRIBUTION VERIFIED. The brief's assignment of this exchange to State's Exhibit 9 is correct and independently confirmed twice: Sturgill on redirect, "I believe it was Exhibit 9, State's Exhibit 9, that Ms. Nester pulled up" (line 3591), and Hull on day1 direct identifying Exhibit 9 as "the area underneath the Hall of Flags that I refer to as the breezeway" (line 8744).

THE FINDING IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE OMISSION STRENGTHENS IT. The finding stopped at 02:01:21 and never read the State's redirect eighteen minutes later. At day2 lines 3711–3723 Mr. Sturgill asked, of the same tunnel view, "Leading up to the shot, what's going on behind that banner?" Hull answered: "There are representatives, I believe, of TP USA... There are law enforcement representatives... people are moving to and fro behind that area. A couple of individuals are retrieving items from a vehicle, but there's consistent movement behind and in that area." Sturgill: "Okay. Directly behind the banner?" Hull: "Correct." Hull had also said on day1 direct (~05:49:43) that the same video "shows some movement behind the stage area." So the record is not one videographer — it is Hull describing consistent movement of multiple people, including law enforcement, directly behind the banner. I checked: "moving to and fro" and "consistent movement" appear in NO .md file in this repository, so this is unbanked.

TEMPORAL SCOPE — THE DISCIPLINE THAT SAVES THE DEFENCE. The redirect is scoped "leading up to the shot"; the cross answer is scoped to the instant shown in the short clip. Those are reconcilable and must not be blended. What they jointly defeat is the brief's CONCLUSION sentence, whose second clause carries no centre-limitation and no moment-limitation: the word "directly" appears in quotation marks in the first proposition only (quoting Ly), and does not reach "or behind him in the breezeway."

WHERE THE FINDING OVERSTATES. Its "this matters because it is the exact allegation in the State's Information" is wrong as a fit. I verified the Information under both U+FFFE readings: "Mr. Kirk's team members were very close to him on his right and left, as well as some behind his canopy." The State alleges TEAM MEMBERS behind the canopy. Hull established a videographer and, on redirect, TPUSA and law-enforcement representatives — none established as security-team members. Hull's testimony therefore does not confirm the State's allegation; it defeats the defence's absolute negative. Two different things.

STEELMAN SOURCE CORRECTED. The "struck on the left" premise is real but is not sworn preliminary-hearing testimony. Capable pattern \bneck\b returned 3 hits in day1 (all "gunshot wound to the neck," no side) and 0 in days 2–5. The left side comes from the 2025-09-16 probable-cause affidavit ("Blood was seen coming out of the left side of his neck as he fell over to his left") and from the brief asserting it at PH4:91-92/StEx 11. Steelman (a) survives with that corrected provenance.

CONFIRMATIONS LOGGED FOR THE DEFENCE (both directions). Hull's "I can't answer that question" was refused to Nestor's own leading proposition, denying both sides the inference — the finding is right. Hull independently corroborated the defence's opacity point from both directions ("You would not be able to see through it... from the audience side"; tunnel side "You cannot"; cannot see Mr. Kirk through it) — the brief's PH2:84-85 citation is faithful. The videographer was on the right; the wound was on the left; the brief's side-specific first clause is untouched. And Hull confirmed on day1 direct that Mr. Kirk sat "approximately dead center" three to five feet from that banner, which is the premise the brief's narrow claim needs.

REFINEMENT TO "FAITHFUL." The brief's narrow sentence is faithful to the proposition Hull affirmed, but it says "Confirmed in testimony from Agent Hull" while dropping the out-of-frame limitation Hull attached in the same breath — and the conclusion then trades on the absence of that limitation.

PRIVACY. I named only public officials in public roles: Agent David Hull (Utah DPS/SBI, sworn case agent), Officer Bagley (sworn police witness), counsel of record, the judge. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named or described. HAZARD FLAGGED: this corpus contains a name at day1 line 8271 for "the videographer for TPUSA," but the record does NOT establish that the person Hull saw behind the tent was that individual. Resolving the role to that name would be precisely the prohibited label-to-person leap; the file must say "a videographer" and stop. Nothing here implies misconduct by anyone — this is a placement question bearing on the KGRD aggravator, not a conduct question.

SEARCH HYGIENE. All corpus searches ran through artifact_search.find() under BOTH the join and hyphen readings of U+FFFE, and I say so. The mis-banked contaminant 2026-07-06_gov-uscourts-utd-165286-1-4-1_dc28417731.txt was excluded per term for "neck", "left side", "right side", "gunshot wound", "canopy" and "behind his"; it returned no hits on any of those terms, so the exclusion cost nothing.

RESIDUAL SCOPE, UNCHANGED. This library holds only the Rev machine transcript and cannot check the brief's page pinpoints PH2:68/69/84-85 — though the offsets are consistent with them at roughly one page per minute. State's Exhibit 9 itself is not published. The videographer's exact position relative to the breezeway mouth is not fixed on this record, so steelman (c) survives in part.
verdicts.corrected_form:
FINDING (corrected, narrowed, and completed): The defence brief's narrow citation to Agent Hull is faithful but strips his caveat; its KGRD conclusion is contradicted by Hull's own testimony on the State's redirect.

TIER: T1 (sworn preliminary-hearing testimony; brief and Information as primary filings). CONFIDENCE: High for the testimony content and the brief's text; Medium-high that the conclusion's second clause is unsupported, because its intended scope is a reading of counsel's language.

1. WHAT THE BRIEF SAYS. Narrow (brief lines 575–577): "Confirmed in testimony from Agent Hull, no one is immediately behind the center of the 'American Comeback' pop-up tent when the shot occurred. PH2:69." Broad, in the KGRD conclusion (lines 911–913): "There was no one 'directly' next to Mr. Kirk when he was shot, and there was no one under the tent on the side that Mr. Kirk was struck or behind him in the breezeway."

2. WHAT HULL SAID ON CROSS (day2 ~02:00:21–02:01:21, examining counsel identified from content as Ms. Nestor by the Judge's own address at 01:59:18 and 01:59:42 and by Mr. Sturgill at 02:17:41). Asked whether anyone stood behind the banner dead centre, Hull said: "So there's a videographer on the right side of the tent and then I can only see as far as the video allows me to. So I can't speak to whether there's anybody out of frame who could have been behind the tent." Asked "is there anyone directly behind the middle of the tent?" — "Yes. There's a videographer who stood behind the tent." Asked "To the right?" — "Yes, behind the tent." Only to the re-narrowed "directly in the middle of the tent, is there anyone standing?" did he say "There's no one stood in the middle behind the tent. No."

3. WHAT HULL SAID ON THE STATE'S REDIRECT — the strongest evidence, and it is unbanked in this library (day2 ~02:19:52–02:20:15, Mr. Sturgill examining). Asked of the same tunnel view, "Leading up to the shot, what's going on behind that banner?": "There are representatives, I believe, of TP USA... There are law enforcement representatives. I don't know if there's any student body. But essentially, people are moving to and fro behind that area. A couple of individuals are retrieving items from a vehicle, but there's consistent movement behind and in that area." Sturgill: "Okay. Directly behind the banner?" Hull: "Correct." Hull had said the same in substance on day1 direct (~05:49:43): the video "shows some movement behind the stage area."

4. RESOLUTION. (a) The brief's narrow sentence is faithful to the proposition Hull affirmed, but it labels it "Confirmed" while omitting the express limitation Hull attached in the same answer — that he could not speak to anyone out of frame. (b) The conclusion's second clause — "no one... behind him in the breezeway" — is not supported. It carries neither the centre-scoping nor the instantaneous scoping that Hull's confirmation depended on; the word "directly" is quoted from Ly and attaches only to the first proposition. On Hull's own testimony a videographer stood behind the tent at the reviewed moment, and multiple people including law enforcement moved directly behind the banner in the period leading up to the shot. (c) The brief's first clause — "no one under the tent on the side that Mr. Kirk was struck" — is untouched: the videographer was to the right, and the wound was on the left.

5. SCOPE DISCIPLINE, MANDATORY. "Leading up to the shot" (redirect) and "at the moment shown in the clip" (cross) are different scopes and are fully reconcilable. Consistent movement before the shot; no one standing in the middle behind the tent at the instant reviewed. Neither answer may be quoted as if it answered the other question.

6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH — correcting the earlier draft. It does NOT match the State's Information allegation. The Information alleges that "Mr. Kirk's team members were very close to him on his right and left, as well as some behind his canopy" (verified under both U+FFFE readings). Hull placed a videographer, TPUSA representatives and law-enforcement representatives behind the banner — none established on this record as members of Mr. Kirk's security team. Hull's testimony therefore does not corroborate the State's pleaded allegation; it defeats the defence's absolute negative. Those are distinct propositions and the file must not merge them. It also does not establish that any of these people was in danger; no witness said so and this file does not infer it.

7. IDENTITY HAZARD — DO NOT RESOLVE. The role stated on the record is "a videographer." This corpus elsewhere names a videographer for TPUSA, but no testimony identifies the person behind the tent as that individual. Refer to role only. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named or described anywhere in this item, and nothing here imputes misconduct to any person.

8. CONFIRMATIONS RUNNING TOWARD THE DEFENCE, LOGGED. Hull's "I can't answer that question" was refused to the defence's own leading proposition that the area behind the tent was invisible from the Losee roof — the refusal denies both sides the inference, and the brief reports it accurately. Hull independently corroborated the opacity of the tent's rear banner from both directions ("You would not be able to see through it... from the audience side"; tunnel side "You cannot"; and Mr. Kirk not visible through it), so the brief's PH2:84-85 citation is faithful. Hull confirmed on day1 direct that Mr. Kirk sat "approximately dead center," three to five feet from that banner.

9. SOURCE CORRECTION ON THE STRUCK SIDE. The left-side wound is T1 from the 2025-09-16 probable-cause affidavit ("Blood was seen coming out of the left side of his neck as he fell over to his left"), and is asserted by the brief citing PH4:91-92/StEx 11. It is NOT stated in the preliminary-hearing transcripts held here: capable pattern \bneck\b returns 3 hits in day1 (all "gunshot wound to the neck," unsided) and 0 in days 2–5, under both U+FFFE readings.

10. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. The certified PH2 transcript pages 68–70 and 84–85 (this project holds only the Rev machine transcript and cannot verify the brief's page pinpoints, though the stream offsets are consistent with them at roughly one page per minute). State's Exhibit 9 itself, which is not published, and which alone could fix whether the videographer stood inside the breezeway or in the open ground immediately behind the tent — the ambiguity on which the defence's best reading of "in the breezeway" still rests.

verdicts.corrected_form:
**CORRECTED FINDING (T1, High for the quoted testimony; the framing is re-scoped and the evidence base widened).**

**Headline.** On the closed evidentiary record of the unfinished preliminary hearing (argument set 2026-09-01; no court finding has issued; posture as of 2026-08-17), Agent David Hull gave three scoped answers about the area behind the "American Comeback" pop-up tent, and the defence brief's narrow citation reports one of them faithfully while omitting the other two — including Hull's own redirect, which the library had not previously read.

**A. What Hull actually said — four passages, all opened directly.**

1. **Direct, day1 ~05:49:43** (State's examiner; see label caveat below), describing State's Exhibit 9 — the Hall of Flags / breezeway surveillance video: *"It's a view kind of looking what would be east under the breezeway towards the back of the stage where Mr. Kirk was situated. **It shows some movement behind the stage area** and I believe through the gaps you can see some of the crowd in the amphitheater."*
2. **Cross, day2 ~02:00:21–02:00:45** (Ms. Nestor, defence): *"You'd have to show me it again. I wasn't specifically looking for that."* … *"So there's a videographer on the right side of the tent and then I can only see as far as the video allows me to. **So I can't speak to whether there's anybody out of frame who could have been behind the tent.**"*
3. **Cross, day2 ~02:01:06–02:01:21.** Q: *"is there anyone directly behind the middle of the tent?"* A: *"**Yes. There's a videographer who stood behind the tent.**"* Q: *"To the right?"* A: *"Yes, behind the tent."* Only to the re-narrowed question *"directly in the middle of the tent, is there anyone standing?"* did he answer: *"**There's no one stood in the middle behind the tent. No.**"*
4. **Redirect, day2 ~02:19:39–02:20:15** (Mr. Sturgill, State) — **not previously in the library; CR-E04 v1.1 §1 records "any redirect… unread."** Q: *"Leading up to the shot, what's going on behind that banner?"* A: *"**There are representatives, I believe, of TP USA… There are law enforcement representatives.** I don't know if there's any student body. But essentially, **people are moving to and fro behind that area.** A couple of individuals are retrieving items from a vehicle, but **there's consistent movement behind and in that area.**"* Q: *"Directly behind the banner?"* A: *"**Correct.**"*

**B. Location identity is settled on the record, against the earlier steelman.** Hull agreed the banner *"forms the back portion of the pop-up tent"*, that the tunnel view is *"from behind"* Mr. Kirk *"on the other side of what appears to be a banner"*, and that on the other side of that banner *"is the tent and then the rest of the courtyard"* (day2 ~02:17:51–02:18:24). **"Behind the tent" and "in the breezeway" are the same place on this record** — the speculation that they might be different locations is refuted by the primary source.

**C. What the brief says, verified verbatim.**
- Narrow statement, brief lines 576–578 — *"Confirmed in testimony from Agent Hull, no one is immediately behind the center of the 'American Comeback' pop-up tent when the shot occurred. PH2:69."* **Faithful.** Matches Hull at ~02:01:18. **Logged as a confirmation for the defence.**
- *"Agent Hull testified that he 'can't answer' what would have been visible to the shooter on the Losee Center roof. PH2:68."* **Faithful** — verified at ~01:58:59. But the question he refused was the *defence's* proposition (*"this area behind the tent would not have been visible to anybody that was on the Losee building. Is that fair?"*). **The refusal denies both sides the inference.** *(Confirmation logged in both directions.)*
- *"You would not be able to see through it"* (PH2:84-85) — **faithful**, verified at day2 ~02:19:02. **Logged as a confirmation for the defence.**
- Conclusion, brief lines 912–914 — *"there was no one under the tent on the side that Mr. Kirk was struck or behind him in the breezeway."* **This sentence carries no citation** and sits in the legal-argument section distinguishing Pennsylvania authority. **It is therefore not characterised here as a misreport of Hull's testimony.** The accurate statement is narrower and is about *scope*: the sentence is true only if read as confined to (i) the exact instant of the shot and (ii) the exact centre line behind the tent. Read more broadly, it is **contradicted by the State's own witness on redirect** (A.4) and unsupported by Hull's cross (A.2–A.3). **The defence's struck-side clause is untouched** — the person Hull placed was on the **right**, and the brief (lines 565, and citing PH4:91-92 / StEx 11) places the wound on the **left side of the neck**; *this project has not independently verified the wound side against the transcript — it is recorded here as the defence's own assertion.*

**D. The register point, corrected.** The State's Information alleges: *"**Mr. Kirk's team members** were very close to him on his right and left, **as well as some behind his canopy** and others at various close locations near him."* The subject of "some" is **Mr. Kirk's team members**. Hull's videographer is **not** established as a team member — no witness said so and this file does not infer it. **The videographer therefore does not corroborate the Information's canopy allegation.** What bears on it, if anything, is Hull's redirect reference to *"representatives, I believe, of TP USA"* directly behind the banner — and even that is hedged by the witness, is scoped to "leading up to the shot," and is **not** testimony about Mr. Kirk's private security team, which Hull never mentioned in these passages.

**E. Category discipline (mandatory).** Every person referred to above is by **role only**. The individual Hull described behind the tent is **"a videographer"** — the record does not identify him, and **this file does not link him to any named individual or vendor**, including the TPUSA videographer already named in the participant roster at CR-E05. No witness made that link; the vantage points differ; and making it would both assert an unverified identification and identify a private individual whose identity bears on no public question here. The "couple of individuals… retrieving items from a vehicle" are likewise role-only and are **not** characterised as security personnel. **Nothing above implies fault, negligence or complicity by any security personnel** — Hull's *"I wasn't specifically looking for that"* is a candid statement of what he had reviewed for, not a lapse, and no official has alleged otherwise.

**F. verdicts.corrected_form:
FINDING (corrected): One day after the shooting, Utah's DPS commissioner placed his own department outside the event's planning and security — and pointed the question elsewhere. The record shows "elsewhere" had already answered it.

RECORDING LAYER — what was said. At the 2025-09-11 morning press conference, a speaker identified from CONTENT by self-identification ("Good morning. I'm Beau Mason, commissioner for the Utah Department of Public Safety," ( 00:37 )) was asked by James Matthews of Sky News ( 08:31 ): "can I ask what were the security arrangements in place? Was that roof being monitored? It's a question many people will have." Mason addressed the suspect, then ( 09:03 ): "As far as the security, I cannot speak to that. Neither the Department of Public Safety nor the Federal Bureau of Investigation was involved in the planning or security of this event, and that'll have to be a question later for other agencies." FBI SAC Robert Bohls (self-identified, ( 06:05 )) did not address the security arrangements at that conference. [T2 · High]

ANALYST LAYER — what the record establishes.

1. DPS's non-involvement in planning/security is established as the assertion of the official best placed to make it, at T2/High. The FBI half is NOT equally established: it is a state commissioner's characterization of a federal agency's role, which the FBI's own SAC — standing at the same podium — did not repeat or confirm. [FBI half: T2 · Medium]

2. THE QUESTION WAS NOT LEFT UNANSWERED. Mason's deferral to "other agencies" had already been discharged. On 2025-09-10, UVU Police Chief Jeff Long (self-identified) answered the security question on the record: "This was an open venue. This was outside. We did have six officers working that event," with "probably over 3,000 people" present, plus "some plainclothes police officers that were in the crowd as well"; and, asked who set the protocol, "So we work together... And I was coordinating with his lead security guy." [T2 · High] The six-officer figure is corroborated under oath: day1.txt 02:44:36 — "There was six of us... patrol one and then five others that were there with the chief." [T1 · High] Note the six may not be the full UVU complement, since the plainclothes officers are described "as well."

3. THE ROOF SPECIFICALLY. No official has stated whether the roof was under real-time human observation, and that narrow gap is real. But the record is not silent on roof coverage. At the 2025-09-16 charging announcement, Utah County Attorney Jeff Gray stated that "Police reviewed surveillance from the camera covering the roof, and discovered that it recorded an individual dressed in dark clothing cross the railing from the public walkway and drop onto the roof at approximately 12:15 PM," and that "At the moment of the shot, a UVU police officer was watching the crowd from an elevated vantage point." [T2 · High; the elevated-vantage element is already held at CR-E08] So: a fixed camera covered the shooter's roof and captured the entry, and an officer occupied an elevated observation post. What is NOT established is live human monitoring of that roof. State the gap at that width and no wider.

4. ENTITIES WITH A STATED ROLE — not a "responsibility map," and not closed. Four entities have a stated role from named officials: Turning Point USA organized the event (Gray, 09-16: "Turning Point USA, a nonprofit organization founded in 2012 by Charlie Kirk organized a public outdoor event to be held at noon on September 10th, 2025 at UVU"); UVU was the venue (same sentence); UVU PD supplied six officers plus plainclothes (Long, 09-10; corroborated under oath); and Mr. Kirk's private security team traveled with him (Long, 09-10; Bagley under oath, day1.txt 02:46:51). THE SET IS NOT CLOSED. Ms. Nestor expressly put "Provo police or Orem police or anyone that you knew of or federal agencies" to Officer Bagley, who answered "I don't know" (day1.txt 02:47:28). Mason's disclaimer removes two agencies from the planning side; it does not enumerate the remainder. [Composite: Medium] Long's testimony further shows UVU PD and the private team were jointly coordinating, not operating as separable silos — so no entity here can be isolated as the holder of a discrete duty.

5. WHAT THE RECORD SAYS IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, GIVEN ITS FULL WEIGHT. Utah "is an open carry state" and a campus is not a gun-free zone (Bagley, day1.txt 02:46:25) [T1]. The venue was outdoors and open — "This was an open venue. This was outside" (Long) [T2]. Bagley "did not see" anyone armed other than law enforcement (02:46:35), and a member of the private team was posted on the Hall of Flags roof beside him and was armed (02:46:55–02:47:07) [T1] — i.e. at least one adjacent roof WAS occupied by security. Responsibility was split across at least three bodies operating in coordination. Bagley's "For this event, no" as to a tactical plan (04:05:26) is one officer's account of what HE received, not an agency-level fact.

NO-FAULT STATEMENT, LOAD-BEARING. Nothing here alleges fault, negligence, or complicity by any security personnel, public or private. No official has made such an allegation. A preliminary hearing tests probable cause for the charged offences; the adequacy of the security arrangement is an element of none of them, so nothing may be inferred from what that record does or does not contain about it. Expressions of grief by officials — including UVU's chief saying hours after the murder that "you try to get your bases covered and unfortunately today we didn't" — are recorded as grief and are NOT treated as admissions of a security failure.

PRIVACY. No member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named or made identifiable, and none may be. Sources referring to "his lead security guy" or "one of the individuals that was on top of the Hall of Flags" are carried in role-only form. Named here are public officials and counsel acting in public roles (Mason, Bohls, Gray, Long, Kellner; counsel Nestor and Grunander; Judge Graf) and a journalist asking a question on the record (Matthews) — a distinct category, named because their conduct in a public capacity is the legitimate subject.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS: an FBI statement on its own pre-event role (would firm or break §1); testimony or a filing on whether the Losee roof camera was under live observation on 09-10 (would close §3); any named official identifying a fifth entity with an event-security role, or testimony closing Bagley's "I don't know" (would settle §4).

RESIDUAL SCOPE: I re-verified the 09-11 conference in full, the 09-10 and 09-16 conferences on the security/roof vocabulary, and the Bagley cross and Goforth passages in day1/day2. I did not re-verify CR-E04, CR-E07, the 2026-08-11 defence briefing, or the State's grave-risk formulation in CR-E08 beyond its elevated-vantage line.

reasons:
The finding is a compound of three clauses. Two survive direct reading; the third — the exclusionary one that does the file-governing work — is flatly false against two banked Tier 1 State sources.

WHAT SURVIVES, VERIFIED BY READING THE FACE.
(1) Both quoted passages are verbatim-accurate. Information lines 136-139: "Mr. Kirk's team members were very close to him on his right and left, as well as some behind his canopy and others at various close locations near him. The large crowd surrounded Mr. Kirk on three sides. Temporary metal fencing separated attendees from Mr. Kirk by only a matter of feet." Lines 144-146: "The bullet's trajectory passed closely to several other individuals beside Mr. Kirk, including the questioner who was standing directly in front of Mr. Kirk." Confirmed word for word.
(2) The null is REAL and STRONGER than claimed. I re-ran it with a wider capable battery via artifact_search.find(), which tests BOTH U+FFFE readings (join and hyphen), and I checked both. Zero hits in BOTH documents for: securit, secur, guard, bodyguard, body.?guard, protect, personnel, staff, escort, agent, entourage, handler. Positive controls in the SAME run on the SAME two files: canopy (Information 2 real occurrences, affidavit 3), team (Information 1), detail (affidavit 1, "detailed in this statement"), great risk (Information 2), grave risk (affidavit 1). The patterns are demonstrably capable of matching person-category nouns in these files — "team", "canopy" and "individuals" all fire — so the absence of the security family is a measured null, not a reach failure. Completeness verified independently: the Information .txt carries page markers 1 through 10 and 10 formfeeds (all ten pages present); the affidavit carries "Page 1 of 3" and 3 formfeeds. The null therefore covers the entire face of each document, not a truncated extraction.
(3) The State's 2026-07-28 preliminary-hearing brief is genuinely not banked. I tested this with stronger patterns than the finding used — /prelim\w*\s+hearing\s+(brief|memo)/, /bind\s?over|bound\s?over/, /state.{0,3}s\s+(memorandum|brief)/ — across all 63 top-level .txt artifacts under both readings. The only preliminary-hearing brief in the corpus is the defence's, in two extractions of the same document. No amended charging document exists either: the xchange docket shows a single "Filed: INFORMATION" entry (09-16-2025) and no amended Information through 2026-03-15.
(4) The defence brief's four "securit" uses are exactly as described, verbatim, and the ALT-EXTRACTION duplicate carries the identical four.

WHAT REFUTES IT. The clause "'security personnel' enters the State's case only through the defence's paraphrase of a brief this library does not hold" fails on two independent banked sources, both authored or spoken by the State:

(a) T1, day1.txt lines 8874-8889 — THE PROSECUTOR'S OWN WORDS ON DIRECT. Deputy Utah County Attorney Ryan McBride (named on the Information's own signature block, line 5 — a public official acting in a public role, nameable) asks the State's lead case agent: "If you know, what happened to Mr. Kirk immediately after he was shot?" The witness answers: "My recollection is that Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid…" McBride then uses the word HIMSELF in the next question: "Okay. Before you go any further, that Mr. Kirk being picked up by his own security, is that portrayed in the video in Exhibit 9?" This is the State's case-in-chief. Per the standing hazard I did NOT rely on the Rev labels: I inferred from CONTENT. The examiner asks open, non-leading questions, lays foundation for and publishes the State's OWN Exhibit 9, and says "Before you go any further" — the proponent controlling his own witness. That is direct examination by the party offering the evidence. (Contrast the same file's Bagley passage at lines 4884-4938, where the known label corruption puts defence attorney "Richard Novak" on the witness's answers and the examiner is Ms. Nestor — docketed as KATHRYN NESTER — conducting CROSS. That security material IS defence-elicited; the finding is right about that passage and wrong to generalise from it.)

(b) T1, a STATE FILING. The 2026-02-02 sworn proffer, docket 368, signed "/s/ Ryan McBride, Deputy Utah County Attorney", paragraph 6: "Members of Charlie Kirk's security team have reported threats, doxing…". A document the State wrote, filed and signed in this case, held in this library, using the exact phrase "Charlie Kirk's security team."

So the word does not enter "only" through the defence. It enters through a State filing and through the prosecutor's own mouth on direct. A file relying on the finding as written would state something the record contradicts, which is why this is a refutation rather than an overstatement — "only" is exclusionary and load-bearing.

WHAT IS SALVAGEABLE AND WHY IT STILL MATTERS. The narrower true claim is about the PROXIMITY THEORY, not about the word in the State's case generally. Neither State usage connects security personnel to grave risk: Hull's and McBride's usage is about post-shooting extraction and transport to Timpanogos, and the proffer's usage is about witness safety and doxing. So the State has never, in anything this library holds, placed "security personnel" in the bullet's path — which preserves the finding's practical guard against citing the Information for that proposition.

- "Pleaded" is loose. The proximity narrative is not charging language. Count 1 pleads only "knowingly created a great risk of death to another individual other than Charlie Kirk and the defendant" and names no category of person at all. The proximity passage sits in the PROBABLE CAUSE STATEMENT, which the document's own face attributes to "Brian Davis of the Utah State Bureau of Investigations… submitted the following evidence in support of the filing of this Information" — incorporated into the State's filing and authorized by the Utah County Attorney, but an affiant's narrative, not the pleaded aggravator.

No individual member of Mr. Kirk's private security team is named anywhere in this analysis, and none is named in the transcripts I read; I refer to them by role only.
